tools.usage: aminx is a lightweight, pure JAX and Equinox re-implementation of ProteinMPNN and LigandMPNN designed for high-throughput protein sequence design and differentiable pipeline integration. aminx supports GPU/TPU JIT compilation, vectorized multi-chain batches, and automatic differentiation for end-to-end gradient-based sequence optimization.
tools.strengths: Extremely clean, modern codebase that plugs directly into modern JAX-based deep learning workflows and Colab environments.
tools.weaknesses: Requires a working JAX installation with CUDA support for optimal hardware acceleration.

tools.name: MULTICOM_ligand
tools.usage: MULTICOM_ligand is a comprehensive ensembling pipeline developed by Jianlin Cheng's laboratory for CASP16 protein-ligand structural modeling and binding affinity estimation. The pipeline integrates state-of-the-art all-atom co-folding models, deep geometric scoring functions, and consensus clustering to achieve competitive accuracy on blind targets.
tools.strengths: Rigorously benchmarked in the CASP16 community experiment with top-tier performance on novel ligand-protein complexes.
tools.weaknesses: Computational resource requirements are high due to running multiple multi-engine inference pipelines.

tools.name: BindCraft-Maturation
tools.usage: BindCraft-Maturation is an automated computational pipeline extending BindCraft with PPIFlow-inspired iterative sequence maturation and interface optimization. By iteratively perturbing interface rotamers, refining backbone contacts with AlphaFold-Multimer, and optimizing residue frequencies, it evolves de novo binders into nanomolar-affinity candidates.
tools.strengths: Transforms moderate-affinity de novo scaffolds into highly optimized, wet-lab-ready binding candidates.
tools.weaknesses: Increases per-target compute time compared to standard single-pass BindCraft generation.

tools.name: ieo-Alphafold-v2
tools.usage: ieo-Alphafold-v2 is an industrial-grade Nextflow workflow developed by the European Institute of Oncology (IEO) Bioinformatics Unit to execute AlphaFold 2 and AlphaFold-Multimer across HPC clusters and cloud infrastructures. It features automated MSA sharding, SLURM batch orchestration, and automated output quality filtering.
tools.strengths: Robust, production-ready reproducibility for institutional HPC clusters and massive proteome screening initiatives.
tools.weaknesses: Configured primarily for POSIX/SLURM HPC architectures; requires Singularity or Apptainer container engines.

tools.name: AlphafoldWrapper
tools.usage: AlphafoldWrapper by Pawel Dabrowski-Tumanski provides a standardized Python framework to automate batch job creation, parameter management, and post-processing for AlphaFold modeling. It parses raw pLDDT, PAE matrices, and multi-chain alignments into structured pandas dataframes and publication-ready plots.
tools.strengths: Significantly lowers the scripting overhead required to process and compare large sets of AlphaFold predictions.
tools.weaknesses: Serves as an orchestration and extraction wrapper; does not alter AlphaFold's underlying neural network weights.

tools.name: optersoft/bio/vina
tools.usage: optersoft/bio/vina provides a streamlined Python interface for running molecular docking calculations with AutoDock Vina against receptor structures (including AlphaFold models). It generates binding poses, calculates binding affinities, and automatically exports interactive 3D visualizations using Mol* and NGL Viewer.
tools.strengths: Zero-friction setup for researchers needing immediate visual and numerical inspection of protein-ligand complexes.
tools.weaknesses: Relies on AutoDock Vina empirical scoring; does not incorporate deep learning-based all-atom co-folding.

tools.name: optersoft/bio/gnina
tools.usage: optersoft/bio/gnina is a production pipeline and Python interface for running molecular docking with Gnina, utilizing 3D convolutional neural networks (CNNs) for scoring and re-ranking binding poses. It evaluates ligand poses docked into predicted AlphaFold receptor binding pockets with deep learning affinity estimates.
tools.strengths: Outperforms classical empirical scoring functions in identifying native-like poses in predicted receptor binding sites.
tools.weaknesses: Requires CUDA-compatible GPU acceleration for high-throughput screening of massive compound libraries.

tools.name: ESMC-6B-sae
tools.usage: ESMC-6B-sae by the Chan Zuckerberg Biohub is a trained Sparse Autoencoder (SAE) applied to Layer 60 of the 6-billion parameter Evolutionary Scale Model (ESMC-6B). Featuring a codebook size of 16,384 and top-k sparsity (k=64), it decomposes polysemantic protein language embeddings into discrete, human-interpretable biophysical concepts.
tools.strengths: Unlocks true mechanistic interpretability for the largest open-source protein foundation models.
tools.weaknesses: Interpreting individual codebook latents still requires domain expertise and downstream validation.

tools.name: AntibodyDesignBFN
tools.usage: AntibodyDesignBFN developed by the Yue Hu Laboratory is a generative model using Bayesian Flow Networks (BFNs) for targeted antibody CDR design. By formulating sequence and 3D structure generation as continuous Bayesian updates over discrete token distributions, AntibodyDesignBFN achieves high CDR-H3 diversity and antigen complementarity.
tools.strengths: Produces native-like, stable CDR loop conformations with high predicted epitope binding affinity.
tools.weaknesses: Focused primarily on CDR loops; framework regions must be provided or scaffolded separately.

tools.name: ligandmpnn-noise020
tools.usage: ligandmpnn-noise020 provides official pretrained model weights for LigandMPNN trained with 0.20 Å Gaussian coordinate noise added to backbone atoms. This calibrated noise level enhances the model's robustness against minor structural inaccuracies in computationally predicted receptor backbones (such as AlphaFold or RFdiffusion models).
tools.strengths: Significantly increases experimental success rates when designing sequences on predicted or diffused backbones.
tools.weaknesses: Slightly less restrictive on side-chain steric clashes compared to the 0.05 Å noise checkpoint when applied to ultra-high-resolution structures.

tools.name: Human-Protein-Language-Model
tools.usage: Human-Protein-Language-Model-0.5 is a BERT-style transformer language model trained exclusively on the curated human proteome and its isoform variations. By capturing human-specific evolutionary patterns, codon usage contexts, and tissue-expression co-variations, it provides superior sensitivity for pathogenic missense mutation classification.
tools.strengths: Outperforms generic universal protein language models on human-specific disease phenotype benchmarks.
tools.weaknesses: Not designed for cross-species evolutionary analyses or bacterial enzyme engineering.

tools.name: ESMCrystal
tools.usage: ESMCrystal is a specialized deep neural network built on top of Evolutionary Scale Modeling representations to predict protein crystallization propensity from primary sequence. It aids structural genomics consortia and experimental crystallographers in prioritizing construct boundaries and solubilizing mutations that facilitate crystal growth.
tools.strengths: Extremely fast zero-shot inference that accelerates construct design for X-ray crystallography.
tools.weaknesses: Does not predict specific crystallization buffer conditions or precipitants.

tools.name: protein-folding-ai
tools.usage: protein-folding-ai is an open HuggingFace Space developed by Ayman Dakir providing instant, serverless protein structure prediction and 3D coordinate exploration. Powered by single-sequence ESMFold inference, it renders interactive 3D cartoons colored by pLDDT confidence with instant PDB downloads.
tools.strengths: Ideal educational and rapid-prototyping tool for immediate structural validation of engineered sequences.
tools.weaknesses: Limited to single chains under 400 amino acids due to HuggingFace Space GPU memory quotas.

tools.name: OpenGerminal
tools.usage: OpenGerminal presents an open-source, community-accessible implementation of the Germinal antibody design pipeline. Simulating in silico somatic hypermutation and affinity selection inside germinal centers, OpenGerminal enables automated de novo antibody generation and affinity maturation against challenging therapeutic targets.
tools.strengths: Democratizes state-of-the-art computational antibody engineering previously confined to proprietary corporate platforms.
tools.weaknesses: Requires substantial GPU cluster resources to run large-scale evolutionary simulations across hundreds of lineages.

tools.name: PathFold
tools.usage: PathFold introduces a deep generative paradigm that predicts the entire temporal folding pathway—from unfolded polypeptide random coils through molten globule intermediates to the native tertiary structure—directly from primary amino acid sequence without molecular dynamics simulations.
tools.strengths: Bridges the long-standing gap between static structural prediction (AlphaFold) and dynamic physical folding mechanisms.
tools.weaknesses: Validation on large multi-domain proteins is currently constrained by sparse experimental time-resolved folding data.

tools.name: AlphaFold-Multimer Reveals Diverse Cyclin-CDK Substrate Docking Interactions
tools.usage: This study deploys AlphaFold-Multimer systematically across hundreds of cell-cycle regulatory complexes to uncover non-canonical cyclin-CDK substrate docking motifs. The work demonstrates how structural co-prediction uncovers previously invisible short linear motifs (SLiMs) mediating substrate recruitment and cell-cycle checkpoint fidelity.
tools.strengths: Demonstrates the power of AlphaFold-Multimer to map transient regulatory kinase-substrate interactomes at atomistic detail.
tools.weaknesses: Phosphorylation-dependent binding events require manual phosphomimetic substitutions due to standard AF lack of post-translational modifications.

tools.name: PINPOINT
tools.usage: PINPOINT leverages pretrained protein language models and structural co-prediction to discover novel protease inhibitors operating at the plant-pathogen molecular interface. It identifies defensive plant peptides that neutralize fungal and oomycete virulence proteases with high specificity.
tools.strengths: Unlocks valuable biocontrol agents and agricultural crop protection scaffolds against destructive pathogens.
tools.weaknesses: Tailored specifically for protease-inhibitor pairs; general enzyme-substrate prediction requires separate fine-tuning.

tools.name: Adapting Co-Folding Models for Structure-Based Protein-Protein Docking Through Flow Matching
tools.usage: This manuscript introduces an approach for adapting all-atom co-folding foundation models into dedicated structure-based protein-protein docking engines using Riemannian flow matching. By conditioning on predetermined monomeric structures, it eliminates MSA search times while accurately predicting rigid and flexible binding poses.
tools.strengths: Combines the accuracy of AlphaFold 3-scale co-folding with the speed required for large-scale interactome screening.
tools.weaknesses: Requires pre-existing or predicted 3D structures for both binding partners.

tools.name: MViewEMA
tools.usage: MViewEMA presents a multi-view deep graph attention network for estimating the global and interface quality of multimeric protein complexes. By synthesizing geometric graphs from multiple spatial perspectives, MViewEMA provides calibrated confidence scores that detect misdocked subunits in AlphaFold-Multimer predictions.
tools.strengths: Identifies subtle interface mispackings and false-positive multimer predictions that evade standard AlphaFold confidence metrics.
tools.weaknesses: Computational evaluation time scales with the number of pairwise subunit interfaces in high-order oligomers.

tools.name: PLI-Parallax
tools.usage: PLI-Parallax is an expansive, standardized open benchmark dataset cataloging experimental and multi-predictor protein-ligand structural coordinates. Designed to benchmark AlphaFold 3, Boltz-1, Chai-1, and classical docking engines, it includes standardized atom-level contact labels, distance matrices, and binding pose fidelity metrics.
tools.strengths: Provides an authoritative, unbiased benchmark resource resolving inconsistencies across individual method self-assessments.
tools.weaknesses: Focuses predominantly on drug-like small molecules; macrocycles and covalent ligands have lower representation.

tools.name: Slice’N’Dice and ABCFold
tools.usage: This published research from the University of Liverpool details Slice’N’Dice and ABCFold, an automated computational pipeline for decomposing AlphaFold models into rigid domain units and docking them into medium-to-low resolution cryo-EM density maps with high geometric fidelity.
tools.strengths: Dramatically reduces the manual effort required to interpret large multi-protein machinery in challenging cryo-EM densities.
tools.weaknesses: Requires user verification when maps exhibit significant continuous conformational heterogeneity.

tools.name: Benchmarking Protein-Ligand Co-Folding Across Voltage-Gated Ion Channels
tools.usage: Published in Frontiers in Biophysics, this study performs an evaluation of state-of-the-art all-atom co-folding models on voltage-gated sodium (Nav), calcium (Cav), and potassium (Kv) channels bound to diverse pore blockers, toxins, and gating modifiers in lipid environments.
tools.strengths: Provides critical guidelines for applying AI co-folding to one of the most therapeutically vital yet challenging drug target classes.
tools.weaknesses: Absence of explicit lipid bilayer simulations in co-folding models can impact boundary pose predictions.

tools.name: Evolutionary Conditional Diffusion Ensembles
tools.usage: Published in the Journal of Chemical Information and Modeling (JCIM), this study introduces evolutionary conditional diffusion to sample functionally diverse conformational ensembles of dynamic proteins, capturing functional substates invisible to static AlphaFold predictions.
tools.strengths: Surpasses standard MSA sub-sampling in generating biophysically continuous conformational transitions.
tools.weaknesses: Computational sampling cost increases when exploring deep, high-barrier allosteric transitions.

tools.name: MG-PDB & MGBench
tools.usage: MG-PDB & MGBench establish the first standardized structural database and evaluation benchmark specifically tailored for molecular glue-induced ternary complexes (E3 ligase - small molecule glue - target neosubstrate). The study systematically benchmarks leading co-folding models on ternary pose recovery.
tools.strengths: Essential benchmark for targeted protein degradation (TPD) and proximity-inducing drug development.
tools.weaknesses: Ternary complexes with flexible, unstructured degron loops remain challenging across all evaluated models.

tools.name: A De Novo CO2 Reductase Featuring a Cysteine-Ligated Cobalt Porphyrin Cofactor
tools.usage: Published in JACS, this landmark study details the de novo computational design of an artificial metallo-enzyme that catalyzes the electrocatalytic reduction of CO2. Featuring a customized cysteine-ligated cobalt porphyrin active site, the de novo catalyst achieves remarkable turnover numbers and selectivity.
tools.strengths: Demonstrates the power of generative protein design to create non-natural catalytic machinery for clean energy and carbon capture.
tools.weaknesses: Synthesis and in vitro reconstitution of non-biological metal cofactors requires specialized experimental protocols.

tools.name: Affinity Fine-Tuning of Boltz-2
tools.usage: This paper presents an open framework for fine-tuning Boltz-2 on experimental binding affinity datasets (ChEMBL, BindingDB). By updating the all-atom pair representations with continuous thermodynamic affinity heads, the authors improve IC50 and Ki ranking across pharmaceutical lead series.
tools.strengths: Transforms all-atom structural co-folding from pose prediction into a quantitative virtual screening engine.
tools.weaknesses: Sensitive to experimental affinity assay discrepancies (e.g. IC50 variations across different protocol conditions).

tools.name: Benchmarking TCR-pMHC Structure Prediction
tools.usage: Published in Briefings in Bioinformatics, this article presents a unified evaluation benchmark for TCR-pMHC complex structure prediction across AlphaFold 3, AlphaFold-Multimer, and specialized immune architectures, examining CDR3 loop orientation fidelity and epitope specificity.
tools.strengths: Provides definitive guidance on the limits and capabilities of deep learning models in TCR therapeutic engineering.
tools.weaknesses: Accurately predicting non-canonical TCR docking angles across diverse HLA class II alleles remains challenging.

tools.name: SNAC-DB
tools.usage: Published in Protein Science, SNAC-DB is an open, machine-learning-ready database cataloging antibody and camelid Nanobody (VHH)-antigen complexes. With structural quality curation, CDR annotations, and standardized benchmarks, SNAC-DB accelerates the development of generative models for single-domain therapeutics.
tools.strengths: Addresses the severe shortage of dedicated, high-quality benchmark datasets for Nanobody engineering.
tools.weaknesses: Limited by the total number of publicly available experimental VHH-antigen co-crystal structures.

tools.name: Benchmarking Docking Protocols for GPCR Allosteric Modulators
tools.usage: This study benchmarks molecular docking protocols and all-atom co-folding architectures against GPCR allosteric binding sites (extrahelical, intracellular, and lipid-interface pockets). It highlights the challenges of modeling subtle induced-fit rearrangements in multi-pass transmembrane receptors.
tools.strengths: Delivers crucial methodological recommendations for the discovery of subtype-selective allosteric GPCR therapeutics.
tools.weaknesses: Extrahelical lipid-facing pockets exhibit higher pose uncertainty due to the absence of explicit membrane bilayers.

tools.name: Atlas of Predicted Protein Complex Structures Across Kingdoms
tools.usage: Published in Nature Communications, this comprehensive study presents a cross-kingdom atlas of predicted protein-protein complexes spanning bacteria, archaea, plants, and animals. Using AlphaFold-Multimer, the authors uncover conserved ancient core complexes and evolutionary divergence in interface architectures.
tools.strengths: Provides an unprecedented global perspective on the structural evolution of cellular machinery.
tools.weaknesses: Accuracy varies across divergent kingdoms with shallow sequence alignments.

tools.name: Unlocking the Application Potential of AlphaFold3-Like Approaches in Virtual Screening
tools.usage: Published in Chemical Science, this article critically assesses the capabilities and caveats of using AlphaFold 3-like all-atom co-folding models in real-world virtual screening. The authors analyze binding pose fidelity, stereochemical plausibility, and enrichment factors against established drug targets.
tools.strengths: Provides practical, reality-tested workflows for integrating deep co-folding into industrial drug discovery pipelines.
tools.weaknesses: Direct generative co-folding remains too compute-intensive for billion-molecule library screening without hierarchical pre-filters.

tools.name: AF_pyDock
tools.usage: AF_pyDock is the companion software and protocol implementation (Methods in Molecular Biology) that synergistically couples AlphaFold-Multimer confidence metrics (pLDDT, PAE, ipTM) with physics-based electrostatic and desolvation energy scoring from pyDock. This hybrid scoring pipeline effectively distinguishes genuine native-like multimeric complexes from false-positive AI predictions.
tools.strengths: Overcomes AlphaFold over-confidence by enforcing strict physical electrostatics and desolvation complementarity.
tools.weaknesses: Requires localized Amber/CHARMM parameter assignment and atomic coordinate preparation.

tools.name: foldrunner
tools.usage: foldrunner is a comprehensive, automated execution and benchmarking pipeline designed for all-vs-all protein structure prediction across leading foundation models. foldrunner uses a single canonical sequence alignment per query and orchestrates parallel prediction across AlphaFold 3, Boltz-2, Protenix, Chai-1, ColabFold, and AlphaFold-Multimer.
tools.strengths: Provides an unbiased, plug-and-play platform for side-by-side comparison of next-generation co-folding architectures.
tools.weaknesses: High computational demands requiring multi-GPU infrastructure to evaluate large multi-chain panels.

tools.name: AF_ClaSeq_Benchmark
tools.usage: AF_ClaSeq_Benchmark is a specialized structural dynamics benchmarking framework evaluating AF-ClaSeq against 6 state-of-the-art conformational ensemble prediction approaches (BioEmu, AlphaFlow, Cfold, SPEACH_AF, AlphaFold3, and AF_Cluster) across 14 experimentally verified two-state switching protein systems.
tools.strengths: Establishes transparent, objective criteria for assessing how generative AI captures functional protein conformational states.
tools.weaknesses: Focuses primarily on two-state equilibrium transitions; continuous intrinsically disordered ensembles require additional metrics.

tools.name: speedyfold
tools.usage: speedyfold is an optimized modification of AlphaFold 3 engineered for high-throughput in silico screening of large antibody and nanobody binder libraries. By calculating the target antigen MSA once and rapidly realigning it to related CDR candidate variants, speedyfold bypasses the dominant sequence homology search bottleneck.
tools.strengths: Reduces total computation time by over 80% when evaluating large candidate libraries against a shared target.
tools.weaknesses: Optimized specifically for fixed-target multi-binder screening; does not accelerate unique all-vs-all pairs.

tools.name: fold2go
tools.usage: fold2go is a production Nextflow workflow developed by the Institute of Molecular Biology (IMB) for high-performance in silico prediction of protein structures and multimeric interactions. fold2go orchestrates AlphaFold 2, AlphaFold-Multimer, AlphaFold 3, and Boltz across SLURM and cloud HPC environments with full Singularity containerization.
tools.strengths: Production-ready, highly robust pipeline that scales effortlessly from single proteins to whole proteomes.
tools.weaknesses: Requires an existing HPC environment with SLURM or cloud runners and container runtime support.

tools.name: pdmodels
tools.usage: pdmodels is an open-source Python library and command-line interface that unifies contemporary protein structure prediction and inverse folding architectures under a clean, consistent API. pdmodels wraps AlphaFold 2/Multimer, ESMFold, ESM-IF1, ProteinMPNN, and LigandMPNN into standardized Python classes and CLI utilities.
tools.strengths: Drastically reduces boilerplate code needed to build multi-stage generative protein design loops.
tools.weaknesses: Relies on local weights and conda/pip environments for multiple underlying packages.

tools.name: pairs
tools.usage: pairs, developed by the Benoit Coulombe Laboratory, is an automated analysis and scoring engine designed to assess protein-protein interactions directly from raw AlphaFold-Multimer output files. pairs extracts inter-chain contact boundaries, parses Predicted Aligned Error (PAE) matrices, and computes composite interaction scores to reliably classify true biological complexes.
tools.strengths: Fast, dependency-light extraction of high-confidence protein interfaces from raw model directories.
tools.weaknesses: Calibrated primarily on binary hetero- and homo-dimers; high-order oligomers require pairwise breakdown.

tools.name: Proteus
tools.usage: Proteus is an open-source agent skill and headless automation library on GitLab designed to equip autonomous AI agents and coding assistants with programmatic structural biology capabilities. By encapsulating PyMOL, UCSF ChimeraX, AlphaFold DB REST APIs, and Rosetta energy functions into standardized agent-callable tools, Proteus allows researchers and language models to inspect coordinates, measure interface metrics, generate publication-grade renders, and validate structural models via natural language commands.
tools.strengths: Bridges generative AI reasoning and rigorous structural biology software, enabling autonomous workflows for structural validation and figure generation. Lightweight, well-documented Python interface with minimal external system dependencies.
tools.weaknesses: Full functionality requires local installations of PyMOL, ChimeraX, and/or Rosetta executables. Complex custom rendering styles and artistic scenes require user-defined preset templates.

tools.name: SEED
tools.usage: SEED (Solvation Energy for Exhaustive Docking), developed by the Amedeo Caflisch Laboratory at the University of Zurich, is an open-source high-throughput docking suite tailored for fragment-based drug discovery. SEED performs exhaustive pose generation and evaluates protein-ligand binding free energies by computing rigorous electrostatic solvation and desolvation penalties via continuum dielectric models.
tools.strengths: State-of-the-art accuracy for fragment-based virtual screening by capturing critical water-displacement thermodynamics.
tools.weaknesses: Assumes a rigid receptor backbone; works best when combined with AlphaFold-generated conformational ensembles.

tools.name: pyproga
tools.usage: pyproga (Python Protein Graph Analyser) is an open-source structural bioinformatics package that transforms 3D macromolecular structures (from PDB or AlphaFold) into rich residue interaction networks (RINs). pyproga analyzes topological network centrality, inter-residue contact graphs, and shortest-path communication corridors to decipher allosteric communication channels.
tools.strengths: Fast, versatile graph-theoretical framework for revealing hidden structural communication pathways in complex proteins.
tools.weaknesses: Graph representations abstract away continuous geometric steric coordinates in favor of topological contact connectivity.

tools.name: MADE
tools.usage: MADE (Macromolecular Maribor Density and Structure Analysis Software) is an open-source structural biology toolkit developed by Marko Jukić for advanced macromolecular structure analysis, pocket volume characterization, and cryo-EM / crystallographic electron density evaluation. MADE directly integrates with AlphaFold 3D coordinates.
tools.strengths: Robust, high-precision geometric analysis of macromolecular binding cavities and experimental density agreement.
tools.weaknesses: Requires C++ build toolchains and BLAS/LAPACK libraries for maximum computational throughput.

tools.name: esm2_rna_binding_site_predictor
tools.usage: esm2_rna_binding_site_predictor (by Amelie Schreiber) is a specialized Transformer model fine-tuned on top of Meta's ESM-2 architecture to predict RNA-binding residues and interface patches directly from primary protein sequence. The model enables rapid scanning of proteomes to identify putative ribonucleoprotein (RNP) complexes.
tools.strengths: Bypasses the computational cost of structural co-folding for rapid initial prioritization of RNA-binding domains.
tools.weaknesses: Predicts binding propensity per residue; does not output 3D atomic coordinates of the bound RNA oligonucleotide.

tools.name: SaProt_650M_PDB
tools.usage: SaProt_650M_PDB, developed by the Westlake University team, is a breakthrough structure-aware protein language model. SaProt is pre-trained on millions of structures from the PDB and AlphaFold Database using a combined alphabet of amino acid sequence tokens and Foldseek 3D structural tokens, unifying sequence evolution with spatial geometry.
tools.strengths: Bridges the gap between 1D language models and 3D geometric networks with exceptional parameter and compute efficiency.
tools.weaknesses: Requires structural 3Di tokens as input for optimal performance (can be generated via Foldseek from PDB/AlphaFold models).

tools.name: ProteinGPT-Llama3
tools.usage: ProteinGPT-Llama3 is an interactive HuggingFace Space hosting a multimodal conversational agent for structural biology. Built on Llama-3 and aligned with protein embeddings, AlphaFold structural metadata, and UniProt functional annotations, ProteinGPT answers complex questions regarding catalytic mechanisms, active site geometry, and evolutionary mutations.
tools.strengths: Enables intuitive, natural-language synthesis of structural, functional, and evolutionary knowledge for target discovery.
tools.weaknesses: Qualitative reasoning engine; quantitative coordinate manipulation requires downstream molecular modeling tools.

tools.name: Antibody-Structure-Prediction-W-IgFold
tools.usage: Antibody-Structure-Prediction-W-IgFold is an interactive HuggingFace application delivering instant 3D structural modeling of paired antibody heavy and light chain variable domains (Fv). Utilizing the pre-trained IgFold neural network, the app outputs all-atom coordinates and per-residue error estimates within seconds.
tools.strengths: Extreme inference speed makes it ideal for real-time web exploration and rapid prototyping of antibody variants.
tools.weaknesses: Dedicated exclusively to antibody Fv domains; does not model non-immunoglobulin scaffolds or antigen complexes.

tools.name: nanobodybert
tools.usage: nanobodybert is a specialized bidirectional Transformer protein language model pre-trained exclusively on extensive repositories of camelid single-domain antibody (VHH / nanobody) sequences. nanobodybert captures nanobody-specific framework conservation, hallmark hydrophobic-to-hydrophilic substitutions, and CDR3 hypervariability.
tools.strengths: Outperforms general-purpose protein language models on nanobody-specific affinity maturation and humanization tasks.
tools.weaknesses: Sequence-only representation; optimal affinity optimization benefits from integration with 3D structural co-folding.

tools.name: protein_binding_search
tools.usage: protein_binding_search (by Roni Gordon) is an interactive HuggingFace Space providing rapid geometric and electrostatic surface matching for protein-protein interface search. Given a target surface patch or binding site, the application scans macromolecular structural databases to identify proteins with complementary binding motifs.
tools.strengths: Enables instantaneous hypothesis generation for discovering novel protein binding partners and interface mimetics.
tools.weaknesses: Evaluates pre-formed rigid surface patches; flexible induced-fit adaptations require subsequent MD refinement.

tools.name: Atlantis
tools.usage: Atlantis is an integrative database and web portal mapping known and predicted functional sites, catalytic residues, post-translational modifications (PTMs), and pathogenic missense variants across the entire AlphaFold-modeled human proteome. Atlantis bridges 3D structural models with cellular functional annotations.
tools.strengths: Consolidates fragmented biomedical annotations into a unified, high-confidence 3D structural resource.
tools.weaknesses: Accuracy of spatial functional clustering depends on the local pLDDT confidence of AlphaFold predictions.

tools.name: Dissecting the Black Box of AlphaFold in Protein–Protein Complex Assembly
tools.usage: This study conducts a rigorous mechanistic dissection of how AlphaFold-Multimer navigates multi-chain complex assembly. By probing internal layer-by-layer attention patterns, evolutionary co-variation signals, and intermediate recycling coordinates, the authors uncover the progressive geometric rules governing subunit docking.
tools.strengths: Provides rare, mechanistic insight into the neural decision-making process underlying AI-driven protein docking.
tools.weaknesses: Investigates AlphaFold 2/Multimer attention mechanics; all-atom diffusion architectures (AF3) operate under different denoising dynamics.

tools.name: Benchmarking MSA Pairing for Complex Structure Prediction Reveals a Depth-Over-Pairing Principle
tools.usage: A comprehensive benchmarking study from Jianyi Yang's laboratory evaluating multiple sequence alignment (MSA) pairing strategies for protein-protein complex structure prediction. The authors systematically demonstrate that total MSA depth and diversity outweigh strict species/taxonomic matching (the 'depth-over-pairing principle').
tools.strengths: Provides critical, actionable guidelines that directly boost multimer prediction success rates for difficult interactome targets.
tools.weaknesses: In paralog-rich eukaryotic families, cross-talk between multiple paralogs still requires careful taxonomic curation.

tools.name: Ion Mobility Mass Spectrometry Guided Modeling with AlphaFold and Rosetta Improves Complex Prediction
tools.usage: A hybrid structural biology investigation by the Lindert and Wysocki laboratories integrating experimental native ion mobility mass spectrometry (IM-MS) collision cross sections (CCS) with AlphaFold-Multimer and Rosetta modeling. Experimental CCS restraints guide ensemble filtering to resolve ambiguous multimeric stoichiometries.
tools.strengths: Bridges low-sample experimental mass spectrometry with deep learning to solve otherwise intractable macromolecular assemblies.
tools.weaknesses: Requires experimental native IM-MS facilities to acquire empirical collision cross section values.

tools.name: Proteome-Wide in Silico Screening for Human Protein-Protein Interactions
tools.usage: A landmark study from Harvard Medical School (Johannes Walter and Alan Brown labs) performing an exhaustive proteome-wide in silico binary interaction screen with AlphaFold-Multimer across uncharacterized human proteins. The screen uncovers previously unknown complexes involved in DNA repair, genome stability, and ribosome biogenesis.
tools.strengths: Demonstrates the real-world discovery power of proteome-scale structural AI to uncover vital, unannotated biological machinery.
tools.weaknesses: Massive computational screening requires institutional supercomputing clusters.

tools.name: A Drug–Target Specificity Foundation Model for Off-Target Prediction and Generative Design
tools.usage: A pharmacogenomic foundation model developed by Sai Reddy's group at ETH Zurich coupling 3D co-folding representations with large-scale binding affinity profiling. The model simultaneously predicts target engagement, flags dangerous off-target interactions across the human proteome, and guides generative de novo binder design.
tools.strengths: Unifies forward target prediction and inverse generative chemistry within a single structural foundation architecture.
tools.weaknesses: Proteome-wide off-target profiling is computationally demanding for large combinatorial chemical libraries.

tools.name: SE(3)-Equivariant Ternary Complex Prediction Towards Target Protein Degradation
tools.usage: Published in Nature Communications, this landmark paper presents an SE(3)-equivariant geometric deep learning framework specifically designed to predict the atomic coordinates of ternary complexes (E3 ligase, small-molecule degrader/molecular glue, and target protein) for targeted protein degradation (TPD).
tools.strengths: Crucial breakthrough for rational design of molecular glues and PROTACs where standard docking tools struggle with three-body thermodynamics.
tools.weaknesses: Requires predefined initial binding pocket regions on the E3 ligase and target protein.

tools.name: TriGlue
tools.usage: TriGlue is a biology-inspired generative framework that unifies structure-conditioned small-molecule generation with ternary complex assembly. By treating molecular glue binding as an induced-fit ternary co-folding process, TriGlue generates novel chemical scaffolds that stabilize neo-substrate recruitment to E3 ligases.
tools.strengths: Directly tackles the inverse design problem for molecular glues rather than relying on brute-force screening of existing compound libraries.
tools.weaknesses: Synthesized chemical suggestions require downstream medicinal chemistry retrosynthesis validation.

tools.name: TCRLens
tools.usage: Published in Bioinformatics Advances, TCRLens is a structure-aware equivariant graph neural network architecture engineered for high-accuracy prediction of T-cell receptor (TCR) binding to peptide-MHC class I (pMHC-I) complexes and immunogenic epitope discovery. TCRLens integrates 3D structural models from AlphaFold with graph attention.
tools.strengths: Significantly outperforms sequence-only TCR predictors by incorporating physical 3D contact geometry.
tools.weaknesses: Relies on high-quality 3D models of the TCR-pMHC interface, requiring AlphaFold or experimental crystal templates.

tools.name: Nativeness-Constrained Diffusion Framework for Nanobody Design
tools.usage: Published in Briefings in Bioinformatics, this paper introduces a geometric diffusion framework for nanobody engineering that incorporates evolutionary nativeness constraints. The architecture generates functional antigen-binding CDR loops while preserving rigid camelid framework scaffolds and canonical loop geometries.
tools.strengths: Ensures that de novo designed nanobodies possess high bacterial expression yields and biophysical developability.
tools.weaknesses: Focuses primarily on single-domain VHH architectures; multi-domain full antibodies require paired light-chain constraints.

tools.name: Antibody and Nanobody Design Dataset (ANDD)
tools.usage: The Antibody and Nanobody Design Dataset (ANDD) is a curated, standardized structural benchmark repository deposited on Zenodo. ANDD compiles thousands of experimentally resolved and AlphaFold-modeled antibody-antigen and nanobody-antigen complexes, pre-split by sequence clustering and epitope diversity for geometric deep learning.
tools.strengths: Fills a critical gap for standardized, reproducible evaluation of AI antibody and nanobody design algorithms.
tools.weaknesses: Regularly requires updates as new antibody-antigen crystal complexes are deposited in the PDB.

tools.name: Assessing State-Specific Accuracy of Cofolding Models for Kinases and GPCRs
tools.usage: A comprehensive structural benchmark study from Charité Universitätsmedizin Berlin evaluating state-specific accuracy across AlphaFold 3, Boltz-1, and Chai-1 on dynamic allosteric signaling proteins. The benchmark quantifies whether all-atom co-folding models accurately reproduce active, inactive, and intermediate states in kinases and GPCRs.
tools.strengths: Provides critical empirical evidence on when all-atom co-folding models succeed or fail in dynamic drug discovery contexts.
tools.weaknesses: Highlights that current co-folding foundation models often collapse toward dominant ground-state crystal conformations without specialized prompting.

tools.name: Zero-Shot Design of Drug-Binding Proteins via Neural Iterative Selection-Expansion
tools.usage: Published in Nature by Benjamin Fry, Katie Slaw, and Nicholas Polizzi, this landmark paper presents neural iterative selection-expansion for the zero-shot computational design of proteins that bind arbitrary small-molecule drugs with high nanomolar affinities without requiring high-throughput experimental screening.
tools.strengths: A watershed achievement in computational structural biology, proving that AI can design high-affinity small-molecule receptors completely zero-shot.
tools.weaknesses: Computationally intensive geometric search required for designing deeply buried, highly polar drug-binding pockets.

tools.name: Discovery of Molecular Glues by Modeling Ternary Complex Ensembles and Thermodynamic Stability
tools.usage: This study from Relay Therapeutics presents an integrated computational-experimental discovery engine for molecular glues. By modeling ternary complex conformational ensembles alongside rigorous thermodynamic binding free energies, the authors prospectively discover novel molecular glues for challenging oncogenic neo-substrates.
tools.strengths: Demonstrates successful prospective discovery of active molecular glues by marrying AI structural models with physics-based thermodynamics.
tools.weaknesses: Free-energy perturbation calculations across ternary ensembles demand substantial GPU compute clusters.

tools.name: Comparative Study of Deep Learning and Classical Modeling for Protein-Ligand Pose and Affinity
tools.usage: Published in the Journal of Chemical Information and Modeling (JCIM), this comparative investigation evaluates deep learning co-folding architectures (AlphaFold 3, NeuralPLexer, DiffDock) against established physics-based docking suites (Glide, AutoDock Vina) across hundreds of viral main protease-ligand complexes.
tools.strengths: Provides honest, highly valuable benchmarking data clarifying the complementary strengths of AI co-folding and traditional physics engines.
tools.weaknesses: Benchmarked specifically on viral cysteine proteases; metallo-enzymes and GPCRs display different pocket flexibility profiles.

tools.name: Protocol for Generating Closed-, Open-, and Inactivated-State hERG Channels Using ColabFold
tools.usage: Published in BIO-PROTOCOL by the Vladimir Yarov-Yarovoy laboratory (UC Davis), this detailed protocol establishes an empirical methodology for driving ColabFold to model specific functional states (closed, open, and inactivated) of the human hERG potassium channel using tailored structural templates and MSA subsampling.
tools.strengths: Provides an invaluable practical blueprint for researchers needing state-specific ion channel models for off-target cardiotoxicity profiling.
tools.weaknesses: Requires careful manual curation of homologous templates representing target functional conformations.

tools.name: Structural Insights into Mpox Virus G9 Protein Mutations and Subcomplex Formation via AlphaFold 3
tools.usage: Published in Molecules, this study employs AlphaFold 3 multi-chain modeling to investigate the structural impact of emerging mutations (such as M142I) in the Monkeypox virus (MPXV) G9 envelope protein. The authors elucidate how specific amino acid changes alter the assembly and interface stability of the multiprotein entry fusion complex.
tools.strengths: Illustrates the frontline utility of AlphaFold 3 for rapid structural virology assessment during infectious disease outbreaks.
tools.weaknesses: Focuses on static subcomplex interfaces; full viral membrane fusion requires cellular cryo-electron tomography context.

tools.name: Structural Bioinformatics of Four Human Aquaporins and Their Water-Soluble QTY Analogs
tools.usage: This study applies the QTY code (substituting hydrophobic leucine, isoleucine, valine, and phenylalanine with glutamine, threonine, and tyrosine) developed by Shuguang Zhang's lab at MIT to redesign four human transmembrane aquaporins into fully water-soluble variants. The structural fidelity and pore channel geometry are validated via AlphaFold.
tools.strengths: Demonstrates the power of combining systematic chemical code rules (QTY) with AlphaFold for detergent-free membrane protein engineering.
tools.weaknesses: Experimental water-permeation transport rates of QTY-designed pores require functional stopped-flow liposome assays.

tools.name: RFOptimization
tools.usage: RFOptimization (RFO) is a training-free framework for all-atom biomolecular binder optimization. It formulates binder improvement as a residue-wise mutational search problem, sampling candidate substitutions alternately based on gradient-guided sequence optimization using all-atom structure prediction models and a cycling-based sequence redesign strategy that alternates structure generation with an orthogonal predictor and MPNN-based sequence design. Final filters use orthogonal AlphaFold 3 metrics to prevent single-model overfitting.
tools.strengths: Training-free framework operating in minutes; leverages gradient-guided all-atom prediction and cycling redesign; avoids reward hacking and overfitting via orthogonal AlphaFold 3 filtering across proteins, small-molecule sensors, and cyclic peptides.
tools.weaknesses: Inference time depends on underlying all-atom structure prediction speed; requires experimental validation for de novo designs.

tools.name: dock-postprocess
tools.usage: dock-postprocess is an open-source structure-based drug design (SBDD) toolkit for standardized docking-pose ingestion, restrained OpenMM energy minimization, pose QC, protein-ligand contact profiling, and ligand strain analysis. Uniquely, it supports single receptors, multichain assemblies, and challenging ternary complexes including molecular glues and PROTACs.
tools.strengths: Fully automated pipeline bridging raw docking engine outputs (e.g. Vina, DiffDock, Boltz-1) with rigorous molecular mechanics refinement. Specialized handling of small-molecule degraders (PROTACs) and molecular glue ternary complexes often neglected by standard tools.
tools.weaknesses: Requires OpenMM and OpenFF environments which may necessitate GPU acceleration for batch minimization of massive compound libraries. Does not perform initial docking sampling itself; relies on upstream docking predictors.

tools.name: PLAID
tools.usage: PLAID is a generative foundation model developed at MIT for all-atom de novo protein generation using latent diffusion. By conditioning diffusion trajectories on compositional functional descriptions and taxonomic evolutionary lineages, PLAID generates physically realizable, multi-domain proteins tailored to specific phylogenetic and biochemical contexts.
tools.strengths: Simultaneous all-atom generation avoids two-stage backbone-then-sequence limitations. Flexible conditioning interface allowing researchers to combine taxonomic, structural, and functional constraints.
tools.weaknesses: Latent decoding requires high-fidelity autoencoder inversion which can occasionally introduce local sidechain packing artefacts. High-end GPU hardware required for rapid interactive diffusion sampling.

tools.name: MMseqs2-App
tools.usage: MMseqs2-App is a self-contained cross-platform application and server orchestrator developed by the Söding Lab for running MMseqs2 searches locally. It provides a modern GUI and Dockerized backend designed to serve high-throughput multiple sequence alignments (MSAs) and sequence database queries directly for local AlphaFold, ColabFold, and Foldseek installations without relying on public webservers.
tools.strengths: Eliminates public server rate limits and downtime for institutional AlphaFold/ColabFold pipelines. Intuitive UI combined with robust REST endpoints for seamless integration into custom bioinformatics workflows.
tools.weaknesses: Requires substantial local storage (hundreds of gigabytes to terabytes) for full uniref/environmental databases. High memory footprint during large-scale database memory mapping.

tools.name: PhysDock
tools.usage: PhysDock is an all-atom generative diffusion model for protein-ligand complex prediction that explicitly embeds physical force-field constraints and energetic priors into the reverse diffusion trajectory. By penalizing steric clashes and electrostatically unfavorable interactions during generative sampling, PhysDock achieves unprecedented chemical plausibility and top-1 RMSD accuracy.
tools.strengths: Significantly reduces severe steric clashes common in unconstrained geometric diffusion models. Superior generalization to unseen chemical scaffolds and novel protein pocket architectures.
tools.weaknesses: Physics gradient computations add moderate inference overhead compared to purely feedforward geometric predictors. Performance depends on accurate initial protonation and formal charge assignment of ligand structures.

tools.name: Promera
tools.usage: Promera is a deep learning suite for biomolecular co-folding, structural binder filtering, and de novo nanobody design developed by Bowen Jing and collaborators at MIT. It implements multi-state geometric ranking, interface quality evaluation, and automated CDR optimization to rapidly filter diffusion-generated binder libraries against target antigen epitopes.
tools.strengths: Engineered specifically for single-domain antibodies (VHH/nanobodies), addressing unique CDR3 loop conformational diversity. Seamless integration with popular generative backbones such as RFdiffusion and ProteinMPNN.
tools.weaknesses: Focused primarily on nanobody and small binder topologies; full-length IgG antibody modeling requires adapted workflows. High computational cost when screening very large combinatorial binder libraries.

tools.name: PoET-2
tools.usage: PoET-2 is a retrieval-augmented multimodal protein language model developed by OpenProtein AI. By retrieving relevant evolutionary homologs and integrating 3D structural contexts during generation, PoET-2 conditions sequence designs on natural evolutionary constraints, enabling zero-shot fitness landscape estimation and generative sequence optimization for diverse protein families.
tools.strengths: Significantly out-competes standard non-retrieval pLMs on orphan protein families and sparse sequence alignments. Open-source code and model weights enabling straightforward adaptation for directed evolution campaigns.
tools.weaknesses: Inference speed is linked to the speed of the underlying homolog retrieval search step. Requires substantial memory when querying against massive multi-billion sequence index stores.

tools.name: SPOC
tools.usage: SPOC (Scoring Predictions of Complexes) is an open-source evaluation and scoring tool developed by the Walter Lab at Harvard Medical School. Designed specifically for binary AlphaFold-Multimer predictions, SPOC computes multi-parametric interface quality metrics to accurately discriminate genuine physiological protein-protein interactions from non-specific co-folding artefacts.
tools.strengths: Substantially increases precision in proteome-wide all-vs-all interactome screens. Requires no heavy retraining; operates directly on standard AlphaFold-Multimer output files.
tools.weaknesses: Tuned specifically for binary (dimeric) complexes; higher-order oligomeric assemblies are not currently handled. Relies on the underlying quality of the AlphaFold-Multimer prediction; cannot rescue completely misfolded subunits.

tools.name: ProteinBender
tools.usage: ProteinBender is an open-source software package hosted on GitLab designed for preparing, voxelizing, and featurizing macromolecular structures for 3D convolutional and graph neural networks. It provides accelerated utilities for coordinate normalization, atomic density field generation, pocket segmentation, and geometric invariant extraction.
tools.strengths: Significantly speeds up the data preparation bottleneck for 3D structural deep learning architectures. Modular architecture allowing custom atomic radius, charge, and hybridization channel definitions.
tools.weaknesses: Grid-based representations are inherently more memory-intensive than sparse point-cloud or graph representations. Limited support for non-standard modified residues without manual chemical dictionary mappings.

tools.name: RepeatsDB3-Modules
tools.usage: RepeatsDB3-Modules is a specialized Python library developed by the REFRACT consortium for processing, analyzing, and visualizing structural repeat units from RepeatsDB. It enables programmatic mapping of genomic exon structures onto 3D tandem repeat protein geometries to investigate the evolutionary modularity and disease-associated variations in repeat proteins.
tools.strengths: Fills a major gap in the structural bioinformatics of tandem repeat proteins, which often present challenges for standard homology models. Direct integration with Ensembl and PDB APIs for automated data synchronization.
tools.weaknesses: Specialized domain tool; not intended for general non-repeat globular protein analyses. Depends on RepeatsDB structural classification schema and web service availability.

tools.name: CPSDB
tools.usage: CPSDB (Compressed Protein Structure Database) is an ultra-efficient database format and indexing toolkit designed to store, stream, and query massive structural archives such as AlphaFold DB and the PDB. By utilizing lossy/lossless quantization and geometric compression algorithms, CPSDB reduces storage footprints by up to 90% while enabling sub-millisecond random coordinate access.
tools.strengths: Reduces multi-terabyte AlphaFold DB organism proteomes into manageable disk footprints. Significantly accelerates I/O throughput during large-scale structural foundation model pre-training.
tools.weaknesses: Custom binary archive format requires specific parser libraries rather than standard mmCIF/PDB parsers. Lossy compression modes must be configured carefully for tasks requiring exact crystallographic B-factors.

tools.name: SE(3)-Transformer PyTorch
tools.usage: SE(3)-Transformer PyTorch is a clean, modular PyTorch implementation of SE(3)-equivariant self-attention networks for 3D point cloud and macromolecular learning. Created to facilitate research into equivariant geometric deep learning and structural prediction architectures, it provides building blocks for rotationally and translationally invariant biomolecular modeling.
tools.strengths: Clean, transparent implementation widely adopted as a foundational reference for custom structural AI architectures. Guarantees exact geometric invariance/equivariance without requiring extensive data augmentation.
tools.weaknesses: Equivariant tensor products with high spherical harmonic degrees (l > 2) scale heavily in computational complexity. Requires foundational understanding of representation theory for advanced architectural customization.

tools.name: ESMC-600M
tools.usage: ESMC-600M is a 600-million parameter Evolutionary Scale Modeling Cambrian (ESM-C) foundation model released by the Chan Zuckerberg Biohub. Trained on diverse evolutionary sequences, ESMC-600M produces rich contextual representations and accurate zero-shot contact predictions, serving as a powerful, open-weights foundation for protein sequence and structure analysis.
tools.strengths: Openly accessible weights under permissible licensing directly integrated with the HuggingFace `transformers` ecosystem. Superior representation capacity compared to older ESM-2 650M models on zero-shot variant fitness benchmarks.
tools.weaknesses: Does not directly output 3D Cartesian coordinates; requires downstream folding heads (e.g. ESMFold or folding decoders) for atomic coordinates. Inference requires a dedicated GPU with at least 8-12 GB VRAM for long protein chains.

tools.name: ESMC-300M
tools.usage: ESMC-300M is the 300-million parameter variant of the Evolutionary Scale Modeling Cambrian foundation model family from CZ Biohub. Engineered for high-throughput and resource-constrained environments, ESMC-300M delivers near-600M representation quality at double the inference speed, ideal for massive screening campaigns and edge deployments.
tools.strengths: Exceptionally high throughput-to-accuracy ratio for large-scale metagenomic and mutational screening. Low barrier to entry, easily runnable in Google Colab free-tier environments.
tools.weaknesses: Slight drop in zero-shot contact precision on complex multi-domain fold architectures relative to ESMC-600M. Cannot generate 3D all-atom coordinates without auxiliary folding decoders.

tools.name: PDBe-PubMedBERT-NER-v3.1
tools.usage: PDBe-PubMedBERT-NER-v3.1 is a specialized natural language processing model released by the Protein Data Bank in Europe (PDBe). Fine-tuned on PubMedBERT using expert-annotated structural biology literature, it accurately extracts entities including protein structures, PDB IDs, macromolecular complexes, ligands, experimental techniques, and resolution metrics from scientific text.
tools.strengths: Highly accurate extraction of structural metadata directly from raw publication abstracts and full-text articles. Pre-packaged on HuggingFace for single-line pipeline integration via `transformers.pipeline('ner')`.
tools.weaknesses: Text-based NLP model; does not process or evaluate 3D coordinate geometry directly. Specialized for English scientific literature; non-standard or informal text may require custom preprocessing.

tools.name: Boltz1-SAEs-Diffusion
tools.usage: Boltz1-SAEs-Diffusion is a mechanistic interpretability model providing Sparse Autoencoders (SAEs) trained on the internal representations of the Boltz-1 all-atom diffusion module. By decomposing polysemantic neural activations into distinct, monosemantic geometric circuits, it allows researchers to dissect how Boltz-1 learns pocket geometry, ligand recognition, and allosteric coupling.
tools.strengths: Pioneering resource for mechanistic interpretability in state-of-the-art all-atom biomolecular co-folding foundation models. Provides open weights and evaluation scripts directly usable for interpretability and safety research in structural AI.
tools.weaknesses: Analysis requires solid grounding in mechanistic interpretability concepts (dictionary learning, SAE activations). Covers specific intermediate diffusion layers; full network interpretability remains an active research area.

tools.name: BAGEL-Boltz
tools.usage: BAGEL-Boltz is an open model checkpoint and training curation released by Thinking Bio Lab. Building upon the open-source Boltz-1 architecture, BAGEL-Boltz incorporates specialized pre-layer-normalization confidence thresholds and multi-domain training curricula to enhance structural accuracy on challenging multi-domain proteins and simultaneous multi-ligand complexes.
tools.strengths: Provides transparent checkpoint steps (2200, 2300) allowing ablation of fine-tuning dynamics on all-atom co-folding. Direct drop-in compatibility with existing Boltz-1 inference pipelines.
tools.weaknesses: Large model checkpoint requires high GPU VRAM for distributed inference on large complexes. Optimized for multi-domain assemblies; minor gains on simple single-domain monomer benchmarks.

tools.name: Boltz-2 Interactive Space
tools.usage: Boltz-2 Interactive Space is a cloud-hosted Gradio web application providing an intuitive visual interface for the Boltz-2 biomolecular co-folding engine. Users can input FASTA sequences and ligand SMILES strings, execute predictions, and inspect 3D structures and binding poses directly in browser-embedded Mol* and 3Dmol viewers with confidence metrics.
tools.strengths: Instant access to cutting-edge Boltz-2 predictions without local high-end GPU hardware. Interactive inspection of confidence scores and pose orientations directly in the browser.
tools.weaknesses: Subject to HuggingFace public space compute limits and queue times during periods of heavy usage. Not intended for massive batch virtual screening campaigns.

tools.name: AlphaFold-Multimer Concatemer Design
tools.usage: This study employs AlphaFold-Multimer to model concatenated pentameric nicotinic acetylcholine receptors (nAChRs), uncovering fundamental structural and topological challenges in artificial concatemer design. The authors demonstrate how synthetic peptide linkers frequently induce subunit tilting, pore distortion, and non-physiological interface packing in predicted assemblies.
tools.strengths: Provides a critical reality check for ion channel electrophysiology studies relying on concatenated constructs. Highlights AlphaFold-Multimer's utility in identifying structural pitfalls prior to laborious wet-lab molecular biology.
tools.weaknesses: Focuses primarily on Cys-loop receptor family pentamers; generalizability to tetrameric or trimeric channels requires further study. Predictions reflect static ground states; dynamic gating transitions require complementary molecular dynamics.

tools.name: AI Peptide Dual Strategy Polymorphism
tools.usage: This work introduces a dual AI design strategy to engineer high-affinity peptide inhibitors capable of targeting highly polymorphic protein conformational landscapes. By combining ensemble structure prediction with constrained sequence generation, the method designs peptides that simultaneously bind multiple distinct conformational states or selectively inhibit pathogenic polymorphic variants.
tools.strengths: Addresses the critical challenge of target conformational plasticity and mutational escape. Combines structural generative modeling with robust biochemical validation.
tools.weaknesses: High computational complexity required to sample and balance multi-state affinity landscapes. Designed linear peptides may require chemical stapling or cyclization for optimal in vivo pharmacokinetic stability.

tools.name: NanoporeDB
tools.usage: NanoporeDB is a comprehensive structural database and analytical platform cataloging multimeric protein nanopores for single-molecule sensing and sequencing technologies. It integrates experimental cryo-EM/crystal structures with AlphaFold-Multimer predicted oligomers, annotating lumen electrostatics, constriction bottleneck diameters, and hydrophobic profiles.
tools.strengths: Unique, high-value specialized resource for the rapidly expanding field of biological nanopore sensing. Combines 3D structural models with practical biophysical and sensing capability annotations.
tools.weaknesses: Predicted multimeric symmetries may deviate slightly from flexible experimental pore conformations in membrane lipid bilayers. Does not simulate ion current translocation directly; requires external electrophysiology simulation tools.

tools.name: Enhanced-Sampling MD Rare RNA
tools.usage: This study establishes an enhanced-sampling molecular dynamics framework to overcome the static limitations of deep-learning RNA structure predictors. Starting from deep-learning predicted initial models (such as RhoFold or AlphaFold 3), the authors utilize metadynamics and replica-exchange MD to recover rare functional RNA conformational states, tertiary transitions, and riboswitch switching intermediates.
tools.strengths: Directly addresses the critical shortcoming of AI predictors in failing to capture dynamic multi-state RNA equilibria. Provides benchmarked collective variables specifically tailored for RNA backbone torsion angles.
tools.weaknesses: Enhanced MD remains computationally demanding, requiring substantial GPU cluster time for long RNA sequences. Accuracy depends on the quality of underlying empirical RNA force fields (e.g., AMBER RNA, DESRES).

tools.name: GATAD2A-CHD4 NuRD Targeting
tools.usage: This paper resolves the molecular architecture of the critical GATAD2A-CHD4 interaction interface within the human MBD2-NuRD transcriptional repressor complex using AlphaFold-Multimer modeling combined with mutational analysis and biophysical binding assays. The findings enable rational structure-guided design of competitive peptide disruptors for therapeutic intervention.
tools.strengths: Exemplary integration of AlphaFold-Multimer structural hypotheses with rigorous experimental biophysics and therapeutic design. Resolves long-standing ambiguities regarding the subunit stoichiometry of the endogenous NuRD complex.
tools.weaknesses: Covers a specific subcomplex interface; full holo-NuRD chromatin remodeling dynamics involve larger macromolecular transitions. Translating peptide disruptors into cell-permeable small-molecule therapeutics remains an ongoing objective.

tools.name: CatSper Holo-Complex Assembly
tools.usage: This study decodes the hierarchical assembly mechanisms of the massive sperm-specific CatSper cation channel complex, composed of over ten distinct transmembrane subunits. By utilizing combinatorial AlphaFold-Multimer co-folding, the authors identify the pivotal CATSPERβ–δ interaction interface that orchestrates channel holo-complex formation and sperm motility.
tools.strengths: Successfully tackles one of the most notoriously intractable multi-pass membrane complexes in structural biology. Direct clinical relevance for reproductive medicine and non-hormonal contraceptive design.
tools.weaknesses: High transmembrane lipid-solvent interactions are not explicitly represented in AlphaFold-Multimer co-folding. Requires future high-resolution cryo-EM verification of the complete intact sperm membrane supercomplex.

tools.name: Generative AI Antibody Agentic Evaluation
tools.usage: This paper presents an agentic generative AI framework for de novo antibody variable region design and multi-objective structural evaluation. The system couples 3D structural generative diffusion with autonomous agents that coordinate conformational relaxation, epitope-directed scoring, humanness checks, and developability profiling in an automated feedback loop.
tools.strengths: Represents the frontier of agentic automated workflows applied to computational antibody engineering. Minimizes human trial-and-error by automating multi-criteria candidate ranking.
tools.weaknesses: Agentic execution loops require robust API orchestration and substantial computational resources. Wet-lab expression and binding kinetics remain mandatory for final therapeutic candidate validation.

tools.name: YB-1 5D-ElectroShape Boltz Cofolding
tools.usage: Published in ACS Omega, this study develops a hybrid virtual screening workflow targeting the oncogenic RNA-binding protein YB-1. The authors combine ultra-fast 5D-ElectroShape shape/electrostatic matching with Boltz all-atom generative co-folding to discover small-molecule inhibitors targeting a cryptic, previously undruggable binding pocket on the cold shock domain.
tools.strengths: Demonstrates real-world practical application of Boltz co-folding in early-stage drug discovery. Solves the computational bottleneck of running deep-learning co-folding on multi-million compound screening libraries.
tools.weaknesses: 5D-ElectroShape filtering relies on rigid conformer generation, which can discard induced-fit conformations if conformer pools are too small. Boltz co-folding confidence metrics must be carefully calibrated against experimental affinity assays.

tools.name: Limits Deep Learning RNA Prediction
tools.usage: Published in Nucleic Acids Research, this landmark benchmark investigates the strengths and critical blind spots of deep-learning RNA structure prediction models (including AlphaFold 3, RhoFold, and related networks). The authors assess tertiary contact fidelity, non-canonical base pairing, and ligand-induced conformational shifts across extensive experimental datasets.
tools.strengths: Provides essential objective accuracy baselines for computational biologists working with AI RNA models. Highlights exact architectural components needing improvement in next-generation nucleic acid foundation models.
tools.weaknesses: Benchmark is bounded by the limited size and diversity of experimentally solved high-resolution RNA structures in the PDB. Rapid evolution of newer all-atom models means benchmarks must be continuously updated.

tools.name: Evaluating Integrin-Ligand DL Models
tools.usage: This benchmark evaluates pre-trained deep learning predictors and co-folding networks on integrin heterodimer-ligand complexes. Because integrin binding is tightly controlled by divalent cations (Mg2+, Mn2+, Ca2+) and large-scale swing-out conformational extensions, this study provides a crucial test case for AI models on metal-dependent, allosterically regulated interfaces.
tools.strengths: Fills a vital gap in benchmarking AI predictors on metal-coordinated and allosterically dynamic membrane receptors. Provides open-source benchmark scripts and standardized evaluation metrics on Zenodo.
tools.weaknesses: All-atom models that omit explicit metal coordination parameters exhibit localized inaccuracies around the MIDAS ion site. Integrin transmembrane domains are excluded to focus on the extracellular ligand-binding headpiece.

tools.name: Gauge Theory Cohomology Protein Folding
tools.usage: This theoretical treatise establishes a gauge-theoretic and cohomological framework for resolving macromolecular conformational spaces and folding pathways. By conceptualizing protein backbone deformations as connections on fiber bundles and applying persistent cohomology with semantic pixel mapping, the authors provide a rigorous topological foundation for deep-learning folding mechanics.
tools.strengths: Provides deep mathematical formalism explaining why equivariant attention networks succeed on macromolecular manifolds. Offers new topological descriptors for tracking allosteric conformational transitions.
tools.weaknesses: Highly theoretical and mathematically demanding; requires familiarity with differential topology and gauge theory. Direct algorithmic implementation into end-to-end neural training pipelines remains to be developed.

tools.name: Cross-Docking AI vs Physics Determinants
tools.usage: This extensive cross-docking and redocking study dissects the fundamental mechanistic differences between physics-based docking algorithms (e.g. Vina, Glide) and generative AI docking architectures (e.g. DiffDock, Boltz-1). The authors identify the precise receptor flexibility thresholds and pocket geometries that determine when AI models outperform classical physics engines, and vice versa.
tools.strengths: Provides an objective, data-driven synthesis of the complementary strengths of physics-based and machine-learning docking paradigms. Open dataset hosted on Figshare with complete docking runs, RMSDs, and pocket pocket-volume classifications.
tools.weaknesses: Evaluations rely on PDB-curated holo/apo pairs; highly flexible unstructured loops present challenges for both paradigms. Computational cost of large-scale diffusion inference remains higher than ultra-fast rigid grid docking.

tools.name: Benchmarking DL PROTAC Ternary
tools.usage: Published in *Proteins: Structure, Function, and Bioinformatics*, this rigorous benchmark evaluates modern deep learning co-folding architectures (AlphaFold 3, Boltz-1, Chai-1) alongside classical physics-based docking in predicting E3 ligase-PROTAC-target protein ternary complexes. The study reveals critical performance differences across flexible linkers and interface packing.
tools.strengths: Addresses one of the most critical unmet needs in targeted protein degradation (TPD) computational modeling. Identifies specific failure modes in AI co-folding when dealing with highly flexible bifunctional molecules.
tools.weaknesses: Small total number of publicly available ternary crystal structures limits the size of gold-standard test sets. Models cannot yet predict degradation efficiency (DC50) directly from static ternary poses.

tools.name: GLP-1R Orforglipron Boltz-2 MD
tools.usage: Published in the *International Journal of Biological Macromolecules*, this study leverages Boltz-2 all-atom co-folding integrated with all-atom membrane molecular dynamics to resolve variant-specific structural rearrangements and pharmacophoric shifts in human GLP-1 receptor bound to the oral non-peptide agonist orforglipron.
tools.strengths: Provides an exemplary template for combining rapid Boltz-2 co-folding with rigorous membrane physics simulations. Direct relevance for precision pharmacology and personalized diabetes/obesity therapeutics.
tools.weaknesses: Full active-state modeling requires auxiliary coupling of G-protein heterotrimer subunits. In silico predictions require confirmation across broad clinical cohort studies.

tools.name: Protein-Nucleic Acid Benchmark JCIM
tools.usage: Published in the *Journal of Chemical Information and Modeling*, this study establishes a gold-standard benchmark dataset and standardized metric suite for assessing all-atom protein-DNA and protein-RNA complex prediction models. The authors compare AlphaFold 3, RoseTTAFold2NA, and classical docking methods on interface contacts and nucleic acid deformations.
tools.strengths: Essential standardized benchmark foundation for the structural bioinformatics community. Includes detailed scripts, dataset splits, and open reproducible workflows.
tools.weaknesses: Evaluation focuses on structural precision; does not model sequence-specific binding affinities directly. Modified nucleotides (e.g. pseudouridine, 5mC) remain underrepresented in the benchmark set.

tools.name: Representation & Charge in Co-Folding
tools.usage: This methodological study systematically investigates how chemical input representation—specifically formal charge states, explicit protonation, tautomer choice, and isomeric SMILES canonicalization—drastically impacts the pose prediction accuracy and stereochemical validity of modern biomolecular co-folding engines (Boltz-1, Chai-1, AlphaFold 3).
tools.strengths: Crucial methodological alert for computational chemists deploying deep-learning co-folding in production virtual screening pipelines. Provides open validation scripts and diagnostic tools to verify ligand input readiness.
tools.weaknesses: Focuses on small-molecule ligands; effects on heavily modified peptide macrocycles require separate evaluation. Different co-folding architectures exhibit differing degrees of sensitivity to input representation.

tools.name: ECD Length Fold Calibration AFM
tools.usage: This study performs large-scale experimental testing of 834 human immune-receptor extracellular domain (ECD) interaction pairs to systematically evaluate and recalibrate AlphaFold-Multimer prediction confidence scores. The authors demonstrate that ECD length, domain count, and structural fold identity strongly influence the baseline false-positive rate and score threshold calibration.
tools.strengths: One of the largest rigorous experimental validation datasets testing AlphaFold-Multimer accuracy on membrane receptor interactomes. Provides practical, statistically grounded scoring thresholds that prevent widespread false positives in immunology.
tools.weaknesses: Restricted to extracellular domains; full-length transmembrane and intracellular signaling couplings are omitted. Experimental screening employed recombinant soluble domains which lack native cell-surface membrane clustering.

tools.name: Risk-Tiered AI Validation Drug Discovery
tools.usage: Published in the *International Journal of Molecular Sciences*, this landmark perspective and methodological blueprint establishes a risk-tiered validation framework for AI in drug discovery. Spanning structure prediction, de novo design, and binding pose generation, it provides standardized criteria for algorithmic reproducibility, negative control benchmarks, and prospective wet-lab validation.
tools.strengths: Establishes much-needed rigorous governance and quality control standards in a field often characterized by retrospective overfitting. Bridges the gap between computer science machine-learning metrics and real-world biophysical and translational criteria.
tools.weaknesses: Implementation of higher-tier validation requires dedicated wet-lab experimental collaboration and funding. Framework must remain adaptive as multi-agent autonomous synthesis systems emerge.

tools.name: Genie 3
tools.usage: Genie 3 is a state-of-the-art, fast, all-atom SE(3)-equivariant diffusion model developed by the AlQuraishi Laboratory (Columbia University / Harvard University). Unlike two-stage generative pipelines that first generate backbone geometries and subsequently pack sidechains with inverse folding models, Genie 3 natively generates full-atom Cartesian coordinates for both backbones and sidechains in a unified continuous-time diffusion process.
tools.strengths: Eliminates steric clashes and packing artifacts often introduced when separating backbone diffusion from sidechain generation. Developed by a premier structural biology AI laboratory with high reproducible engineering standards and permissive open licensing.
tools.weaknesses: Requires substantial GPU memory (>= 24GB VRAM) for large multimeric complexes exceeding 600 residues. Unconditioned generation requires downstream structural filtering (e.g. via AlphaFold 3 or ESMFold) to assess foldability.

tools.name: PepPCBench
tools.usage: PepPCBench is an open-source benchmarking suite and standardized evaluation dataset specifically constructed to evaluate modern all-atom co-folding architectures (AlphaFold 3, Boltz-1, Chai-1) on protein-peptide complexes. It provides non-redundant structural splits, interface RMSD (iRMSD), ligand RMSD (L-RMSD), fraction of native contacts (fnat), and dockQ metric pipelines.
tools.strengths: Addresses a critical evaluation gap as peptide-protein interactions involve flexible disordered transitions that challenge standard docking tools. Ready-to-use Docker and Conda environments with reproducible evaluation scripts.
tools.weaknesses: Focused strictly on linear peptidic motifs; does not natively score non-canonical macrocyclic restraints without external extensions. High-throughput benchmarking requires multi-GPU infrastructure to run inference across the full structural corpus.

tools.name: HADDOCK Cyclic-Peptides
tools.usage: HADDOCK Cyclic-Peptides is an open-source structural modeling and integrative docking repository developed by the Bonvin Laboratory (Utrecht University). It integrates specialized conformational sampling protocols for cyclic and backbone-cyclized peptides into the HADDOCK2.4 / HADDOCK3 framework, providing benchmarking scripts and restraint generators for macrocyclic therapeutics.
tools.strengths: Maintained by the core HADDOCK team with decades of authority in data-driven macromolecular docking. Directly compatible with ambiguous interaction restraints (AIRs) derived from NMR, cross-linking, or mutational data.
tools.weaknesses: Physics-based conformational sampling can be computationally expensive compared to single-shot deep learning co-folding. Requires user familiarity with CNS (Crystallography & NMR System) syntax for deep parameter customizations.

tools.name: AlphaPanda
tools.usage: AlphaPanda is a geometric deep learning architecture developed by the Yue Hu Laboratory for the joint co-design of antibody sequences and 3D CDR loop conformations. By fusing hierarchical multi-scale transformers with 3D convolutional geometric encoders, AlphaPanda simultaneously optimizes antigen-binding complementarity, loop conformation, and developability.
tools.strengths: Overcomes the sequence-structure mismatch common in decoupled design pipelines by coupling loop folding and sequence assignment. Demonstrated superior recovery of native-like CDR conformations on therapeutic antibody benchmarks.
tools.weaknesses: Requires pre-aligned antigen structures and designated epitope coordinates as spatial inputs. 3D-CNN component increases memory usage during the spatial feature encoding step.

tools.name: FoldingDiff-PyTorch
tools.usage: FoldingDiff-PyTorch is a clean, modular PyTorch implementation of the FoldingDiff generative diffusion architecture for protein backbone structure generation. It models backbone conformations in continuous angular space (phi, psi, omega angles) using denoising diffusion probabilistic models, providing an accessible codebase for generative protein backbone research.
tools.strengths: Significantly lower computational overhead during training and inference compared to all-atom Cartesian diffusion models. Highly educational and extensible codebase ideal for benchmarking novel noise schedules and loss formulations.
tools.weaknesses: Outputs backbone dihedral angles only; sidechains must be designed subsequently using tools like ProteinMPNN or LigandMPNN. Long polypeptide chains may accumulate lever-arm angular errors without Cartesian distance penalty terms.

tools.name: DiffBP
tools.usage: DiffBP is the official open-source implementation of DiffBP (Generative Diffusion of 3D Molecules for Target Protein Binding).
