tools.usage: ProteinBench is an interactive web-hosted HuggingFace Space providing a standardized, multi-task benchmark suite for evaluating protein language models and structure predictors. It ranks frontier architectures (ESM-2, ESM-3, SaProt, Ankh, ProGen2) across standardized downstream tasks—including zero-shot variant effect prediction, secondary structure classification, contact map accuracy, and binding affinity regression.
tools.strengths: Transparent, community-driven platform for objective comparison of protein foundation models.
tools.weaknesses: In-browser inference is limited to smaller model checkpoints; full 650M+ models rely on pre-computed evaluation matrices.

tools.name: foldingdiff
tools.usage: foldingdiff is an interactive HuggingFace Space demonstrating de novo protein backbone generation using continuous diffusion models formulated in internal torsion angle space (phi, psi, omega). Created by Kevin Wu, foldingdiff samples realistic, foldable polypeptide backbones by diffusing on the torus rather than 3D Cartesian coordinates, ensuring bond lengths and planar angles remain strictly physical by construction.
tools.strengths: Elegant biophysical formulation avoiding Cartesian coordinate drifting and unphysical bond stretching artifacts.
tools.weaknesses: Backbone-only generator; requires subsequent sequence design via ProteinMPNN or LigandMPNN.

tools.name: GT4SD-protein-properties
tools.usage: GT4SD-protein-properties is an interactive HuggingFace Space developed by IBM Research as part of the Generative Toolkit for Scientific Discovery (GT4SD). It calculates a comprehensive battery of biophysical developability indicators, thermodynamic stability predictions, solubility scores, hydropathy profiles, and charge distributions for engineered protein sequences and de novo designs.
tools.strengths: Clean, immediate triage tool for identifying aggregation-prone or unstable protein candidates early in the design cycle.
tools.weaknesses: Relies primarily on sequence-level physicochemical formulas and statistical predictors rather than explicit atomistic MD.

tools.name: SaProt_650M_AF2_inverse_folding
tools.usage: SaProt_650M_AF2_inverse_folding contains the 650-million-parameter foundation model weights for SaProt (Structure-aware Protein language model) fine-tuned specifically on millions of AlphaFold2 predicted structures for sequence design and inverse folding. By tokenizing structural 3D environments into discrete Foldseek vector tokens alongside amino acid identities, SaProt conditioned on 3D structures achieves state-of-the-art sequence recovery and zero-shot mutation fitness prediction.
tools.strengths: Outperforms pure sequence-based language models (ESM-2) on fitness prediction by explicitly conditioning on local 3D structural packing.
tools.weaknesses: Requires structural coordinates to be converted into Foldseek 3Di tokens prior to model inference.

tools.name: Twisted-Diffusion-Structure
tools.usage: This preprint introduces twisted diffusion, a Bayesian guidance framework for protein structure prediction models that steers generative all-atom diffusion trajectories toward specific mechanical or experimental constraints without retraining. Applied to mechanosensitive ion channels and mechanical force-bearing biomolecules, twisted diffusion samples diverse, mechanically strained open/closed states that conventional AlphaFold 3 sampling fails to explore.
tools.strengths: Provides a rigorous mathematical foundation for guiding all-atom diffusion models along functional conformational reaction coordinates.
tools.weaknesses: Requires defining appropriate steering potential functions corresponding to the experimental observable.

tools.name: PTM-DrugBinding-AI
tools.usage: This study demonstrates how all-atom structural prediction models (Boltz-1, AlphaFold 3) can be leveraged to map and predict the structural consequences of post-translational modifications (PTMs, such as phosphorylation, acetylation, and ubiquitination) on small-molecule drug binding pockets across the human proteome. The authors uncover pervasive PTM-induced pocket remodeling mechanisms that alter clinical drug efficacy and trigger resistance.
tools.strengths: Tackles a pervasive blind spot in modern medicinal chemistry where PTMs drastically alter binding affinities in disease states.
tools.weaknesses: Parameterized handling of bulky, heterogeneous PTMs (e.g., branched poly-ubiquitin chains) remains challenging for current architectures.

tools.name: Bioinf-Farma
tools.usage: Bioinf-Farma presents an automated, supervised computational pipeline that couples structural epitope prediction with recombinant protein developability metrics for high-throughput vaccine candidate triage. By combining AlphaFold-derived surface accessibility, B-cell/T-cell epitope immunogenicity, aggregation propensity, and heterologous expression yields in bacterial/mammalian hosts, Bioinf-Farma prioritizes candidates with both high immunogenicity and robust manufacturability.
tools.strengths: Prevents costly wet-lab failures by weeding out highly immunogenic antigens that suffer from insolubility or expression failure.
tools.weaknesses: Epitope prediction accuracy is influenced by HLA allele coverage and diversity in training cohorts.

tools.name: Calpain5-Targeting
tools.usage: This paper investigates structure-guided therapeutic inhibition of the calcium-dependent protease Calpain-5, whose hyperactivating mutations drive autosomal dominant neovascular inflammatory vitreoretinopathy (ADNIV). Using AlphaFold-Multimer, Chai-1, and microsecond molecular dynamics simulations, the authors model mutant Calpain-5 catalytic domain opening and discover selective macrocyclic peptide and natural product inhibitors that block pathological autolysis.
tools.strengths: Demonstrates precision structure-based design for a neglected orphan disease target lacking experimental crystal structures.
tools.weaknesses: Candidate lead molecules require in vivo validation in animal models of vitreoretinopathy.

tools.name: TRAF6-Trimerization
tools.usage: This study resolves the longstanding question of how the coiled-coil domain of tumor necrosis factor receptor-associated factor 6 (TRAF6) orchestrates high-order signalosome trimerization. Using AlphaFold 3 structural modeling combined with mutational biophysical assays, the authors uncover the precise inter-helical hydrophobic zippers and polar salt bridges that drive TRAF6 self-assembly, providing a template for designed disruptors of inflammatory NF-κB signaling.
tools.strengths: Decodes an essential immune signaling hub that had resisted classical crystallographic elucidation due to elongated flexible helices.
tools.weaknesses: Focuses on the trimeric core; transient interactions with upstream receptor cytoplasmic tails require broader pulldown modeling.

tools.name: USP21-Autoinhibition
tools.usage: Published by the Wolberger Lab, this investigation reveals the molecular mechanism governing the autoinhibition and nucleosome substrate engagement of ubiquitin-specific protease 21 (USP21). By integrating cryo-EM reconstructions with AlphaFold-Multimer complex predictions, the authors establish how an N-terminal autoinhibitory segment occludes the ubiquitin-binding cleft and how nucleosomal acidic patch binding relieves this inhibition to deubiquitinate histone H2AK119.
tools.strengths: Superb integration of AlphaFold-Multimer with high-resolution cryo-EM to explain chromatin regulatory machinery.
tools.weaknesses: Dynamic histone tail disordered states are sampled as ensemble averages.

tools.name: YdbL-Membrane-Bridge
tools.usage: This study decodes a previously uncharacterized bacterial multi-protein trans-envelope bridge system in Escherichia coli composed of YdbH, YnbE, and YdbL. Utilizing AlphaFold 3 and native mass spectrometry, the authors determine the stoichiometry and structural architecture of the span bridging the inner and outer membranes, showing that YdbL acts as a conformational gating regulator maintaining phospholipid/lipopolysaccharide homeostasis.
tools.strengths: Demonstrates AlphaFold 3's unique capability in solving complex, membrane-spanning macromolecular assemblies across periplasmic spaces.
tools.weaknesses: Lipid transport kinetics through the interior hydrophobic channel require extended molecular dynamics simulations.

tools.name: HIF2A-RNA-Switch
tools.usage: This discovery documents a post-translational functional switch where phosphorylation at Ser345 transforms hypoxia-inducible factor 2 alpha (HIF-2α) from a classical DNA-binding transcription factor into an RNA-binding protein. Using AlphaFold 3 nucleic acid co-folding and cross-linking mass spectrometry, the authors characterize the allosteric conformational rearrangement that disassembles the ARNT heterodimer and opens an RNA-binding basic cleft.
tools.strengths: Groundbreaking paradigm shift demonstrating that transcription factors can moonlighting as RNA regulators via phosphorylation switches.
tools.weaknesses: Genome-wide RNA target repertoires require high-throughput CLIP-seq cross-validation.

tools.name: Macrocycle-Diff
tools.usage: Published in Nature Chemical Biology (2025), this study establishes a general deep-learning framework for the accurate de novo design of structured, high-affinity cyclic peptide macrocycles targeting challenging protein surfaces. By incorporating periodic cyclic boundary constraints into SE(3) diffusion and sequence inverse folding models, the authors designed nanomolar macrocyclic binders against diverse clinical targets without requiring natural peptide templates.
tools.strengths: Milestone publication expanding generative protein diffusion into the highly lucrative therapeutic macrocycle space.
tools.weaknesses: Synthetic yields depend on chemical cyclization protocols for non-canonical cross-linkers.

tools.name: Post-AlphaFold-Dynamics
tools.usage: Published in Briefings in Bioinformatics (2025), this authoritative review and methodological benchmark assesses the paradigm shift from static 3D structure prediction toward dynamic conformational ensemble modeling. The paper reviews MSA subsampling tricks (ColabFold-subsampling, AF-Cluster), physics-steered generative flows (BioEmu, Topos, Flow matching), and evaluates their real-world ability to predict allosteric states and cryptic drug pockets.
tools.strengths: Definitive reference and critical benchmark for researchers transitioning from static AlphaFold models to conformational thermodynamics.
tools.weaknesses: Computational comparison highlights that Boltzmann weight recovery remains imperfect across purely data-driven methods.

tools.name: TNFR-Diffusion
tools.usage: Published in Science (2024), this landmark paper demonstrates the de novo computational design of potent agonists and antagonists targeting tumor necrosis factor receptor (TNFR) superfamily members using target-conditioned structural diffusion (RFdiffusion). The engineered miniprotein binders achieve sub-nanomolar receptor affinities, selectively controlling oligomerization geometry to either trigger robust immune signaling or block ligand binding in vivo.
tools.strengths: Definitive proof-of-concept in Science proving that generative AI protein design produces clinically viable, geometry-tailored therapeutics.
tools.weaknesses: Engineering agonistic oligomers requires precise control over valency and linker flexibility.

tools.name: DiffPepBuilder
tools.usage: Published in the Journal of Chemical Information and Modeling (2024), DiffPepBuilder introduces a conditional diffusion framework tailored specifically for generating target-specific, linear and flexible peptide binders against designated protein surface pockets. By modeling flexible backbone dynamics in tandem with chemical sidechain conditioning, DiffPepBuilder generates peptide leads with high binding complementarity and favorable conformational stability.
tools.strengths: Tailored specifically for linear bioactive peptide design, addressing the high conformational flexibility that trips up whole-protein diffusion models.
tools.weaknesses: Linear peptides require subsequent chemical stapling or cyclization to maintain serum stability in vivo.

tools.name: AFflecto
tools.usage: Published in the Journal of Molecular Biology (2025), AFflecto is an open-access web server that transforms static AlphaFold models of multi-domain and flexible proteins into physically realistic conformational ensembles. By combining low-frequency normal mode analysis, AlphaFold PAE distance constraints, and torsional sampling, AFflecto generates ensembles that accurately mirror solution scattering (SAXS) profiles and NMR dynamics.
tools.strengths: Extremely fast, biophysically grounded method for exploring inter-domain hinge bending without running multi-microsecond MD.
tools.weaknesses: Focuses on large-scale domain hinge motions; subtle local active-site loop rearrangements require fine-grained sampling.

tools.name: Membrane-Transporters-Conformation
tools.usage: Published in JCIM, this comprehensive biophysical study investigates whether modern deep-learning structure prediction methods can reliably sample both inward-facing (IF) and outward-facing (OF) functional conformations of secondary active membrane transporters. Benchmarking AlphaFold2, ColabFold MSA subsampling, and ESMFold across transport families, the authors identify key phylogenetic depth thresholds required to capture the full alternating-access transport cycle.
tools.strengths: Provides definitive operational guidelines for modeling conformational switches in drug-targetable solute carrier (SLC) transporters.
tools.weaknesses: Certain transporter families remain strongly biased toward a single dominant thermodynamic state in the training PDB.

tools.name: Watermark-AI-Proteins
tools.usage: Published in Nature (2026), this landmark paper introduces a function-preserving watermarking protocol for AI-generated protein sequences and structures. By utilizing structural redundancy and evolutionary substitution matrices to embed imperceptible statistical signatures into amino acid sequences, the system enables forensic detection and provenance tracking of de novo proteins without compromising their 3D fold, enzymatic activity, or stability.
tools.strengths: Seminal contribution to biosecurity and intellectual property provenance in the era of frontier generative biology models.
tools.weaknesses: Watermark persistence can be degraded if sequences undergo extensive iterative laboratory directed evolution.

tools.name: ADAR-RNA-Programming
tools.usage: Published in Cell (2026), this breakthrough research deciphers how tertiary RNA structures program endogenous adenosine deaminase acting on RNA (ADAR) enzymes to achieve precise, off-target-free RNA editing. Integrating AlphaFold 3 RNA-protein co-folding with high-throughput enzymatic kinetics, the authors design structured guide RNAs (gRNAs) that recruit native ADAR with high efficiency for therapeutic mRNA repair.
tools.strengths: High-impact therapeutic translation showing how all-atom AI modeling of RNA-protein complexes enables programmable in vivo gene editing.
tools.weaknesses: Requires target mRNA sequences to accommodate specific structural recruiting motifs.

tools.name: Protenix-v1
tools.usage: This paper presents Protenix-v1, a fully open-source, high-accuracy biomolecular structure prediction system developed to replicate and extend the capabilities of AlphaFold 3. Protenix provides complete open training recipes, model weights, and inference pipelines for multi-chain proteins, nucleic acids, ions, and small-molecule ligands, closing the performance gap with proprietary commercial systems.
tools.strengths: Vital community milestone ensuring that full-spectrum all-atom structure prediction remains transparent and accessible to academic researchers.
tools.weaknesses: Retaining optimal multi-GPU distributed training requires substantial compute resources (~thousands of GPU hours).

tools.name: IntraCell-Binders
tools.usage: Published in Nature Biomedical Engineering (2026), this comprehensive study demonstrates the de novo computational design of cysteine-free, disulfide-independent protein binders engineered to fold robustly in the reducing environment of the mammalian cytoplasm. Designed using RFdiffusion and ProteinMPNN, these synthetic binders function as intracellular probes, optogenetic actuators, and targeted degraders.
tools.strengths: Overcomes the major biological limitation of traditional antibodies (which misfold without disulfides) to unlock the intracellular proteome.
tools.weaknesses: Cellular delivery of protein biologics requires lipid nanoparticles, cell-penetrating peptides, or mRNA vectors.

tools.name: Diffusion-Design-Review
tools.usage: Published in the International Journal of Molecular Sciences (2026), this authoritative review dissects the mathematical foundations, geometric formulation, and experimental validation workflows of structural diffusion models in protein design. It contrasts Riemannian manifold diffusion with Euclidean flows, details rigorous in-silico quality control pipelines (AF2/Boltz validation, interface scoring), and outlines remaining thermodynamic challenges.
tools.strengths: Essential primer and critical reference guide for computational structural biologists entering the generative protein design field.
tools.weaknesses: Broad review; focused on methodological evaluation rather than releasing a standalone executable binary.

tools.name: AlphaFold-SFA
tools.usage: Published in PLoS ONE, AlphaFold-SFA introduces an enhanced sampling pipeline that combines AlphaFold 2 structural ensembles with Slow Feature Analysis (SFA) and well-tempered metadynamics. By identifying the slowest kinetic collective variables from MSA-subsampled AlphaFold trajectories, the method accelerates molecular dynamics simulations by orders of magnitude to reveal hidden cryptic drug binding pockets and allosteric pathways.
tools.strengths: Bridges the gap between machine-learned conformational snapshots and rigorous physics-based thermodynamic free energy landscapes.
tools.weaknesses: Requires standard molecular dynamics engines (e.g., GROMACS, PLUMED) for execution of biased metadynamics runs.

tools.name: agent-rosetta
tools.usage: agent-rosetta is an autonomous large language model agent framework created by Polymathic AI designed to translate high-level protein engineering objectives into executable RosettaScripts protocols. It autonomously synthesizes XML mover/filter pipelines, manages execution environments, monitors convergence metrics, and iteratively refines simulation parameters based on structural energy scoring feedback.
tools.strengths: Democratizes complex RosettaScripts protocol development, drastically reducing human error in XML script crafting and accelerating computational protein redesign.
tools.weaknesses: Requires local or cluster installations of Rosetta binaries with valid academic or commercial licenses.

tools.name: Fold2Reason
tools.usage: Fold2Reason is an open-source framework developed by GENTEL Lab demonstrating that post-training general-purpose large language models on 3D protein structure coordinates and topological invariants significantly improves both biological reasoning and abstract spatial reasoning. By tokenizing backbone geometry into invariant structural representations, the model learns complex relational graph topologies that transfer to non-biological reasoning tasks.
tools.strengths: Provides compelling evidence and open toolchains for cross-pollinating structural biology data with frontier LLM foundational reasoning capabilities.
tools.weaknesses: Compute-intensive post-training pipeline requiring multi-GPU setups for 7B+ parameter model adaptation.

tools.name: KASSPer
tools.usage: KASSPer (Kinase Active Site Structure Prediction) is a specialized deep learning suite that couples protein language model representations with small-molecule SMILES transformers to predict conformational substates of kinase catalytic pockets and rank inhibitor binding interactions. It focuses on resolving flexible activation loops (DFG-in vs DFG-out) and hinge-region contacts critical for kinase inhibitor selectivity.
tools.strengths: Highly specialized for kinase targeted therapeutics, capturing subtle conformational switches often missed by general-purpose predictors.
tools.weaknesses: Constrained specifically to kinase fold topologies; not generalizable to non-kinase catalytic cavities.

tools.name: SwitchTune
tools.usage: SwitchTune is an autonomous agentic framework engineered to design mutations that selectively stabilize or destabilize specific conformational states in bistable and allosteric proteins. Orchestrated through Model Context Protocol (MCP) tool endpoints, SwitchTune coordinates ensemble AlphaFold predictions, energy landscape perturbation calculations, and ProteinMPNN sequence optimization to drive targeted population shifts between active and inactive states.
tools.strengths: Addresses the fundamental challenge of designing dynamic, multistate functional proteins rather than static ground-state folds.
tools.weaknesses: Relies on pre-existing knowledge or predictions of both alternative conformational endpoints.

tools.name: openfold-mac-tool
tools.usage: openfold-mac-tool provides a native Apple Silicon (M1/M2/M3/M4) acceleration framework for running OpenFold 3 and local MMseqs2 database searches entirely offline. Utilizing Apple's MLX machine learning library and unified memory architecture, it eliminates dependencies on cloud APIs or remote ColabFold server queues, achieving high memory bandwidth utilization for large biomolecular complexes directly on macOS.
tools.strengths: Enables completely private, offline, high-fidelity biomolecular structure prediction on consumer Mac hardware without cloud fees or latency.
tools.weaknesses: Strictly limited to macOS systems running on Apple Silicon hardware.

tools.name: DesignForge
tools.usage: DesignForge is an open-source, reproducible hotspot-guided de novo protein binder design pipeline developed by the Kidder Lab. Designed to streamline binder generation against flat or challenging oncogenic targets, it seamlessly orchestrates solvent-mapping hotspot identification, BindCraft backbone generation, ProteinMPNN sequence optimization, AlphaFold2 validation, and short OpenMM molecular dynamics interface relaxation.
tools.strengths: Combines generative diffusion with physical molecular dynamics relaxation in a single automated containerized pipeline.
tools.weaknesses: Requires GPU resources to execute both the AlphaFold validation and OpenMM simulation stages.

tools.name: ESM3di
tools.usage: ESM3di is a lightweight, high-speed neural translator developed by the Dessimoz Lab that converts primary amino acid sequences directly into Foldseek 3Di structural alphabet strings using pretrained ESM-2 language model embeddings. By bypassing the computationally intensive 3D coordinate generation step entirely, ESM3di allows billion-scale sequence databases to be searched with Foldseek's structural sensitivity at sequence search speeds.
tools.strengths: Dramatically bridges sequence databases and structure search, enabling structural-level homology clustering across unmodeled proteomes.
tools.weaknesses: Approximates 3Di tokens probabilistically; does not generate physical 3D coordinate PDB/mmCIF files.

tools.name: Shapespyer
tools.usage: Shapespyer is an open-source Python toolchain and automated workflow orchestrator designed to streamline molecular dynamics (MD) simulations and conformational trajectory analysis for biological macromolecules and soft matter. It automates system setup, solvent box creation, energy minimization, production runs across GROMACS and NAMD engines, and post-simulation cluster analysis of AlphaFold model dynamics.
tools.strengths: Simplifies repetitive command-line MD workflows into reproducible, version-controlled Python pipelines.
tools.weaknesses: Requires external installation of underlying molecular simulation engines such as GROMACS.

tools.name: Projet_Ramachandran
tools.usage: Projet_Ramachandran is a standalone structural bioinformatics tool engineered to extract, calculate, and visualize phi-psi backbone dihedral angles from experimental and AI-predicted PDB coordinate structures. It maps residue coordinates against empirical favored and allowed energetic regions, providing automated stereochemical quality reports to identify strained backbone conformations in de novo designs.
tools.strengths: Fast, dependency-light stereochemical validation utility ideal for batch QC filtering of diffusion and flow-matching backbones.
tools.weaknesses: Focuses strictly on backbone dihedrals; does not calculate sidechain chi angles or all-atom clash scores.

tools.name: EmrE-setup
tools.usage: EmrE-setup is a specialized biophysical simulation framework and topology setup kit tailored for investigating the antiparallel dual-topology homodimer EmrE and related small multidrug resistance (SMR) transporters. It establishes rigorous parameter sets, lipid bilayer embedding configurations, and asymmetric protonation states required to simulate alternating-access substrate transport mechanisms in AI-predicted transporter models.
tools.strengths: Provides critical, pre-validated parameters for notoriously challenging membrane transporter simulations, preventing artifactual unfolding.
tools.weaknesses: Specialized parameterization focused primarily on SMR family transporters and related antiparallel topologies.

tools.name: zeca
tools.usage: zeca is an exploratory computational biophysics tool that searches for discrete cellular automata (CA) transition rules capable of modeling and explaining local secondary structure formation in proteins. By mapping amino acid sequences to discrete local state spaces, zeca uncovers minimal rule sets that govern alpha-helix nucleation and beta-sheet propagation without requiring continuous energy function minimization.
tools.strengths: Provides fresh theoretical and educational insights into the discrete information-theoretic rules underlying secondary structure formation.
tools.weaknesses: Theoretical modeling tool; not intended for high-resolution all-atom 3D coordinate prediction.

tools.name: Llama-3-1-8B-dominant-protein-SS-structure
tools.usage: Llama-3-1-8B-dominant-protein-SS-structure is an 8-billion parameter foundation language model released by the Laboratory for Atomistic and Molecular Mechanics (LAMM) at MIT (Markus Buehler's group), fine-tuned specifically to predict dominant secondary structure states and execute generative protein sequence design conditioned on target structural phenotypes. It bridges natural language understanding with structural biopolymers in a unified autoregressive architecture.
tools.strengths: Brings state-of-the-art 8B parameter autoregressive language modeling capabilities to secondary structure prediction and de novo sequence composition.
tools.weaknesses: Requires substantial GPU memory (minimum 16 GB VRAM with 4-bit/8-bit quantization) for local inference.

tools.name: antibody-esm2-finetuned
tools.usage: antibody-esm2-finetuned is a specialized antibody representation model fine-tuned on curated antibody heavy and light chain variable domain sequences using Meta's ESM-2 backbone. Engineered for immunotherapeutic discovery, it extracts contextualized residue representations that capture CDR loop hypervariability, paratope residue propensities, and germline developability scores.
tools.strengths: Extremely lightweight and fast for high-throughput screening of antibody display and next-generation sequencing repertoires.
tools.weaknesses: Focuses primarily on antibody variable fragments (Fv); not optimized for non-immunoglobulin scaffold designs.

tools.name: Human-Protein-Language-Model-0.9
tools.usage: Human-Protein-Language-Model-0.9 is a specialized protein language model pretrained exclusively on the canonical and isoform sequences of the human proteome. By restricting pretraining to human evolutionary space rather than pan-organismal UniRef databases, it maximizes sensitivity to human-specific regulatory motifs, post-translational modification sites, and pathogenicity predictions of clinical missense variants.
tools.strengths: Optimized specifically for translational medicine and human genetic disease variant interpretation.
tools.weaknesses: Less effective for bacterial, viral, or synthetic de novo proteins outside the human proteomic distribution.

tools.name: protein-folding-demo
tools.usage: protein-folding-demo is an interactive web-based protein structure prediction and inspection Space created by Edward Beeching on the Hugging Face Hub. Powered by ESMFold, it allows users to input any protein sequence, execute real-time GPU-accelerated atomic folding in seconds, and interactively explore the resulting 3D structure colored by per-residue pLDDT confidence using integrated 3Dmol.js viewer controls.
tools.strengths: Ideal for rapid educational exploration, quick structural spot-checks, and demonstrating language model folding to non-specialists.
tools.weaknesses: Subject to sequence length limitations imposed by free-tier Hugging Face Space GPU memory.

tools.name: EnsPlex
tools.usage: EnsPlex is an integrative computational framework published in bioRxiv (October 2026) that addresses the failure modes of standard AlphaFold-Multimer on challenging multisubunit complexes. It combines multi-source complementary structural sampling (integrating MSA depth perturbation, template dropout, and physics-based docking restraints) with a graph neural network for topology-aware candidate selection, dramatically improving interface accuracy on transient and high-order complexes.
tools.strengths: Directly tackles the longstanding plateau in multimer interface prediction accuracy for flexible, transient, and asymmetric assemblies.
tools.weaknesses: Requires generating multiple independent ensemble predictions per target, increasing total computational cost.

tools.name: sdAbs-LLM
tools.usage: sdAbs-LLM introduces a generative large language model framework specialized for single-domain antibodies (nanobodies / VHHs) coupled with an agentic in silico evaluation loop. The model generates functional CDR3 loop variations tailored to antigen epitopes while maintaining framework stability, followed by automated agentic screening across predicted binding affinity, solubility, and developability profiles.
tools.strengths: Combines generative sequence design with realistic biophysical developability filters tailored specifically to modular single-domain biotherapeutics.
tools.weaknesses: Requires antigen structural coordinates or epitope definitions to steer generative sampling effectively.

tools.name: EnzyGen2
tools.usage: EnzyGen2 is a generative deep learning platform engineered for the simultaneous co-design of catalytic backbones and amino acid sequences in de novo synthetic enzymes. By enforcing geometric transition-state constraints and catalytic residue placement throughout SE(3) diffusion and sequence sampling, EnzyGen2 generates novel biocatalytic scaffolds tailored to accelerate challenging chemical reactions with high catalytic efficiency.
tools.strengths: Overcomes the traditional two-step bottleneck (scaffold hallucination followed by sequence design) in computational enzymology.
tools.weaknesses: High computational requirements for transition-state quantum mechanical constraint definition.

tools.name: CycleDesigner
tools.usage: CycleDesigner is a generative pipeline published in bioRxiv that harnesses RFdiffusion and HighFold to design structurally constrained cyclic peptide binders targeting intracellular and undruggable protein surfaces. By enforcing periodic boundary conditions on backbone atoms during diffusion and scoring cyclic topologies with HighFold, CycleDesigner achieves high conformational stability and nanomolar target engagement.
tools.strengths: Pioneers generative de novo design for macrocyclic peptides, a crucial therapeutic modality for undruggable protein-protein interactions.
tools.weaknesses: Chemical synthesis of designed non-canonical cyclizations may require specialized peptide chemistry workflows.

tools.name: FlashBind
tools.usage: FlashBind is an ultra-fast structure-based virtual screening model presented in bioRxiv that combines lightweight geometric protein pocket encoders with equivariant message passing to evaluate millions of small molecules in seconds. It strikes an optimal trade-off between the biophysical precision of heavy co-folding models (like AlphaFold 3 / Boltz) and the extreme throughput required for billion-compound library exploration.
tools.strengths: Makes structure-aware virtual screening truly practical for ultra-large on-demand chemical libraries (e.g., Enamine REAL space).
tools.weaknesses: Assumes rigid or semi-rigid pocket coordinates; less suited for targets requiring extensive induced-fit rearrangements.

tools.name: EpiESM-GA
tools.usage: EpiESM-GA is a resource-efficient conformational B-cell epitope prediction framework published in bioRxiv (June 2026). It employs genetic algorithm (GA) optimization to extract the most informative embedding subspaces from ESM-2 and AlphaFold structural surfaces, achieving state-of-the-art epitope mapping performance on low-compute hardware for global pathogen surveillance and equitable vaccine development.
tools.strengths: High accuracy with minimal computational overhead, democratizing advanced structural epitope prediction for low-resource biomedical labs.
tools.weaknesses: Relies on accurate 3D antigen coordinates from AlphaFold or PDB for optimal conformational surface calculation.

tools.name: LLMsFold
tools.usage: LLMsFold is a hybrid computational drug design methodology reported in bioRxiv that marries autoregressive generative language models with rigorous biophysical free energy simulations. LLMs propose diverse de novo peptide and small-molecule binders, which are immediately funneled through AlphaFold conformational validation and alchemical free energy perturbation (FEP) scoring to filter out unphysical candidates.
tools.strengths: Provides an exemplary blueprint for integrating generative AI creativity with physical chemistry verification.
tools.weaknesses: High computational cost for the molecular dynamics and alchemical free energy simulation stages.

tools.name: MechFind
tools.usage: MechFind is an innovative deep-learning framework presented in bioRxiv that predicts step-by-step chemical reaction mechanisms for enzymes directly from 3D active site geometries. By analyzing active site residue spatial networks in AlphaFold models, MechFind identifies nucleophiles, general acid/base catalysts, and proton transfer pathways, reconstructing plausible catalytic pathways for uncharacterized orphan enzymes.
tools.strengths: Fills a critical gap between static structural prediction and dynamic biochemical reaction mechanism understanding.
tools.weaknesses: Accuracy depends on the precision of sidechain rotamer placement in predicted active site cavities.

tools.name: Emyx
tools.usage: Emyx is a next-generation all-atom protein generation architecture indexed in OpenAlex (June 2026) that achieves unprecedented sampling efficiency by formulating backbone and full sidechain coordinates in a unified continuous SE(3) diffusion manifold. By eliminating disjoint rotamer packing stages, Emyx generates sterically validated, designable all-atom macromolecules at a fraction of existing computational time.
tools.strengths: Radically accelerates all-atom de novo protein generation while improving physical stereochemistry.
tools.weaknesses: Requires GPU support for specialized SE(3) equivariant tensor contraction kernels.

tools.name: VelocityFM
tools.usage: VelocityFM is a continuous flow matching methodology documented in OpenAlex (June 2026) that predicts short-horizon molecular dynamics trajectories and conformational transitions in velocity space. Rather than predicting static ensembles, VelocityFM models the instantaneous vector fields governing atomistic velocities, capturing kinetic transition pathways between AlphaFold metastable states.
tools.strengths: Bridges the gap between static structural prediction and dynamic kinetic transition mechanisms.
tools.weaknesses: Accuracy on long-timescale millisecond transitions remains constrained by training trajectory horizons.

tools.name: CryoARC
tools.usage: CryoARC, developed by Rémi Vuillemot and Sergei Grudinin and documented in OpenAlex (May 2026), is an atomic-resolution conformational landscape reconstruction engine that extracts continuous conformational variability of protein complexes from single-particle cryo-EM images using AlphaFold evolutionary structural priors. It resolves discrete sub-states and continuous flexibility from noisy micrographs.
tools.strengths: Significantly improves the interpretability of flexible, disordered, and multi-state cryo-EM reconstructions.
tools.weaknesses: Requires large, high-quality single-particle cryo-EM image datasets for training and latent manifold mapping.

tools.name: LineageFlow
tools.usage: LineageFlow is a family-aware flow matching model indexed in OpenAlex (May 2026) that navigates phylogenetic trees to generate diverse, functional protein sequences along controlled evolutionary lineages. By conditioning vector fields on phylogenetic distances and ancestral nodes, LineageFlow enables targeted directed evolution and ancestral sequence reconstruction in silico.
tools.strengths: Provides unprecedented evolutionary controllability in generative protein sequence design campaigns.
tools.weaknesses: Requires well-curated multiple sequence alignments and reliable phylogenetic tree annotations.

tools.name: ProteinFlux
tools.usage: ProteinFlux is a generative deep learning architecture published in OpenAlex (May 2026) dedicated to predicting the dynamic conformational consequences of post-translational modifications (PTMs), such as phosphorylation, acetylation, and ubiquitination. It directly maps how local covalent modifications propagate across allosteric networks to trigger large-scale conformational remodeling.
tools.strengths: Solves a critical blind spot of standard AlphaFold models, which typically predict unmodified canonical protein states.
tools.weaknesses: Requires accurate structural models of the unmodified resting state as baseline inputs.

tools.name: RePaRank
tools.usage: RePaRank is a lightweight, high-precision neural architecture developed by Konrad Krawczyk's group (OpenAlex, March 2026) designed for antibody-antigen interface prediction and docking pose ranking via residue-pair proximity ranking. By training on relative spatial proximities rather than absolute coordinates, RePaRank achieves superior discrimination of native antibody complexes from docking decoys.
tools.strengths: Highly effective scoring filter for ranking candidate antibody poses generated by high-throughput docking algorithms.
tools.weaknesses: Specialized for antibody-antigen complexes; not calibrated for small-molecule or protein-nucleic acid docking.

tools.name: ProtSeqGen
tools.usage: ProtSeqGen is a peer-reviewed deep learning model published in BMC Bioinformatics (May 2026) that enhances protein sequence design (inverse folding) through multi-scale sequence-structure attention networks. It captures both local microenvironments (hydrogen bond networks and backbone dihedrals) and global topological folds to design sequences with higher native sequence recovery and superior thermodynamic stability.
tools.strengths: Proven peer-reviewed architecture yielding highly expressible and foldable sequences for de novo backbones.
tools.weaknesses: Inference time is slightly higher than lightweight GNN baselines due to dense multi-scale attention heads.

tools.name: GeoFlow-V2
tools.usage: GeoFlow-V2 is a unified all-atom biomolecular diffusion framework published in EuropePMC that executes both forward structure prediction and reverse de novo binder design within a single mathematical foundation. By harmonizing flow matching with physical force field priors, GeoFlow-V2 achieves state-of-the-art accuracy on monomer folding while enabling conditioned design of binders against arbitrary protein surfaces.
tools.strengths: Unified theoretical model removing the architectural divide between structural predictors and generative designers.
tools.weaknesses: Large model size requiring high-memory GPUs (24GB+ VRAM) for large multimeric complexes.

tools.name: AlphaDesign
tools.usage: AlphaDesign is a peer-reviewed protein design framework published in Molecular Systems Biology (June 2025) that operates by inverting AlphaFold neural network gradients. Through backpropagation through AlphaFold's Evoformer and structure modules, AlphaDesign hallucinates entirely novel protein folds and functional motifs with high predicted structural confidence and experimental biophysical expression.
tools.strengths: Directly optimizes sequences against AlphaFold's internal energy landscape without surrogate scoring approximations.
tools.weaknesses: Gradient descent through iterative recycling blocks requires substantial GPU memory and gradient checkpointing.

tools.name: Kideraspa
tools.usage: Kideraspa is a peer-reviewed methodology published in the Journal of Computer-Aided Molecular Design (October 2025) that utilizes a continuous diffusion model conditioned on Kidera physicochemical factors to design hyper-stable variants of Staphylococcal Protein A. Optimized for biopharmaceutical monoclonal antibody purification, it enhances alkaline stability and IgG binding affinity.
tools.strengths: Directly demonstrates real-world industrial impact of generative diffusion on biopharmaceutical manufacturing ligands.
tools.weaknesses: Model fine-tuning is currently focused on three-helix bundle protein A domains.

tools.name: Single-Sequence-KRAS-DL
tools.usage: This peer-reviewed study published in IUBMB Life (June 2026) demonstrates that single-sequence deep learning models can predict crystal-quality 3D atomic coordinates of covalent inhibitor complexes targeting oncogenic K-Ras G12 mutants (G12C, G12D, G12V). By resolving switch-I and switch-II flexible loop motions without multiple sequence alignments, it accelerates covalent oncology drug design.
tools.strengths: Crucial proof that modern all-atom neural predictors can achieve crystallographic precision on dynamic covalent oncology drug targets.
tools.weaknesses: Requires precise covalent bond parameterization between small-molecule warheads and reactive residues.

tools.name: DisDock
tools.usage: DisDock is a peer-reviewed deep learning method published in Proteins: Structure, Function, and Bioinformatics (January 2025) that tackles the challenging problem of predicting metal ion binding sites and redocking metal ions into protein structures. By learning geometric distance distributions and coordination chemistry rules, DisDock reconstructs native transition metal and alkali ion binding geometry with high precision.
tools.strengths: Addresses a major limitation of standard AlphaFold predictions, which typically output apo-structures without essential metal ions.
tools.weaknesses: Focuses on mono- and bi-nuclear metal sites; highly complex multi-metal inorganic clusters (e.g. Fe-S clusters) require additional constraints.

tools.name: T-REX
tools.usage: T-REX is an agentic campaign orchestration framework for adaptive, multi-method de novo protein binder design under finite computational budgets. Rather than executing fixed static pipelines, T-REX dynamically monitors intermediate structural metrics (e.g., interface pLDDT, contact surface area, hydrophobic match, and predicted binding energy) across RFdiffusion, ProteinMPNN, and ColabFold/AlphaFold2 trajectories, reallocating compute to promising structural motifs while pruning unviable scaffolds early.
tools.strengths: Maximizes the hit-rate of de novo binder campaigns by up to 4x per GPU-hour compared to brute-force batch generation pipelines.
tools.weaknesses: Requires integration with existing local installations of RFdiffusion, BindCraft, and ColabFold/AlphaFold2.

tools.name: DYB-Pro
tools.usage: DYB-Pro is an autonomous end-to-end protein design pipeline that hands the full in-silico engineering cycle to specialized AI agents. Given a natural language biological objective and starting sequence/target structures, the system coordinates sub-agents performing sequence optimization, backbone modeling, stability auditing, and developability filtering. All intermediate decisions and mutations are tracked in a version-controlled graph for lineage reproducibility, outputting a ranked, order-ready wet-lab synthesis shortlist.
tools.strengths: Provides a turnkey, goal-driven autonomous design loop that connects biophysical design algorithms to actionable wet-lab synthesis lists.
tools.weaknesses: Dependent on external API access or local LLM inference engines to drive high-level orchestration agents.

tools.name: origin-1
tools.usage: Origin-1 is Absci's open generative AI platform for de novo antibody design against difficult and non-immunogenic antigen epitopes. It couples structure-conditioned generative diffusion models with epitope-guided sequence generation, directly synthesizing antibody variable heavy and light chain frameworks with CDR loops designed to interact with specified target surface residues.
tools.strengths: Enables zero-shot de novo antibody generation against historically intractable targets where traditional animal immunization fails.
tools.weaknesses: Requires high-memory GPU hardware for full all-atom structure conditioning and ensemble validation.

tools.name: GenCDR
tools.usage: GenCDR is AstraZeneca's open framework providing generative antibody language models tailored for framework-conditioned complementary-determining region (CDR) design, scoring, and preference-based alignment. GenCDR enables targeted redesign of CDR loops (CDR-H1, H2, H3 and light-chain CDRs) while preserving human framework structural integrity and optimal biophysical developability profiles.
tools.strengths: Developed and benchmarked by industry antibody engineers, offering exceptional sequence diversity while respecting clinical developability constraints.
tools.weaknesses: Primarily focused on variable domain sequence generation; requires external 3D co-folding (AlphaFold-Multimer/Chai-1) to evaluate bound complexes.

tools.name: macfoldkit
tools.usage: macfoldkit is a dedicated biomolecular folding and protein design runtime optimized specifically for Apple Silicon (M1/M2/M3/M4) chips. It provides isolated, zero-dependency local environments executing Boltz-2, ColabFold, and experimental Mosaic runtimes using Apple Metal Performance Shaders (MPS) and MLX acceleration, enabling completely offline biomolecular co-folding on Mac laptops and workstations.
tools.strengths: Allows structural biologists and students to run cutting-edge co-folding models locally on Mac hardware with zero cloud setup.
tools.weaknesses: Restricted to macOS on Apple Silicon; execution speed on base 8GB/16GB unified memory models is constrained for large multimers (>1500 residues).

tools.name: colabfold_boltz_structure_confidence_pipeline
tools.usage: colabfold_boltz_structure_confidence_pipeline is an open benchmark suite designed to evaluate the real-world fidelity of deep learning structure confidence metrics (pLDDT and PAE) against true experimental lDDT scores across viral and human targets. The pipeline systematically investigates the thermodynamic and geometric costs of docking small molecules into predicted AlphaFold/Boltz receptor conformations versus corresponding experimental crystal structures.
tools.strengths: Provides critical, unbiased empirical guidance for when predicted protein structures are reliable enough for structure-based drug design.
tools.weaknesses: Currently pre-configured primarily around coronavirus and viral target benchmark sets; extending to whole proteomes requires custom dataset ingestion.

tools.name: BepiPocket-1.0
tools.usage: BepiPocket-1.0, developed by the Morten Nielsen Lab, is a specialized computational tool for the structural analysis and binding pocket prediction of antibody-antigen complexes. It combines geometric pocket detection with antibody-specific residue contact propensities to identify functional conformational B-cell epitopes and guide antibody engineering.
tools.strengths: Bridges the gap between raw geometric surface pocket detectors and biological antibody-antigen interaction reality, providing superior epitope localization.
tools.weaknesses: Performance depends on the quality of antigen surface models; flexible loop regions with low pLDDT can introduce false-positive pocket boundaries.

tools.name: ParaLig
tools.usage: ParaLig is an open-source, high-throughput parallel toolchain developed by the Amedeo Caflisch Laboratory (University of Zurich) for automated ligand-based and receptor-based docking preparation. It provides MPI-accelerated routines for ligand force-field parameterization, low-energy conformer generation with free or restrained dihedral sampling, and combinatorial library construction for virtual screening pipelines.
tools.strengths: Industrial-grade throughput and robustness for preparing multi-million compound libraries for structural docking against predicted protein targets.
tools.weaknesses: Requires Linux HPC environments with MPI installations for optimal distributed execution.

tools.name: bslib
tools.usage: bslib is an open computational biology library and database generation suite developed by Janez Konc and colleagues for extracting, storing, and rapidly querying 3D protein binding site surfaces. It provides algorithms to compile comprehensive repositories of pre-calculated binding pockets and bound ligands, enabling proteome-wide structural pocket alignment, polypharmacology prediction, and drug repurposing.
tools.strengths: Enables rapid structural polypharmacology and off-target liability screening across the entire Protein Data Bank and AlphaFold DB.
tools.weaknesses: Requires disk storage for pre-computed surface graphs; highly flexible pockets may escape rigid graph matching.

tools.name: ULaMDyn
tools.usage: ULaMDyn is an open unsupervised machine learning program designed for the deep structural analysis of macromolecular dynamics trajectories. It employs non-linear dimensionality reduction, density-based clustering, and transition network mapping to extract metastable states, folding intermediates, and allosteric conformational switches from complex MD simulations without relying on human-selected collective variables.
tools.strengths: Automates the identification of cryptic pockets and functional protein conformational transitions without manual collective variable bias.
tools.weaknesses: Computational scaling requires trajectory downsampling or GPU acceleration for multi-microsecond all-atom systems.

tools.name: MemTropy
tools.usage: MemTropy is an optimized simulation and thermodynamic analysis framework written in C++ and Cython for investigating membrane proteins within explicit and implicit lipid bilayer environments. It specifically quantifies the conformational entropy changes associated with transmembrane helix reorientation, ligand binding, and lipid-protein allosteric coupling.
tools.strengths: Provides rare quantitative insights into the entropic penalties of membrane protein activation and allosteric signaling.
tools.weaknesses: Specialized for membrane systems; requires basic familiarity with lipid bilayer coordinate setups and force fields.

tools.name: PDBEurope-PubMedBERT-ProteinStructure-NER
tools.usage: PDBEurope-PubMedBERT-ProteinStructure-NER is an official language model released by the Protein Data Bank in Europe (PDBe) fine-tuned specifically for named entity recognition (NER) of 3D macromolecular structure concepts. The model automatically parses scientific articles to extract mentions of secondary structure motifs, active site residues, quaternary interfaces, ligands, and cryo-EM resolution metrics with high precision.
tools.strengths: Enables automated large-scale literature mining to enrich structural databases and connect predicted protein models to published experimental evidence.
tools.weaknesses: Restricted to text classification/token labeling; does not process raw 3D atomic coordinates directly.

tools.name: ligandmpnn-noise005
tools.usage: ligandmpnn-noise005 is an optimized model checkpoint of LigandMPNN fine-tuned with a low Gaussian coordinate noise level (sigma = 0.05 A). This checkpoint is specifically calibrated for high-precision inverse folding of protein binding pockets around rigid, tightly bound small molecules, cofactors, and nucleic acid ligands where subtle sub-angstrom sidechain-ligand packing determines affinity.
tools.strengths: Significantly outperforms default 0.20 A and 0.30 A noise checkpoints when redesigning catalytic residues and tightly sterically constrained pocket geometries.
tools.weaknesses: More sensitive to backbone coordinate strain in de novo diffused backbones; best used after minor minimization or with high-confidence scaffolds.

tools.name: bagel_protein_boltz
tools.usage: bagel_protein_boltz_train_2200 is an open-source deep learning checkpoint developed by Thinking Bio Lab implementing the Boltz architecture with pre-computed scaling factors and pre-layer-norm stabilization, trained across the BAGEL biophysical dataset. The model provides enhanced numerical stability during iterative diffusion sampling of large multi-chain protein-ligand complexes.
tools.strengths: Demonstrates excellent stability during long trajectory diffusion sampling without requiring aggressive coordinate clamping.
tools.weaknesses: Requires compatible Boltz execution frameworks supporting custom scaler tensor injections.

tools.name: Boltz_Interface
tools.usage: Boltz_Interface is an open Hugging Face Space developed by Cpt-Nemo providing a full-featured Gradio web GUI for the Boltz biomolecular co-folding engine. It allows users to input multi-chain FASTA sequences and small-molecule SMILES strings, launch inference, and interactively explore predicted all-atom 3D structures with pLDDT coloring and PAE matrix heatmaps directly in the browser.
tools.strengths: Drastically democratizes access to Boltz for experimental biochemists, chemists, and students without access to high-end Linux GPU workstations.
tools.weaknesses: Inference time is bounded by Hugging Face Space GPU hardware tiers; large complexes (>1000 residues) may experience queuing delays.

tools.name: ComP-Multimodal-DNA-Docking
tools.usage: This comparative benchmark by Helsem et al. systematically investigates the DNA-protein binding mechanisms of the bacterial competence protein ComP using AlphaFold 3, RoseTTAFold2NA, and Chai-1, followed by energetic re-docking and refinement in HADDOCK. The study discovers two distinct, robustly modeled conformational binding modes corresponding to specific vs non-specific DNA sequence interactions, providing crucial benchmark insights into nucleic acid prediction reliability across modern all-atom models.
tools.strengths: One of the most thorough independent evaluations of nucleic acid co-folding capabilities across the three leading generative architectures.
tools.weaknesses: Focuses on a specific bacterial DNA-binding system; broader generalizability to RNA tertiary assemblies remains to be expanded.

tools.name: Cancer-Surfaceome-Binders
tools.usage: Broske et al. demonstrate the successful prospective end-to-end design, production, and in vitro/in cellulo validation of de novo designed protein binders targeting critical cancer cell surface receptors. Utilizing RFdiffusion and ProteinMPNN with AlphaFold validation, the authors engineered picomolar-to-nanomolar affinity binders that selectively discriminate tumor cells and enable targeted therapeutic delivery without traditional hybridoma or phage display screening.
tools.strengths: Provides definitive experimental proof that modern generative protein design pipelines can replace animal immunization and library screening for therapeutic oncological targets.
tools.weaknesses: In vivo pharmacokinetic stability and immunogenicity profiling require additional engineering iterations.

tools.name: Viral-Quaternary-Atlas
tools.usage: Han, Steinegger, Dallago et al. present a comprehensive, proteome-wide structural atlas mapping predicted quaternary assemblies across pandemic-relevant viral families (Coronaviridae, Filoviridae, Flaviviridae, Orthomyxoviridae). Using scalable distributed AlphaFold-Multimer and ColabFold pipelines, the authors predict homomeric and heteromeric oligomerization states, uncovering hundreds of previously uncharacterized cryptic viral functional complexes.
tools.strengths: An extraordinary community resource that significantly advances structural virology and pandemic preparedness.
tools.weaknesses: Heteromeric viral-host complexes are not fully covered; predicted oligomers without homologous templates require experimental confirmation.

tools.name: Tie2-DeNovo-Activator
tools.usage: McCurdy, Baker, Ruohola-Baker et al. report the de novo computational design of geometrically defined multimeric protein architectures that selectively activate the Tie2 receptor pathway without requiring integrin co-receptor cross-talk. By programming exact geometric spacing and valency between designed Tie2 binding domains, the synthetic ligands promote vascular stabilization and endothelial barrier protection in vivo.
tools.strengths: Demonstrates the pinnacle of structural biology design: creating synthetic agonists with tailored signaling properties that surpass natural evolutionary ligands.
tools.weaknesses: Large multi-subunit protein complexes pose manufacturing and formulation challenges compared to traditional monoclonal antibodies.

tools.name: Enzyme-Miniaturization-PLM
tools.usage: Lala et al. introduce an energy landscape-guided framework that utilizes dense representations from protein language models (ESM-2) to systematically excise non-essential peripheral loops and domains from large natural enzymes while preserving the active site catalytic architecture. The resulting miniaturized enzymes retain full catalytic efficiency while exhibiting enhanced thermal tolerance, expression yield, and cellular delivery profiles.
tools.strengths: Opens transformative possibilities for industrial biocatalysis and gene therapy, allowing large enzymes to fit inside viral vector packaging limits.
tools.weaknesses: Requires careful experimental validation of substrate access channels, which can be inadvertently altered by nearby scaffold truncations.

tools.name: PhysBioDynamics
tools.usage: Feng et al. present a physics-grounded generative architecture for simulating all-atom protein conformational dynamics and rare kinetic transition paths. By embedding Hamiltonian mechanics and energy gradient priors into continuous flow matching networks, the model samples thermodynamic Boltzmann distributions and predicts transition state ensembles up to 1,000x faster than traditional all-atom MD.
tools.strengths: Bridges the gap between static AlphaFold predictions and millisecond-scale molecular dynamics, providing accurate kinetic and thermodynamic ensembles.
tools.weaknesses: Requires GPU acceleration with high floating-point precision for long-horizon numerical ODE integration.

tools.name: Rewriting-Protein-Alphabets
tools.usage: Pantolini, Steinegger, Schwede, Durairaj et al. investigate the fundamental information density of biological sequences by using language models to rewrite the standard 20-letter amino acid alphabet into compressed, functionally optimized discrete token spaces. The authors show that protein language models trained on reduced 10-14 letter alphabets maintain near-identical structural fold and functional prediction capability while drastically reducing sequence entropy.
tools.strengths: Provides fundamental insights into the redundancy of the genetic code and offers efficient tokenization strategies for next-generation protein foundation models.
tools.weaknesses: Subtle stereochemical features like proline cis-trans isomerism and cysteine disulfide bridges require dedicated token treatment.

tools.name: ExplainBind
tools.usage: ExplainBind by Meng et al. is an explainable deep learning framework that predicts protein-ligand binding affinities while decomposing predictions into quantifiable non-covalent interaction networks (hydrogen bonds, pi-pi stacking, salt bridges, and hydrophobic contacts). Unlike black-box neural docking scorers, ExplainBind provides residue-level and atom-level attribution maps that align directly with medicinal chemistry intuition.
tools.strengths: Solves the critical interpretability problem in machine-learning virtual screening, giving chemists actionable structural rationale for affinity predictions.
tools.weaknesses: Requires accurate co-folded or docked 3D receptor-ligand complex coordinates as input.

tools.name: FoldKit
tools.usage: FoldKit by Levine, Pathil, Nitz et al. is an open high-performance Python library engineered for the scalable storage, indexing, querying, and retrieval of multi-million structure co-folding datasets generated by AlphaFold-Multimer, Boltz-1/2, and Chai-1. FoldKit uses chunked array storage formats (Zarr/HDF5) and spatial indexing to enable instant sub-millisecond retrieval of coordinates, PAE matrices, and contact maps.
tools.strengths: Essential infrastructure for teams running high-throughput screening campaigns that generate terabytes of co-folding predictions.
tools.weaknesses: Focused purely on data engineering, storage, and retrieval; does not perform molecular modeling or folding inference itself.

tools.name: HighMorph
tools.usage: HighMorph, published in the Journal of Medicinal Chemistry by Lan et al., is a computational design strategy for generating de novo cyclic peptide inhibitors by morphing and recapitulating complex protein-protein interaction (PPI) interfacial hotspots into stable macrocyclic scaffolds. HighMorph couples geometric backbone circularization with structural inverse folding and MD validation to produce cell-permeable cyclic peptides targeting flat, undruggable protein interfaces.
tools.strengths: Demonstrates high experimental inhibitory potency against challenging oncology targets previously considered undruggable by traditional small molecules.
tools.weaknesses: Macrocycle synthesis and non-canonical amino acid incorporation require specialized peptide chemistry facilities.

tools.name: binderqc
tools.usage: binderqc by Siddhant Sharma is an automated biophysical quality control and purification-tag scoring suite designed for synthetic biology and protein engineering pipelines. Given de novo binder structures from RFdiffusion or BindCraft, binderqc audits terminal flexibility, hydrophobic patches, electrostatic dipole moments, and optimal placement of purification tags (His-tag, Flag-tag, Avi-tag) to avoid disrupting target binding interfaces.
tools.strengths: Prevents costly experimental failures caused by purification tags clashing with target binding interfaces or triggering insoluble inclusion bodies.
tools.weaknesses: Heuristic and structure-based scoring; requires experimental expression screening for definitive verification.

tools.name: Mac1-Cofolding-Evaluation
tools.usage: Published in eLife by Kim, Correy, Fraser et al., this landmark study presents a rigorous prospective evaluation of biomolecular co-folding architectures (AlphaFold 3, Boltz, and Chai) across hundreds of SARS-CoV-2 Mac1 domain-ligand complexes. By benchmarking against hundreds of crystallographic ground-truth complexes and three prospective virtual screens, the authors delineate exact accuracy boundaries, false-positive enrichment modes, and pose prediction limitations in real-world drug discovery.
tools.strengths: Provides the definitive experimental standard for evaluating generative co-folding models in practical structure-based lead optimization.
tools.weaknesses: Focused primarily on the Mac1 macrodomain enzyme target; multi-domain receptor complexes may exhibit additional conformational variables.

tools.name: Natural-Language-Binder-Shortlisting
tools.usage: Lee, Yoo, Seo et al. propose a natural-language-guided, generator-agnostic shortlisting pipeline for de novo protein binder engineering. The framework allows researchers to express high-level biological criteria (e.g., 'compact all-helical scaffold targeting epitope region A with high thermal stability and zero cysteine residues') in plain text, which is parsed by an LLM-guided biophysical agent to filter and rank millions of candidate designs across RFdiffusion, Chroma, and BindCraft.
tools.strengths: Democratizes complex structural filtering scripts, allowing experimental biologists to easily formulate nuanced computational triage rules.
tools.weaknesses: Relies on an LLM parser to interpret natural language prompts, requiring sanity checks on generated filtering boundaries.

tools.name: CheMelt
tools.usage: Published in Protein Science by Lampinen, Burastero et al., CheMelt is an open biophysical analysis platform and experimental protocol for the global thermodynamic dissection of thermal and chemical denaturation in de novo designed proteins. Given that machine-learning-designed proteins frequently exhibit hyper-stability (melting temperatures exceeding 100°C), CheMelt provides robust models to quantify exact unfolding free energies (ΔG) and cooperativity.
tools.strengths: Fills a critical need in computational protein design by enabling accurate experimental stability measurement of AI-generated hyper-stable proteins.
tools.weaknesses: Requires experimental denaturation data from CD or differential scanning fluorimetry instruments.

tools.name: Surfaceome-Targetable-Sites
tools.usage: Published in PNAS by Balbi, Sadek, Marchand, Correia et al., this study provides a comprehensive computational and experimental mapping of targetable structural sites across the human surfaceome. By scanning thousands of membrane receptor extracellular domains using surface-patch descriptors and AlphaFold models, the authors identify druggable functional epitopes and validate de novo designed binders targeting these conserved sites.
tools.strengths: Transformative roadmap for the design of novel biotherapeutics, CAR-T targeting domains, and diagnostic sensors against previously unexplored receptors.
tools.weaknesses: Post-translational glycosylation of surfaceome receptors must be accounted for during detailed atomic docking.

tools.name: Reading-TEA-Leaves
tools.usage: Reading TEA Leaves introduces a topological profiling method termed Target Epitope Accessibility (TEA) to systematically diagnose whether a specified antigenic surface region is sterically and energetically accessible to de novo protein binders. The method computes approach cones, steric collision envelopes, and desolvation penalties, preventing computational binder design pipelines from generating infeasible scaffolds against buried or restricted epitopes.
tools.strengths: Dramatically reduces wasted GPU compute by eliminating binder generation attempts on sterically occluded or energetically unfavorable surface regions.
tools.weaknesses: Static accessibility analysis; target conformational flexibility (induced fit) can open cryptic access paths that static cones miss.

tools.name: OTalign
tools.usage: Published in Bioinformatics by Kim, Bae, Jo, Joo et al., OTalign is an optimal transport-based sequence and structural alignment tool for detecting remote protein homologs that share structural fold architecture despite sequence identities below 15% (the twilight zone). OTalign formulates pairwise protein alignment as an entropic regularized optimal transport problem over dense ESM-2 residue embeddings.
tools.strengths: Significantly expands remote homology detection, functional annotation of uncharacterized proteins, and evolutionary trace discovery.
tools.weaknesses: Sinkhorn iterations introduce slight computational overhead compared to classic dynamic programming on short sequences.

tools.name: AbTune
tools.usage: Published in Briefings in Bioinformatics by Xu and Bonvin, AbTune is a parameter-efficient fine-tuning framework for adapting general protein language models (ESM-2) to specialized antibody engineering tasks. By selectively updating critical transformer layers identified through attention attribution and freezing general evolutionary representations, AbTune achieves state-of-the-art paratope prediction, affinity optimization, and developability scoring with minimal GPU training overhead.
tools.strengths: Enables academic labs and smaller biotechnology teams to tailor massive protein foundation models to antibody campaigns on a single desktop GPU.
tools.weaknesses: Specialized for antibody and nanobody scaffolds; general enzyme or multimer engineering tasks require distinct layer attribution masks.

tools.name: DAQplugin
tools.usage: DAQplugin by Terashi, Zhu, and Kihara is an interactive deep learning-based validation and density assessment plugin for UCSF ChimeraX. Using 3D convolutional neural networks that evaluate local Density Around atom Quality (DAQ), the tool allows structural biologists to interactively audit, highlight, and repair poorly fitted amino acid residues, misaligned secondary structures, and stereochemical errors in cryo-EM protein models.
tools.strengths: Greatly improves cryo-EM model quality and user efficiency by bringing AI-powered validation directly inside the world's most popular structural visualization environment.
tools.weaknesses: Requires local UCSF ChimeraX installation; GPU acceleration recommended for real-time map scoring.

tools.name: EMAlign
tools.usage: Marking the landmark Issue #1000 milestone for Alphafoldology, EMAlign by Cao, Chen, Li, and Huang introduces a deep learning framework for the precise, automated rigid and flexible alignment of cryo-EM density maps using neural main-chain probability distributions. By transforming raw, noisy voxel densities into probabilistic backbone feature vectors, EMAlign enables accurate cross-map superposition, domain movement tracking, and conformational heterogeneity analysis across multiple structural states.
tools.strengths: Provides an automated, objective foundation for comparing macromolecular machines across functional cycles without manual marker placement.
tools.weaknesses: Highly disordered peripheral loops without clear backbone density may yield diffused probability distributions.

tools.name: drug-discovery-agent-skills
tools.usage: drug-discovery-agent-skills by K-Dense AI is an open library of Model Context Protocol (MCP) servers and modular agent skills designed to equip LLM coding agents with autonomous capabilities for structural biology and drug discovery. The toolkit provides plug-and-play interfaces for querying AlphaFold DB, running AutoDock Vina / Smina docking, parsing PDB/mmCIF structures, profiling ADMET properties, and executing multi-step virtual screening campaigns.
tools.strengths: Enables seamless plug-and-play integration of computational chemistry and structural biology capabilities into modern agentic frameworks.
tools.weaknesses: Requires local installations of underlying docking binaries (e.g., AutoDock Vina) for local docking tasks.

tools.name: rfdiffusion-rfpeptides-mps
tools.usage: rfdiffusion-rfpeptides-mps is an optimized fork of Baker Lab's RFdiffusion and RFpeptides tailored specifically for Apple Silicon (M1/M2/M3/M4) architectures using PyTorch Metal Performance Shaders (MPS). It eliminates CUDA dependencies, enabling structural biologists and computational chemists to design de novo linear and cyclic peptide binders locally on macOS workstations without relying on cloud GPU clusters.
tools.strengths: Enables zero-setup, confidential de novo peptide design directly on Mac hardware without cloud fees or external GPU server queuing.
tools.weaknesses: Restricted to Apple Silicon hardware; large multi-chain protein complexes (>800 residues) may encounter memory limits on 8GB/16GB unified memory models.

tools.name: boltz-antibody-antigen-complex-prediction
tools.usage: boltz-antibody-antigen-complex-prediction is an open benchmarking and pipeline repository assessing the capability of the all-atom diffusion model Boltz-1/2 for antibody-antigen complex modeling. It systematically evaluates epitope-paratope contact recovery, CDR-H3 loop conformations, and interfacial binding metrics across standardized non-redundant antibody benchmark sets compared to AlphaFold-Multimer and Chai-1.
tools.strengths: Provides empirical clarity on the strengths and blind spots of all-atom diffusion architectures when applied to highly flexible antibody CDR loops.
tools.weaknesses: Requires substantial GPU memory (minimum 24GB VRAM) for large antigen complexes.

tools.name: metalic
tools.usage: metalic, developed by InstaDeep, is a specialized deep learning framework for identifying, classifying, and modeling metal ion binding sites in protein structures. Given experimental PDBs or AlphaFold-predicted coordinate files, metalic predicts the presence, coordinate location, and coordination geometries of diverse transition metal and alkali earth ions (Zn, Fe, Mg, Ca, Cu, Mn, etc.) with high geometric precision.
tools.strengths: Essential for functional annotation of metalloenzymes and designing metal-dependent catalytic active sites in de novo proteins.
tools.weaknesses: Accuracy can decrease in flexible apo-conformations where coordinating sidechains deviate from holo crystal geometries.

tools.name: abagym-zero-shot-antibody-antigen
tools.usage: abagym-zero-shot-antibody-antigen is an open benchmarking suite and evaluation framework for testing zero-shot variant effect and binding affinity predictors on antibody-antigen complexes. It standardizes datasets across deep mutational scanning (DMS) campaigns on therapeutic antibodies (e.g., trastuzumab, pertuzumab, CR3022), evaluating log-likelihood ratios from ESM-2, ESM-C, AntiBERTy, and structure-conditioned models without task-specific training.
tools.strengths: Provides an unbiased, leak-free benchmark for comparing foundation protein models on real-world antibody affinity maturation tasks.
tools.weaknesses: Restricted to single-point and low-order mutational datasets where experimental binding Kd or enrichment values are published.

tools.name: target-conditioned-peptide-binder-design
tools.usage: target-conditioned-peptide-binder-design is an automated computational pipeline for generating high-affinity peptide binders directed against specified receptor surface targets. Integrating RFdiffusion hotspot conditioning, ProteinMPNN sequence sampling, and ColabFold/AlphaFold2 validation, the workflow provides automated trajectory filtering, interface energy calculation, and clustering to deliver ranked peptide candidate lists.
tools.strengths: Streamlines the multi-step peptide binder design process into a single executable pipeline suitable for both academic and industrial screening.
tools.weaknesses: Requires external installation of RFdiffusion and AlphaFold/ColabFold environments.

tools.name: AlphaFold3_workflow
tools.usage: AlphaFold3_workflow is an open, production-grade Snakemake pipeline for orchestrating large-scale AlphaFold 3 structure prediction campaigns across HPC clusters and cloud instances. It automates input JSON construction for proteins, DNA, RNA, ligands, and ions, handles Slurm GPU batch job scheduling, and executes automated post-processing, quality metric aggregation (pLDDT, PAE, ipTM), and PDB/mmCIF trajectory extraction.
tools.strengths: Scales AlphaFold 3 predictions from single manual submissions to thousands of biomolecular complexes with full workflow reproducibility.
tools.weaknesses: Requires valid AlphaFold 3 model parameters and local model installation according to DeepMind's academic release terms.

tools.name: Gromologist
tools.usage: Gromologist, developed by the KomBioMol group, is an advanced Python library for inspecting, programmatically editing, and generating GROMACS molecular dynamics topology (.top) and coordinate files. It enables automated parameter assignment, virtual site construction, charge modification, topology merging for multimeric complexes, and validation of force field parameters for biomolecular simulation.
tools.strengths: Invaluable for automated simulation pipelines and high-throughput MD relaxation of AI-generated protein structures.
tools.weaknesses: Focused specifically on GROMACS topologies; converting to AMBER or CHARMM requires intermediate formats.

tools.name: CIFDock
tools.usage: CIFDock is an open computational biology protocol built on the CHARMM molecular simulation engine for flexible, induced-fit ligand docking. By coupling extensive ligand conformational sampling with harmonic receptor sidechain and backbone relaxation, CIFDock accurately models ligand binding into predicted pockets that undergo conformational adaptations upon ligand engagement.
tools.strengths: Excels at docking into cryptic or partially closed AlphaFold pockets where rigid docking engines fail.
tools.weaknesses: Computationally more intensive than grid-based docking engines due to all-atom energy minimizations.

tools.name: charmm2gmx
tools.usage: charmm2gmx is an open-source Python tool designed to convert CHARMM toppar (topology and parameter) files directly into native GROMACS force field directory structures. It parses complex CHARMM stream (.str) and parameter (.prm/.rtf) files—including non-standard post-translational modifications, lipids, and specialized drug-like cofactors—and generates clean, GROMACS-compliant [ moleculetype ] and parameter tables.
tools.strengths: Bridges the gap between CHARMM's extensive chemical matter parameterizations and GROMACS' high GPU simulation performance.
tools.weaknesses: Requires basic understanding of force field directory structures and stream file dependencies.

tools.name: GBNeck2-CpHMD-Patches
tools.usage: GBNeck2-CpHMD-Patches, developed by the Jana Shen Laboratory, provides source code patches and scripts implementing the Continuous Constant pH Molecular Dynamics (CpHMD) method in Amber. Utilizing the GBNeck2 implicit solvent model, the framework allows continuous titration of acidic and basic residues alongside conformational sampling, enabling accurate calculation of residue pKa shifts, proton-coupled conformational changes, and pH-dependent protein stability.
tools.strengths: Provides unmatched physical accuracy for dissecting pH-dependent biological mechanisms and titratable residue states in AI-modeled structures.
tools.weaknesses: Requires compiling Amber source code with the provided patch files.

tools.name: ProtSent-V2-ESMC-300M
tools.usage: ProtSent-V2-ESMC-300M is a protein sequence representation model trained using contrastive sentence-transformer objectives on top of EvolutionaryScale's ESM-C (Cambrian) 300M foundation model. It maps entire protein primary sequences into fixed-dimensional semantic vector spaces optimized for cosine-similarity retrieval, enabling sub-millisecond remote homology search, functional clustering, and zero-shot family classification across millions of sequences.
tools.strengths: Dramatically outperforms raw unpooled language model representations in protein family classification and functional nearest-neighbor search.
