tools.weaknesses: Provides sequence-level embeddings rather than residue-level 3D coordinate reconstructions.

tools.name: Boltz1-SAEs-L2-Diffusion
tools.usage: Boltz1-SAEs-L2-Diffusion is an open checkpoint suite of Sparse Autoencoders (SAEs) trained directly on the internal representations of the Boltz-1 biomolecular co-folding diffusion trunk (Layer 2). By projecting dense intermediate diffusion activation tensors into highly sparse, overcomplete feature spaces, this model allows structural biologists to identify interpretable geometric features corresponding to secondary structure motifs, ligand contact points, and domain boundaries.
tools.strengths: Pioneers mechanistic interpretability inside all-atom diffusion models, moving beyond black-box protein structure generation.
tools.weaknesses: Trained specifically on Layer 2 diffusion activations of Boltz-1; requires corresponding Boltz-1 trunk inference code to extract features.

tools.name: ligandmpnn-noise030
tools.usage: ligandmpnn-noise030 is an official fine-tuned LigandMPNN checkpoint trained with 0.30 Å Gaussian coordinate noise added to backbone atoms during training. This elevated noise regime encourages the model to generate broader sequence diversity and avoid overfitting to rigid crystal or predicted backbone coordinates, making it especially well-suited for redesigning flexible loops, multimeric interfaces, and dynamic protein-ligand binding pockets.
tools.strengths: Yields substantially higher sequence novelty and experimental expression success rates when designing sequences for unrelaxed diffusion backbones.
tools.weaknesses: Higher noise may occasionally propose non-canonical sidechain conformations in extremely tight active site geometries.

tools.name: esm3-conformational-sampling
tools.usage: esm3-conformational-sampling is an interactive HuggingFace Space developed by Tonic demonstrating generative conformational sampling and structural ensemble generation using EvolutionaryScale's multimodal ESM-3 foundation model. Users can input primary sequences or partial structural motifs to explore alternative backbone fold states, generate structural ensembles, and visualize predicted 3D structures directly in the browser.
tools.strengths: Allows researchers and educators to immediately test ESM-3's all-atom generative power without configuring heavy local PyTorch runtimes.
tools.weaknesses: Subject to HuggingFace Space GPU quota limits and sequence length caps for interactive sessions.

tools.name: Plasmodium CSP Targeting RFdiffusion Peptides
tools.usage: This preprint presents the de novo computational design of cyclic and topologically constrained peptide inhibitors targeting the major repeat region of the Plasmodium falciparum circumsporozoite protein (CSP). Leveraging RFdiffusion with cyclic symmetry restraints and ProteinMPNN sequence optimization, the authors generated macrocyclic binders that achieve nanomolar affinity and protect hepatocytes from sporozoite invasion in vitro.
tools.strengths: Provides an effective blueprint for applying generative diffusion models to combat challenging infectious disease pathogens using stable cyclic peptides.
tools.weaknesses: Synthesis of complex cyclic peptides with non-canonical linkers requires specialized chemical synthesis routes.

tools.name: Poxvirus Entry Binders via RFdiffusion
tools.usage: In this prospective study, the authors apply RFdiffusion and ProteinMPNN to create de novo mini-protein binders targeting essential components of the poxvirus multiprotein entry fusion complex (EFC). The computationally designed binders target conserved hydrophobic interfaces across orthopoxviruses, exhibiting picomolar to low-nanomolar affinities and broad neutralizing potency against vaccinia and monkeypox (mpox) virions.
tools.strengths: Demonstrates rapid computational generation of potent, hyper-stable antiviral countermeasures against emerging biosecurity threats.
tools.weaknesses: Requires structural coordinates of viral entry machinery; unmodeled membrane-proximal regions could alter binding kinetics.

tools.name: Phosphotyrosine-Peptide-Binders
tools.usage: This study achieves the de novo computational design of synthetic protein domains that specifically recognize phosphorylated tyrosine (pTyr) residues within targeted sequence contexts. Mimicking and surpassing natural SH2 domains, the engineered binders integrate precisely positioned basic sidechains (Arg/Lys) to coordinate the phosphate oxygens while utilizing customized peripheral loops to achieve exquisite sequence selectivity for flanking residues.
tools.strengths: Provides powerful molecular tools for live-cell imaging and targeted inhibition of oncogenic kinase signaling pathways.
tools.weaknesses: Cellular delivery of protein binders requires conjugation to cell-penetrating peptides or viral vector transduction.

tools.name: mBER De Novo Antibody Design
tools.usage: mBER introduces a scalable deep generative framework for controllable de novo antibody design, coupled with million-scale experimental high-throughput yeast display screening. The system combines geometry-conditioned diffusion models with protein language model priors to generate human antibody variable domains targeted to pre-selected antigen epitopes, yielding dozens of verified binders across multiple therapeutic targets in a single experimental round.
tools.strengths: Drastically reduces the turnaround time of antibody discovery from months to days while bypassing animal immunization entirely.
tools.weaknesses: High-throughput experimental validation requires access to massive automated yeast display and NGS sequencing facilities.

tools.name: Claudin-5 Blood-Brain Barrier Peptide Binder
tools.usage: This study demonstrates the rational, structure-guided computational design of high-affinity peptide binders targeting the extracellular loops of Claudin-5, the predominant tight-junction component of the blood-brain barrier (BBB). Utilizing AlphaFold-Multimer co-folding and molecular dynamics simulations, the authors designed peptides that specifically disrupt Claudin-5 trans-dimerization, enabling transient and reversible BBB opening for CNS drug delivery without systemic toxicity.
tools.strengths: Addresses one of the holy grails of neuropharmacology—controlled, reversible drug delivery across the intact blood-brain barrier.
tools.weaknesses: Precise dosage titration is required in vivo to ensure rapid recovery of barrier integrity and prevent neuroinflammation.

tools.name: Metal-Carbonate De Novo Protein Design
tools.usage: In this multidisciplinary work, the authors employ de novo protein design (RFdiffusion and ProteinMPNN) to engineer artificial proteins that precisely control the nucleation, polymorphism, and macroscopic morphology of metal-carbonate minerals (e.g., calcium carbonate and magnesium carbonate). By engineering atomic interfaces with complementary carboxylate arrays matching specific crystal lattice faces, the designed proteins dictate crystal growth pathways.
tools.strengths: Expands the scope of de novo protein design from therapeutic biology into advanced materials science, green cement, and carbon sequestration.
tools.weaknesses: Requires careful control of mineral solution supersaturation and ionic strength during crystallization experiments.

tools.name: XL-MS TREM2 De Novo Motif
tools.usage: This study combines cross-linking mass spectrometry (XL-MS) with de novo protein design to uncover the structural prerequisites for activating the microglial receptor TREM2, a major therapeutic target in Alzheimer's disease. Using AlphaFold-Multimer models constrained by experimental cross-links, the researchers generated de novo designed agonist ligands that cross-link and cluster TREM2 receptors on microglial membranes, stimulating downstream SYK phosphorylation.
tools.strengths: Provides an experimental-computational paradigm to design targeted agonists for complex immune cell surface receptors.
tools.weaknesses: Receptor clustering thresholds vary between cell types and endogenous expression levels.

tools.name: Rigidity-Aware Pretraining
tools.usage: Published on arXiv and indexed in OpenAlex, Ni et al. introduce a rigidity-aware geometric pretraining framework for SE(3)-equivariant protein graph neural networks. By incorporating Pebble Game kinematic rigidity theory into self-supervised pretraining objectives, the network learns to distinguish rigid domain cores from flexible hinges and loops, leading to significant accuracy improvements in conformational ensemble generation and inverse folding.
tools.strengths: Bridges classical mechanical rigidity theory with modern geometric deep learning, solving over-stabilization biases in protein generation.
tools.weaknesses: Rigidity graph computation adds pre-processing overhead during training dataset compilation.

tools.name: PepBridge
tools.usage: PepBridge by Oscar Junhong Luo and colleagues is a unified structure-aware deep learning framework tailored for modeling peptide-major histocompatibility complex (pMHC) recognition by T-cell receptors (TCRs). PepBridge treats the bound immunogenic peptide as a dynamic molecular bridge, employing geometric cross-attention between TCR CDR loops and MHC presentation grooves to predict ternary recognition and cross-reactivity.
tools.strengths: Significantly outperforms sequence-only TCR-pMHC predictors by incorporating explicit 3D interface geometric constraints.
tools.weaknesses: Requires reliable structural models of the pMHC-TCR ternary complex; non-canonical TCR docking angles can reduce prediction confidence.

tools.name: Pair-Complete Structural Gating Cyclic Peptides
tools.usage: This paper presents a pair-complete structural gating mechanism that enables Pareto multi-objective optimization of de novo cyclic peptides. By gating pairwise interaction representations during diffusion and inverse folding, the algorithm co-optimizes high binding affinity, rigid backbone geometry, and oral developability attributes (e.g., cell permeability and low polar surface area) without sacrificing target engagement.
tools.strengths: Solves the traditional inverse relationship between high peptide affinity and poor membrane permeability.
tools.weaknesses: Requires multi-parameter scoring pipelines that increase per-candidate computational generation time.

tools.name: Crossmodal Nanobody-Antigen Interaction
tools.usage: Published in IEEE proceedings, Zhang et al. develop an epitope-aware crossmodal attention deep learning architecture for predicting nanobody (VHH)-antigen interactions. By fusing 3D structural graph representations of antigen epitope surfaces with pre-trained protein language model representations of nanobody CDR1, CDR2, and CDR3 sequences, the network predicts binding specificity and affinity across diverse viral and human targets.
tools.strengths: Delivers rapid, high-throughput screening of massive synthetic nanobody libraries against structurally characterized antigen targets.
tools.weaknesses: Requires pre-defined or predicted epitope location information to achieve maximum scoring fidelity.

tools.name: Superposition Cryo-EM Dengue Complex
tools.usage: This comparative benchmark investigates structural superposition and conformational concordance between high-resolution cryo-EM density maps and AlphaFold predictions of dengue virus envelope (E) protein antigen-antibody neutralization complexes. The authors quantify local backbone deviations, quaternary symmetry packing errors, and antibody approach angles across diverse serotypes.
tools.strengths: Provides critical benchmarking insights into where AlphaFold models succeed and where experimental cryo-EM remains indispensable for viral structural biology.
tools.weaknesses: Focuses primarily on flavivirus envelope proteins; generalization to non-enveloped viral capsids requires broader study.

tools.name: Multiple-Basin Go-Martini
tools.usage: Published in JCTC by Yang and Song, this work presents Multiple-Basin Go-Martini, a coarse-grained molecular dynamics framework designed to simulate large-scale conformational transitions between distinct structural states of proteins. By combining Martini 3 coarse-grained physics with multi-basin Go-like potentials parameterized from AlphaFold-predicted active and inactive conformations, the method simulates microsecond transitions with low computational cost.
tools.strengths: Enables microsecond-scale exploration of allosteric switches and transporter mechanics that are impossible to simulate with all-atom MD.
tools.weaknesses: Coarse-grained resolution lacks atomic detail of hydrogen bonding and water-mediated interactions at the interface.

tools.name: RLpMIEC
tools.usage: Published in JCIM by Deng et al., RLpMIEC is a generative reinforcement learning framework designed for the targeted generation and optimization of high-affinity peptides binding to Major Histocompatibility Complex class I (MHC-I). Guided by residue-level interaction spectrum feedback, RLpMIEC explores peptide sequence space while maintaining biological anchor residue constraints.
tools.strengths: Provides an interpretable, goal-oriented reinforcement learning engine for therapeutic cancer peptide vaccine engineering.
tools.weaknesses: Requires trained allele-specific affinity surrogate models to provide reward signals during generation.

tools.name: Delta-PSA Macrocyclic Dynamics
tools.usage: This study introduces Delta-PSA (polar surface area differential), a physical descriptor quantifying conformational transitions that govern passive membrane permeability in macrocyclic peptides. By calculating the difference in solvent-accessible polar surface area between polar aqueous conformations and intramolecularly hydrogen-bonded non-polar membrane states, Delta-PSA accurately predicts oral bioavailability and cell permeability in computationally designed cyclic peptides.
tools.strengths: Provides a crucial missing link for converting high-affinity macrocyclic protein binders into orally bioavailable therapeutics.
tools.weaknesses: Requires multi-environment conformational ensemble sampling (water vs chloroform/octanol) to evaluate Delta-PSA accurately.

tools.name: Peptide-Protein Docking Review
tools.usage: Published in Chemical Communications by Daisuke Kihara and colleagues, this comprehensive review provides a rigorous analysis of the evolution of peptide-protein docking methodology. The review charts the transition from classical grid-based rigid docking and Monte Carlo flexible sampling to deep-learning co-folding architectures (AlphaFold-Multimer, Boltz, Chai-1) and SE(3) diffusion models, outlining remaining frontiers in cyclic peptides, PTMs, and binding affinity quantification.
tools.strengths: An authoritative, up-to-date roadmap authored by leading experts, essential for grounding peptide modeling workflows in Alphafoldology.
tools.weaknesses: A review article synthesizing current methodology rather than a standalone software library.

tools.name: CABS-dock Cyclic Peptides
tools.usage: Published in JCTC by Zalewski, Badaczewska-Dawid, and Kmiecik, this work presents an extension of the CABS-dock framework for blind, flexible docking of cyclic peptides to proteins. By combining coarse-grained Monte Carlo dynamics with unrestrained receptor flexibility and subsequent all-atom reconstruction, CABS-dock enables unbiased de novo binding site identification and pose prediction for complex macrocycles without prior pocket knowledge.
tools.strengths: Excels at blind global docking of cyclic peptides across entire protein surfaces where the binding site is unknown.
tools.weaknesses: Sampling times increase significantly for large macrocycles (>25 residues) or highly flexible multi-domain receptors.

tools.name: Bicyclic Peptide Conformational Deep Learning
tools.usage: This study combines multi-microsecond all-atom molecular dynamics simulations with deep autoencoder neural networks to dissect the conformational transition pathways and free energy landscapes of constrained bicyclic peptides. The authors reveal how cross-link topology and chemical core modifications tune the equilibrium between rigid bioactive conformations and flexible intermediate states.
tools.strengths: Provides quantitative physical insights to guide the engineering of rigid, proteolytically stable bicyclic peptide therapeutics.
tools.weaknesses: Requires extensive molecular dynamics sampling to ensure convergence of slow macrocyclic transition states.

tools.name: Antigen-Detected NMR NaV1.7 Nanobody
tools.usage: Published in Advanced Science by Liu et al., this study integrates antigen-detected NMR spectroscopy with AlphaFold-guided structural modeling to discover and engineer a subtype-selective therapeutic nanobody targeting the voltage-gated sodium channel NaV1.7. By pinpointing minimal conformational epitope residues on the extracellular voltage-sensing domain, the authors developed a high-affinity nanobody that selectively blocks NaV1.7 without off-target inhibition of cardiac NaV1.5.
tools.strengths: Provides an exemplary case study of combining experimental biophysical NMR with AlphaFold structural predictions to overcome extreme ion channel selectivity hurdles.
tools.weaknesses: Antigen-detected NMR requires isotopic labeling of receptor extracellular fragments.

tools.name: AKR1B10-Inhibitors-Boltz2
tools.usage: Published in the Journal of Chemical Information and Modeling (Kawano, Ikari, Endo, Tomii), this landmark paper demonstrates the prospective, experimentally validated discovery of potent small-molecule inhibitors of human aldo-keto reductase AKR1B10 using the diffusion-based all-atom co-folding architecture Boltz-2. The study achieves exceptional virtual screening enrichment and confirms nanomolar enzymatic inhibition in vitro.
tools.strengths: Provides definitive prospective experimental proof that modern all-atom co-folding foundation models like Boltz-2 can drive successful real-world hit discovery.
tools.weaknesses: Virtual screening throughput with all-atom diffusion models requires GPU cluster resources compared to CPU-based empirical scoring.

tools.name: ProStab
tools.usage: ProStab is an advanced deep learning framework for zero-shot and supervised prediction of protein thermodynamic stability changes (ΔΔG) caused by single- and multiple-point mutations. By synergistically integrating structural geometric features from inverse folding representations with evolutionary embeddings from masked protein language models (ESM-2), ProStab captures both local conformational perturbations and global evolutionary epistatic constraints.
tools.strengths: State-of-the-art correlation on unseen deep mutational scanning datasets with rapid inference speed suitable for proteome-wide scans.
tools.weaknesses: Requires pre-computed 3D structures (experimental PDBs or high-confidence AlphaFold models) for inverse folding feature extraction.

tools.name: Emap2secPlus
tools.usage: Emap2secPlus, developed by the Kihara Lab at Purdue University, is a specialized 3D deep convolutional neural network tool that detects secondary structure elements of proteins (α-helices, β-sheets, other) and nucleic acids (DNA/RNA) in intermediate-resolution cryo-EM density maps (5–10 Å). Where atomistic tracing is difficult due to map blurring, Emap2secPlus provides unambiguous probabilistic segmentation to guide de novo model building and AlphaFold domain docking.
tools.strengths: Accurate identification of secondary structures in sub-optimal density maps, bridging the gap between low-resolution cryo-EM envelopes and atomic models.
tools.weaknesses: Computational memory demand scales cubicly with map box size; large complexes require map tiling or downsampling.

tools.name: EM-GAN
tools.usage: EM-GAN is a generative adversarial network architecture that enhances structural information in intermediate-resolution cryo-EM maps. By mapping noisy, lower-resolution density volumes into sharpened, feature-rich representations that correlate with atomic coordinates, EM-GAN recovers crucial secondary structure boundaries, loop connectivity, and backbone topology, directly facilitating AlphaFold model docking and automated trace completion.
tools.strengths: Significantly clarifies blurred backbone regions in cryo-EM maps, particularly in flexible peripheral domains.
tools.weaknesses: Care must be taken when analyzing de novo features to ensure generated density features are grounded in experimental evidence.

tools.name: TABR-BERT
tools.usage: TABR-BERT is a robust transfer learning architecture built on pre-trained biological BERT language models to predict T-cell receptor (TCR) binding affinity and specificity against peptide-major histocompatibility complexes (pMHC). By jointly encoding CDR3 amino acid sequences and peptide epitopes through cross-attention mechanisms, TABR-BERT achieves high generalization accuracy even on unseen, out-of-distribution neoepitopes.
tools.strengths: Demonstrates benchmark-leading performance on unseen epitopes compared to standard baseline CNNs and pure sequence classifiers.
tools.weaknesses: Focuses primarily on TCRβ and peptide sequence inputs; full 3D quaternary MHC-TCRαβ structural docking requires complementary co-folding tools.

tools.name: ArcRefine
tools.usage: ArcRefine is an innovative de novo protein binder refinement engine built on Mosaic and the all-atom diffusion architecture Boltz-2. Rather than relying on independent random sampling rounds, ArcRefine implements 'structural carryover'—iteratively seeding diffusion trajectories with subtle topological constraints and partial contact feedback from prior high-scoring poses to converge rapidly on picomolar binding interfaces.
tools.strengths: Drastically increases the in silico success rate of de novo binders targeting flat, historically challenging protein surfaces.
tools.weaknesses: Requires CUDA-compatible GPU with high VRAM to execute multiple concurrent Boltz-2 all-atom refinement cycles.

tools.name: abstain-dti
tools.usage: abstain-dti is a rigorous evaluation framework and benchmark dataset for drug–target interaction (DTI) models, introducing calibrated abstention mechanisms. Grounded in physical difficulty coordinates—such as pocket depth, flexibility, and chemical novelty—abstain-dti enables machine learning predictors to express selective confidence ('abstaining' on out-of-distribution or chemically ambiguous complexes), thereby dramatically reducing false discovery rates in virtual screening.
tools.strengths: Provides much-needed realistic evaluation for ML drug discovery pipelines, preventing dangerous overconfidence on uncharacterized targets.
tools.weaknesses: Focuses on binary and continuous binding metrics; does not directly generate or optimize the molecular conformations.

tools.name: TiDE-Ab
tools.usage: TiDE-Ab, developed by the Computational Structural Systems Biology Lab at Seoul National University (SNU-CSSB), is a generative framework for the target-specific de novo design of therapeutic antibodies. Given the 3D structure of an antigen and user-specified target epitope residues, TiDE-Ab designs complementary CDR loop conformations and sequence variants optimized for epitope shape complementarity, electrostatic matching, and developability.
tools.strengths: Facilitates rational targeting of cryptic or neutralizing epitopes while bypassing standard laboratory immunization campaigns.
tools.weaknesses: Final binding affinities require post-design molecular dynamics relaxation or empirical affinity maturation.

tools.name: FleXgeo2
tools.usage: FleXgeo2 is an advanced scientific Python package designed to extract differential geometry descriptors, Riemannian curvature, and topological manifold invariants from protein conformational ensembles. Whether analyzing molecular dynamics trajectories or generative ensemble distributions produced by AlphaFold sampling / BioEmu, FleXgeo2 decomposes complex 3D backbone deformations into interpretable geometric invariants.
tools.strengths: Provides coordinate-frame-independent metrics that isolate localized hinge bending from overall rigid-body rotations.
tools.weaknesses: Primarily focused on protein backbone coordinates; sidechain rotamer dynamics are not directly parameterized.

tools.name: EPIC-TRACE
tools.usage: EPIC-TRACE is an open-source deep learning repository for predicting TCR-pMHC recognition and tracing structural determinants of immune specificity. By harmonizing sequence-level paired αβ-chain repertoires with 3D structural interface features derived from AlphaFold-Multimer, EPIC-TRACE provides high-resolution classification of binding affinities and cross-reactive escape profiles.
tools.strengths: Addresses the critical need for paired αβ modeling, substantially outperforming single CDR3β-only classifiers.
tools.weaknesses: Performance depends on high-quality sequence pairs, which can be limited in single-cell TCR sequencing datasets.

tools.name: fullFold
tools.usage: fullFold, developed at the Department of Drug Design and Pharmacology at the University of Copenhagen (DSDD-UCPH), is an optimized, high-throughput pipeline designed to unlock the maximum inference speed of AlphaFold 3. It orchestrates automated MSA pre-caching, GPU batching, memory optimization, and streamlined JSON input generation, enabling researchers to fold hundreds of protein-ligand and multimer complexes per day.
tools.strengths: Significantly accelerates large-scale academic and industrial screening campaigns utilizing local AlphaFold 3 installations.
tools.weaknesses: Requires local AlphaFold 3 model weights and an active high-performance computing environment with modern GPUs.

tools.name: CAPTAn
tools.usage: CAPTAn (Context-Aware Predictor of T-cell Antigens), developed by the Xavier Lab computation team, is an open-source Python toolkit on GitLab for predicting the presentation, immunogenicity, and TCR recognition likelihood of peptide antigens. Unlike simple MHC-binding affinity predictors, CAPTAn incorporates processing context, cleavage flank signatures, and structural surface accessibility into a unified Bayesian framework.
tools.strengths: Significantly reduces false positive rates in clinical neoantigen prioritization compared to pure binding affinity algorithms.
tools.weaknesses: Currently optimized for human HLA class I alleles; HLA class II prediction modules are under active development.

tools.name: proteinmpnn_hcv_e2_decoy_design_pipeline
tools.usage: proteinmpnn_hcv_e2_decoy_design_pipeline is an open scientific workflow hosted on GitLab that automates the design of high-affinity soluble CD81 receptor decoys to neutralize Hepatitis C Virus (HCV) glycoprotein E2. Utilizing ProteinMPNN for inverse folding and AlphaFold-Multimer for structural verification, the pipeline executes mutational diversity exploration, solubility profiling, and binding energy evaluation.
tools.strengths: Turnkey, reproducible design pipeline with comprehensive diagnostic scripts and validation criteria for antiviral protein engineering.
tools.weaknesses: Tailored specifically around the CD81-E2 interface topology; adapting to novel viral targets requires editing interface coordinate definitions.

tools.name: vina_gnina_pose_benchmark_pipeline
tools.usage: vina_gnina_pose_benchmark_pipeline is a standardized benchmarking suite on GitLab comparing classical empirical docking scoring functions (AutoDock Vina) with 3D convolutional deep learning scoring (GNINA) across 308 diverse crystallographic protein-ligand complexes. The pipeline assesses not only binding pose RMSD but also rigorous physical plausibility metrics (clashes, bond angles, internal strain) via PoseBusters.
tools.strengths: Provides an unbiased, reproducible assessment of deep learning vs physics-based docking reliability.
tools.weaknesses: Rigid receptor assumptions; conformational changes of binding pockets during induced fit require external ensemble docking.

tools.name: neurips19-graph-protein-design
tools.usage: neurips19-graph-protein-design provides a foundational, highly referenced GitLab implementation and benchmark harness for geometric Graph Neural Networks (GNNs) applied to fixed-backbone protein sequence design. Encoding protein backbones as spatial graphs with 3D directional edge features and distance invariant representations, the codebase serves as an open testing ground for inverse folding algorithms.
tools.strengths: Transparent, lightweight codebase that is exceptionally easy to modify for custom energy functions and domain-specific design constraints.
tools.weaknesses: Fixed backbone only; cannot perform de novo backbone diffusion or loop relaxation.

tools.name: ESM-ClimbMix-520M
tools.usage: guan-wang/ESM-ClimbMix-520M is a 520M-parameter evolutionary mixture protein language model hosted on HuggingFace tailored specifically for navigating rugged protein fitness landscapes and guiding in silico directed evolution. By combining masked language model likelihoods with epistatic mixture layers, ESM-ClimbMix predicts higher-order epistatic interactions and identifies optimal multi-point mutation trajectories.
tools.strengths: Accurately predicts epistatic fitness peaks where single-point mutations are neutral or deleterious.
tools.weaknesses: Model size requires GPU acceleration for screening combinatorial mutant libraries exceeding 100,000 variants.

tools.name: RFdiffusion-Weights
tools.usage: OneScience-Group/RFdiffusion provides clean, verified model checkpoints and architecture configs on HuggingFace for the Baker Lab RFdiffusion suite. By packaging standard, active site, and symmetric scaffolding checkpoints into a centralized HuggingFace repository, this project eliminates fragmented multi-gigabyte downloads and streamlines cloud deployment on containerized platforms.
tools.strengths: Dramatically lowers setup friction for automated cloud pipelines and continuous integration testing of RFdiffusion workflows.
tools.weaknesses: Hosts checkpoint weights and configurations; execution scripts require the underlying SE(3) transformer and PyTorch environment.

tools.name: tau_neoepitope_antibody_screening
tools.usage: tau_neoepitope_antibody_screening is an interactive HuggingFace Space designed for exploring, screening, and evaluating candidate antibody and nanobody binders targeting pathological Tau neoepitopes involved in Alzheimer's disease and tauopathies. Users can submit antibody sequences or explore pre-docked structural models to assess binding likelihood, epitope coverage, and steric clashes.
tools.strengths: Highly accessible demonstration tool for neurobiologists and translational immunologists without bioinformatics programming expertise.
tools.weaknesses: Web Space compute tier restricts batch screening to dozens of candidates; large libraries require local execution.

tools.name: cyclic-peptide-holonomy
tools.usage: rOGUEgRINGO/cyclic-peptide-holonomy is a specialized machine learning model and representation dataset hosted on HuggingFace that leverages geometric holonomy and SE(3) gauge transformations to model macrocyclic peptide backbone closure and conformational flexibility. By treating cyclic peptide rings as closed topological loops with non-trivial curvature, the model enables efficient conformational sampling without ring-breaking artifacts.
tools.strengths: Solves the notorious ring closure failure mode common to linear diffusion models when applied to macrocyclic scaffolds.
tools.weaknesses: Specialized architecture focused on cyclic backbone geometry; sequence design requires downstream inverse folding tools.

tools.name: Angular-Deviation-Diffuser
tools.usage: Angular Deviation Diffuser (ADD) is a transformer-based diffusion architecture operating in internal torsion and angular deviation space to generate equilibrium conformational ensembles of dynamic proteins. Rather than diffusing in Cartesian coordinates where bond length and planarity violations occur, ADD denoises backbone dihedral and pseudo-torsion deviations, naturally guaranteeing valid covalent geometries while sampling realistic functional sub-states.
tools.strengths: Guarantees exact covalent bond lengths and planar peptide geometries without requiring post-hoc energy minimization.
tools.weaknesses: Large multi-domain hinge bending with complex quaternary rearrangements may require hierarchical global frame guidance.

tools.name: Inference-Time-Projection-Diffusion
tools.usage: This preprint (October 2026) introduces a mathematical framework for 'Inference-Time Projection' in biomolecular diffusion models. Standard generative diffusion models frequently output unphysical artifacts, such as steric clashes, bond length violations, and non-chiral inversions during the final denoising steps. By projecting intermediate generative trajectory states onto physically valid manifold constraints without retraining, this method dramatically enhances the experimental synthesis success of generated backbones.
tools.strengths: Guarantees physically realizable 3D coordinates without costly post-hoc molecular dynamics energy minimization.
tools.weaknesses: Adds a modest computational overhead (approx. 10-15%) to standard diffusion inference runtime per step.

tools.name: Prion-Tiled-Conformation
tools.usage: This study performs systematic conformational sensitivity benchmarking of AlphaFold and ESMfold across a comprehensive tiled peptide library covering the human prion protein (PrP). By comparing predictions against the Waltz amyloid algorithm and experimental biophysical assays, the authors identify a critical C-terminal hotspot displaying extreme structural polymorphism and conformational bistability.
tools.strengths: Provides an empirical methodology for detecting conformationally switchable and amyloidogenic segments using AI folding divergence.
tools.weaknesses: Fragment-based predictions do not account for full tertiary stabilization conferred by distant sequence contexts.

tools.name: MIMOSA
tools.usage: MIMOSA introduces a novel framework for guiding de novo antibody and nanobody design by incorporating 'natural interaction fingerprints' extracted from evolutionary immune repertoires. Rather than sampling unconstrained CDR geometric space, MIMOSA biophysically biases generative trajectories toward interaction patterns observed in naturally evolved high-affinity antibodies, ensuring superior developability and minimal immunogenicity.
tools.strengths: Bridges the gap between unconstrained generative AI designs and clinically viable therapeutic antibody leads.
tools.weaknesses: May bias against highly unusual non-canonical binding chemistries that have not been observed in natural repertoires.

tools.name: DiffNB
tools.usage: DiffNB adapts Direct Preference Optimization (DPO)—widely successful in aligning large language models—to 3D nanobody (VHH) generative diffusion models. By fine-tuning diffusion backbones on pairwise preferences between high-affinity binders and non-binding/destabilizing decoys, DiffNB learns to eliminate common failure modes such as steric clashes, burial of polar groups, and CDR loop collapse.
tools.strengths: Demonstrates marked improvement in in silico binding success rates without requiring complex reinforcement learning reward models.
tools.weaknesses: Requires high-quality curated pairs of binding vs non-binding structural models for effective preference tuning.

tools.name: FlowDyn
tools.usage: FlowDyn is a generative flow-matching and diffusion architecture designed to sample Boltzmann-distributed protein conformational ensembles directly from primary sequence. Addressing the limitation of AlphaFold's static single-state predictions, FlowDyn models functional conformational transitions, cryptic pocket openings, and allosteric switches orders of magnitude faster than atomistic molecular dynamics simulations.
tools.strengths: Generates thousands of diverse, equilibrium-weighted conformations in minutes, enabling rapid allosteric drug discovery.
tools.weaknesses: Extremely slow transitions (>millisecond timescales) involving major unfolding intermediates remain challenging to capture completely.

tools.name: MeDCycFold
tools.usage: MeDCycFold is a neural distillation model trained on extensive Rosetta energy landscapes to predict the 3D structures of non-canonical macrocyclic peptides containing mixed L/D-amino acids and backbone N-methylations. While traditional Rosetta GeneralizedKinematicClosure (GenKIC) requires hours of sampling per peptide, MeDCycFold predicts sub-angstrom accuracy conformations in milliseconds.
tools.strengths: Transforms cyclic peptide structure prediction from a computational bottleneck into a high-throughput computational pipeline.
tools.weaknesses: Specialized for cyclic peptides up to 15 residues; macrocycles exceeding 20 amino acids require modular assembly.

tools.name: LinkerMind
tools.usage: LinkerMind is an interpretable, biophysics-informed deep learning framework tailored for the de novo design and optimization of peptide and chemical linkers in Antibody-Drug Conjugates (ADCs). By modeling the conformational flexibility, lysosomal enzyme cleavability (cathepsin B kinetics), and plasma stability of linker constructs, LinkerMind guides the engineering of highly targeted, stable biotherapeutics.
tools.strengths: Directly tackles one of the greatest clinical failure modes in antibody-drug conjugate development (linker instability and premature release).
tools.weaknesses: Requires integration with small-molecule payload chemical structures for full biophysical profiling.

tools.name: GlycanDesign-DeNovo
tools.usage: This cutting-edge study (October 2026) demonstrates the rational programming of N-linked glycan processing, branching, and spatial shielding on de novo designed protein scaffolds. By engineering the local steric and structural environment surrounding engineered glycosylation sequons (Asn-X-Ser/Thr), the authors control whether glycans remain oligomannose or undergo complex maturation, opening transformative avenues for immune cloaking and vaccine design.
tools.strengths: Establishes programmable glycosylation as a first-class citizen in de novo computational protein design.
tools.weaknesses: Glycan processing pathways depend partly on the specific expression host (HEK293, CHO, yeast) used for production.

tools.name: CCL25-DeNovo-Miniproteins
tools.usage: This paper presents the de novo computational design of ultra-potent, picomolar miniprotein antagonists that selectively target the chemokine CCL25, suppressing its interaction with inflammatory receptor CCR9 while functionally biasing atypical chemokine receptor ACKR4 scavenging. Designed using BindCraft and verified via AlphaFold-Multimer, these miniproteins offer high metabolic stability for inflammatory bowel disease therapeutics.
tools.strengths: Demonstrates the power of de novo protein design for selectively fine-tuning complex GPCR signaling axes in vivo.
tools.weaknesses: Requires careful optimization of pharmacokinetic half-life for systemic in vivo administration.

tools.name: ScoreDistill-AllAtom
tools.usage: This seminal paper presents a mathematical and computational methodology to invert state-of-the-art all-atom structure prediction models (AlphaFold 3, Chai-1) for direct generative biomolecular design via Geometric Score Distillation. By propagating exact gradients through the structure module, the framework steers random polymer chains into high-confidence folds and binders that simultaneously satisfy shape complementarity, hydrogen bonding, and ligand coordination.
tools.strengths: Directly harnesses the vast biochemical knowledge embedded within all-atom prediction foundation models for generative engineering.
tools.weaknesses: High computational cost per designed structure due to repeated backward passes through complex pair-former / diffusion modules.

tools.name: CDR-Landscape-Rescue
tools.usage: This study maps and navigates the global structural landscape of antibody Complementarity-Determining Regions (CDRs) using high-dimensional geometric embeddings. The authors demonstrate that antibodies with poor expression, solubility, or stability can be systematically 'rescued' by traversing the structural manifold toward consensus conformational basins without compromising antigen binding affinity.
tools.strengths: Provides an indispensable roadmap for late-stage antibody optimization and developability remediation in industrial pipelines.
tools.weaknesses: Highly idiosyncratic or extreme non-canonical CDR-H3 loops may lie outside well-populated manifold regions.

tools.name: StrucNS
tools.usage: StrucNS demonstrates that interaction-weighted network topology and graph spectral properties serve as primary determinants of absolute thermodynamic stability (ΔG_folding and Tm) across both natural and de novo designed proteins. By transforming atomic contact networks into spectral graph descriptors, StrucNS outpredicts classical empirical force fields and identifies critical stress bottlenecks in generative designs.
tools.strengths: Offers a physical, interpretable, and computationally instantaneous filter for ranking de novo designed backbones before lab synthesis.
tools.weaknesses: Relies on accurate atomic coordinates; low-resolution or distorted structural models can perturb edge weights.

tools.name: MARL-Pareto-ProteinDesign
tools.usage: This paper presents a multi-agent reinforcement learning (MARL) paradigm for computational protein design, where specialized autonomous agents collaborate to navigate conflicting design objectives (e.g., target binding affinity, folding stability, expressibility, and immunogenicity). By formulating the search on a Pareto-optimal frontier, the multi-agent system discovers balanced protein sequences superior to single-objective optimization.
tools.strengths: Overcomes the notorious problem of single-objective protein design where high predicted affinity comes at the cost of catastrophic aggregation.
tools.weaknesses: Computational training and rollout phases require orchestrating multi-agent environments.

tools.name: Evolutionary-YFV-NS1-Design
tools.usage: Published in ACS Omega, this study presents the evolutionary dynamics-aware de novo computational design of a thermostable Non-Structural Protein 1 (NS1) antigen engineered for Yellow Fever Virus (YFV) point-of-care serodiagnostics. By utilizing ancestral sequence reconstruction, ProteinMPNN fixed-backbone redesign, and AlphaFold conformational validation, the authors engineered an antigen with high diagnostic sensitivity and elevated thermal stability.
tools.strengths: Demonstrates successful real-world application of computational protein design for point-of-care neglected tropical disease diagnostics.
tools.weaknesses: Recombinant expression yield must be optimized for large-scale field test kit manufacturing.

tools.name: SPAFESTWDILK-MDM2-Peptide
tools.usage: This study reports the computational discovery, all-atom structural co-folding, and multi-method biophysical evaluation of SPAFESTWDILK—a plant-derived dodecapeptide from Zingiber officinale that acts as a potent inhibitor of the oncogenic MDM2–p53 protein-protein interaction. Through AlphaFold-Multimer docking, umbrella sampling, and PoseBusters physical validation, the dodecapeptide demonstrates deep insertion into the MDM2 hydrophobic binding cleft.
tools.strengths: Provides a non-toxic, biocompatible peptide scaffold for reactivating the p53 tumor suppressor pathway in MDM2-overexpressing malignancies.
tools.weaknesses: Linear peptides require cyclization or stapling to ensure prolonged in vivo protease stability.

tools.name: CyclicPeptide-MixedChirality-Diff
tools.usage: Published in the Journal of Chemical Theory and Computation (JCTC), this groundbreaking study introduces a tailored geometric diffusion framework that generates simulation-quality conformational ensembles of mixed-chirality (L- and D-amino acid) cyclic peptides in seconds. Validated against multi-microsecond explicit-solvent molecular dynamics and experimental NMR J-coupling constants, the model captures accurate ring dynamics and transannular hydrogen bonding.
tools.strengths: Overcomes one of the greatest barriers in macrocyclic peptide drug discovery: the high computational cost of obtaining reliable conformational ensembles.
tools.weaknesses: Focuses on cyclic peptides with standard peptide bond backbones; complex non-peptidic synthetic stapling motifs require custom parameterization.

tools.name: MultimerMapper
tools.usage:
MultimerMapper is an automated bioinformatics tool and visualization suite designed for the high-throughput generation, topological integration, analysis, and visual inspection of large protein assemblies modeled with AlphaFold-Multimer. The framework resolves combinatorial subunit stoichiometries, automates multi-chain pairing pipelines, and computes interface quality metrics (ipTM, PAE inter-chain matrices, and buried surface areas) across diverse oligomeric states.

By unifying multi-chain MSA extraction with programmatic interface assessment, MultimerMapper facilitates the systematic exploration of protein-protein interaction networks and quaternary structure predictions. It provides publication-ready visualizations, interface residue contact mapping, and clustering of predicted complex conformations.
tools.strengths: Simplifies the complex multi-step workflow of generating and evaluating AlphaFold-Multimer models for multi-subunit assemblies, offering robust contact statistics.
tools.weaknesses: Requires AlphaFold-Multimer output files and local Python/ChimeraX dependencies for 3D visual rendering.

tools.name: miniprotein-binder-rfdiffusion
tools.usage:
miniprotein-binder-rfdiffusion is an open-source, automated end-to-end computational pipeline developed by Izgys for the generative design and rigorous multi-stage validation of de novo miniprotein binders targeting viral glycoproteins and cell-surface receptors. The workflow unifies target interface cropping, RFdiffusion backbone generative trajectories, ProteinMPNN combinatorial sequence design, and AlphaFold self-consistency co-folding into a cohesive automated system.

The framework automatically ranks generated candidate designs through interface energy metrics, shape complementarity (Sc), buried solvent-accessible surface area (bSASA), and AlphaFold complex confidence (pLDDT > 85, ipTM > 0.85, interface RMSD < 1.5 Å), accelerating de novo binder screening campaigns.
tools.strengths: Clean, highly automated script architecture that lowers the technical hurdle for executing high-throughput RFdiffusion binder campaigns.
tools.weaknesses: Requires local GPU infrastructure equipped with PyTorch and AlphaFold weight checkpoints for full pipeline execution.

tools.name: REAPS
tools.usage:
REAPS (Receptor-Aware Protein Sequence Design) is an all-atom geometric deep learning framework that models full receptor contexts during de novo protein design and sequence generation. While conventional inverse folding models frequently isolate target backbones or neglect explicit atomistic receptor environments, REAPS processes target-receptor coordinates within an SE(3)-equivariant graph neural network to preserve crucial interfacial hydrogen bonds, salt bridges, and steric packing constraints.

By conditioning autoregressive sequence generation on dense all-atom receptor graphs, REAPS produces designed binder sequences with substantially higher target specificity, lower energetic penalties, and enhanced in silico folding success rates when validated by AlphaFold 2 and ESMFold.
tools.strengths: Directly resolves interfacial packing and chemical complementarity during sequence generation, reducing post-hoc filtering attrition.
tools.weaknesses: Requires precise receptor coordinates; sensitive to substantial conformational plasticity in the unbound receptor target.

tools.name: PESI
tools.usage:
PESI (Paratope-Epitope Set Interaction) is a structural deep learning model that predicts antibody neutralization potency and antigenic escape by modeling cross-attention interactions between structural paratope and epitope sets. Recognizing that antigen-antibody binding is driven by localized clusters of contacts rather than global average sequence properties, PESI extracts geometric residue sets from 3D structures and learns invariant set-to-set interaction matrices.

The framework accurately forecasts neutralization titers against emerging viral variants (including SARS-CoV-2 and influenza strains) and identifies key escape mutation hotspots without requiring expensive full-scale molecular dynamics simulations.
tools.strengths: Highly accurate in predicting neutralization potency across viral escape variants while providing interpretable residue-pair attention weights.
tools.weaknesses: Relies on structural annotations of paratope/epitope boundaries or high-confidence predicted complex structures.

tools.name: TurboPairFormer-Quickstart
tools.usage:
TurboPairFormer-Quickstart provides high-performance custom CUDA and Triton kernels developed jointly by Lambda and Stevens Institute of Technology to drastically accelerate PairFormer attention in OpenFold3 and AlphaFold 3 model architectures on modern NVIDIA Hopper (H100/H200) GPUs. PairFormer computation constitutes the dominant memory and throughput bottleneck in all-atom diffusion and structure prediction pipelines.

By fusing triangular update operations, optimizing shared-memory layout, and leveraging Tensor Core FP8/FP16 matrix engines, TurboPairFormer achieves multi-fold speedups in PairFormer block execution while cutting peak VRAM consumption, enabling structure prediction of massive biomolecular complexes and high-throughput virtual screening.
tools.strengths: Drastically reduces execution time and compute costs for large-scale structural prediction campaigns on Hopper-class hardware.
tools.weaknesses: Hardware-specific optimizations designed primarily for NVIDIA Hopper architectures (compute capability 9.0+).

tools.name: boltz-input-generator
tools.usage:
boltz-input-generator is a command-line tool and Python library that automates the generation of compliant YAML manifests and complex input specifications required by Boltz-1 and Boltz-2 all-atom biomolecular structure prediction models. Preparing multi-component inputs containing proteins, modified residues, nucleic acids, and small-molecule SMILES is error-prone and complex.

boltz-input-generator parses multi-chain FASTA files, chemical SMILES strings, CCD ligand identifiers, and custom covalent modifications, automatically generating properly formatted, validated input manifests ready for distributed GPU batch prediction.
tools.strengths: Eliminates syntax and specification errors in Boltz workflows, accelerating complex setup from hours to seconds.
tools.weaknesses: Focused specifically on input manifest formatting; does not perform structure prediction itself.

tools.name: Bonsai
tools.usage:
Bonsai is an automated, deterministic target-preparation framework created to solve a widespread bottleneck in computational protein binder design: preparing clean, biologically relevant target structures for generative models like RFdiffusion and BindCraft. Starting from a simple UniProt accession ID, Bonsai retrieves AlphaFold DB models or experimental PDB structures, prunes unstructured flexible loops, detects physiological domain boundaries, and isolates solvent-exposed epitope patches.

By systematically preparing target coordinates, defining catalytic/binding hotspots, and applying coordinate centering, Bonsai ensures reproducible, high-quality starting scaffolds for downstream binder diffusion simulations.
tools.strengths: Standardizes and automates target preparation, preventing common geometry artifacts that cause de novo binder campaigns to fail.
tools.weaknesses: Automated domain trimming may occasionally truncate functional peripheral secondary structure elements if pLDDT thresholds are set too strictly.

tools.name: ChopChopMF
tools.usage:
ChopChopMF is an interactive plugin and analysis tool for UCSF ChimeraX tailored for structural biologists working with AlphaFold 2, AlphaFold-Multimer, and AlphaFold Protein Structure Database models. The tool streamlines the inspection of complex multimeric assemblies by interactively parsing per-residue pLDDT confidence scores, inter-chain PAE matrices, and multi-domain alignments directly within the 3D graphics view.

With one-click commands, ChopChopMF can dissect multi-domain proteins into rigid globular cores, mask flexible linkers, color interfaces by predicted aligned error, and export publication-ready structural figures with customized confidence legends.
tools.strengths: Brings comprehensive AlphaFold metric evaluation and domain dissection into an intuitive ChimeraX graphical environment.
tools.weaknesses: Requires a local UCSF ChimeraX installation; primarily designed for visual inspection rather than headless batch processing.

tools.name: boltz_mcp
tools.usage:
boltz_mcp is an open-source Model Context Protocol (MCP) server that exposes the full structural prediction and binding affinity calculation capabilities of Boltz-2 to autonomous LLM agents and pair-programming assistants. Through standard MCP JSON-RPC endpoints, agents can dynamically formulate biomolecular co-folding tasks, submit multi-chain protein-ligand queries, inspect predicted complex confidence metrics, and retrieve 3D coordinate outputs.

By embedding Boltz-2 into the MCP ecosystem, boltz_mcp bridges generative AI agents with cutting-edge biomolecular foundation models, enabling autonomous closed-loop hypothesis generation, in silico mutagenesis, and target engagement validation.
tools.strengths: Seamlessly integrates Boltz-2 into modern agentic frameworks (Antigravity, Claude Desktop, Cursor), democratizing programmatic structural biology.
tools.weaknesses: Requires high-end GPU resources hosting the underlying Boltz-2 model backend.

tools.name: dsh-pdb
tools.usage:
dsh-pdb is an agent-driven workflow orchestration platform designed for automated de novo protein binder generation. Developed by PKU-MDL, the framework structures the classic generative pipeline—target receptor parsing, RFdiffusion backbone generation, ProteinMPNN sequence design, and AlphaFold 2 / ESMFold self-consistency validation—into a resilient directed acyclic graph (DAG).

An autonomous agent layer monitors candidate metrics across DAG nodes, dynamically pruning suboptimal backbones, re-running sequence packing with varied temperature hyperparameters, and generating comprehensive ranking reports for top-affinity designs.
tools.strengths: High degree of automation and modularity; eliminates tedious manual shell scripting across multi-step design pipelines.
tools.weaknesses: Requires cluster setup or multi-GPU environment to execute full DAG nodes efficiently.

tools.name: Bondamino
tools.usage:
Bondamino is a dedicated web application and analysis toolkit tailored for structural biologists and model builders to audit fine-grained stereochemical geometries in experimental and AI-predicted protein structures. The tool parses PDB and mmCIF coordinate files to calculate exact covalent bond lengths, bond angles, peptide bond planarities (omega dihedrals), and backbone Ramachandran phi/psi distributions.

While global metrics like pLDDT and TM-score evaluate domain topology, generative diffusion backbones frequently introduce non-physical bond stretches or stereochemical strain. Bondamino provides real-time interactive plots and residue-level outlier tables to catch geometric anomalies before experimental synthesis or simulation.
tools.strengths: Fast, accessible, and essential for validating the physical realism and stereochemical integrity of diffusion-generated and inverse-folded backbones.
tools.weaknesses: Focused strictly on covalent geometry and backbone torsions; does not calculate long-range electrostatic or solvation energies.

tools.name: protein-folding-fret
tools.usage:
protein-folding-fret is a specialized scientific computing repository and analysis pipeline designed for processing and kinetic modeling of single-molecule Förster Resonance Energy Transfer (smFRET) experiments on folding proteins. While static AI predictions provide snapshots, smFRET traces resolve real-time transitions between native, intermediate, and unfolded conformational basins.

The tool implements robust baseline correction, photon burst filtering, Hidden Markov Model (HMM) state idealization, and transition path time calculations, providing rigorous empirical dynamic constraints to validate predicted conformational sampling ensembles.
tools.strengths: Provides crucial empirical time-resolved validation for AI-generated protein conformational ensembles and allosteric state models.
tools.weaknesses: Designed specifically for calibrated single-molecule donor/acceptor photodetector trajectories; requires experimental fluorophore distance inputs.

tools.name: cd8-t-cell-epitope-prediction-benchmarking
tools.usage:
The cd8-t-cell-epitope-prediction-benchmarking suite by the Immune Epitope Database (IEDB) team provides an automated, rigorous benchmarking pipeline to evaluate algorithmic predictions of CD8+ T-cell epitopes and peptide-MHC Class I presentation. In an era where AI co-folding models (AlphaFold 3, Boltz) and protein language models claim high accuracy in TCR-pMHC prediction, standardized empirical benchmarking is essential.

This framework periodically evaluates competitive machine learning and structural models against newly published experimental binding affinity datasets and mass spectrometry immunopeptidomics, assessing performance via strict ROC-AUC, PR-AUC, and rank consistency metrics.
tools.strengths: The definitive gold-standard benchmarking suite for evaluating peptide-MHC and TCR binding predictors without training set bias.
tools.weaknesses: Requires structured tabular datasets formatted to IEDB specifications; focuses on Class I presentation rather than full TCR-pMHC ternary complex mechanics.

tools.name: Ymir
tools.usage:
Ymir is an open-source structural simulation engine and educational library designed for exploring protein folding principles, conformational energy landscapes, and kinetic pathways using discrete 3D lattice models (cubic and face-centered cubic lattices) as well as continuous off-lattice extensions. By simplifying residue representations to discrete coordinate graphs while preserving hydrophobic-polar (HP) energetics and steric self-avoidance, Ymir computes exact thermodynamic partition functions.

This platform serves as an ideal testbed for developing new sampling algorithms, benchmarking Monte Carlo simulated annealing protocols, and analyzing folding funnel topologies before scaling to high-dimensional all-atom molecular simulations.
tools.strengths: Provides clean theoretical transparency into folding thermodynamics and energy landscape theory without all-atom compute overhead.
tools.weaknesses: Lattice representations cannot capture atomistic sidechain packing or specific hydrogen-bonding geometries found in real proteins.

tools.name: oteam-rfdiffusion-base
tools.usage:
oteam/rfdiffusion-base is a standardized, production-ready checkpoint packaging of the landmark RFdiffusion base model hosted on the HuggingFace Model Hub using secure `safetensors` format. Historically, distributing RFdiffusion model checkpoints required cloning multi-gigabyte external drive shares or legacy pickle files vulnerable to deserialization security risks.

This repository provides clean, verified model architectures, complete tokenizer/config metadata, and standardized HuggingFace Hub download APIs, enabling seamless programmatic loading within modern automated workflows, cloud containers, and CI/CD pipelines.
tools.strengths: Solves checkpoint distribution fragility and security concerns for the structural biology community's most essential backbone generator.
tools.weaknesses: Contains the model weights and architecture configuration; requires downstream inverse folding (ProteinMPNN) for full sequence assignment.

tools.name: RFdiffusion3_demo
tools.usage:
RFdiffusion3_demo is a public HuggingFace Space focused on interactive demonstration and rapid prototyping of protein binder design and functional motif scaffolding. The application provides curated reference targets (such as viral glycoproteins and oncogenic receptors) and guides users through setting up contig maps, specifying fixed functional motifs, and sampling novel de novo folds that position the catalytic or binding residues with atomic accuracy.

The tool features integrated output diagnostics, calculating backbone clash scores, radius of gyration, and secondary structure composition distributions across generated ensembles.
tools.strengths: Ideal educational and rapid testing platform for mastering contig notation and motif scaffolding without command-line overhead.
tools.weaknesses: Restricted to demo-scale batch sizes; not suitable for high-throughput library generation.

tools.name: protein-folding-esm2
tools.usage:
protein-folding-esm2 is a HuggingFace Space offering instantaneous, single-sequence protein 3D structure prediction powered by ESMFold and Meta's ESM-2 language model. By leveraging large language model representations to infer structural coordinates directly without calculating multiple sequence alignments (MSAs), the Space predicts atomic models in seconds.

The interface features an interactive 3D molecular viewer with per-residue pLDDT color coding, secondary structure ribbons, and downloadable PDB coordinates, enabling researchers to instantly screen mutations and orphan protein folds directly from any browser.
tools.strengths: Extremely fast and user-friendly for rapid validation of short-to-medium protein sequences and synthetic construct screening.
tools.weaknesses: ESMFold accuracy decreases on complex multi-chain oligomers or proteins requiring deep co-evolutionary signals.

tools.name: esm2_t12_35M-SS-Prediction
tools.usage:
This HuggingFace model repository contains a fine-tuned checkpoint of Meta's `esm2_t12_35M_UR50D` protein language model, specialized as a token-classification head for per-residue secondary structure prediction (alpha-helix, beta-sheet, coil). By transferring the evolutionary semantic representations learned across UniRef50 into downstream structural classification, the model delivers high Q3 accuracy with minimal computational overhead.

The lightweight 35M-parameter architecture enables instantaneous execution on standard CPUs or edge devices, making it an ideal pre-filtering component for high-throughput protein design pipelines.
tools.strengths: High inference throughput and tiny memory footprint, perfectly suited for rapid screening of millions of designed sequences.
tools.weaknesses: Predicts 1D secondary structure states (Q3) rather than full 3D spatial atomic coordinates.

tools.name: AlphaProtein Novo
tools.usage:
AlphaProtein Novo introduces a transformative generative artificial intelligence platform engineered specifically for the de novo design of catalytic biocatalysts and artificial enzymes capable of mediating new-to-nature chemical transformations and processing abiotic substrates. While natural evolution optimized enzymes for cellular physiological metabolites, industrial green chemistry demands catalysts for synthetic precursors that possess no natural counterparts.

AlphaProtein Novo directly scaffolds transition state ensembles and catalytic pocket geometries into de novo protein backbones. Integrating quantum mechanical transition state geometries with diffusion backbone sampling, the platform achieves orders-of-magnitude increases in catalytic proficiency (kcat/KM) across non-natural ester hydrolysis, stereoselective cyclization, and carbon-carbon coupling reactions.
tools.strengths: Bridges quantum chemistry and generative structural AI, successfully creating functional biocatalysts for reactions without natural biological precedents.
tools.weaknesses: Requires precise DFT quantum transition state models of the intended reaction mechanism prior to generative scaffold placement.

tools.name: HADDOCK3-Aptamer-Benchmark
tools.usage:
Dohi presents a comprehensive benchmark investigating the applicability domain and failure modes of HADDOCK3 when applied to protein-nucleic acid aptamer docking. Utilizing a rigorous 5×7 cross-target screening matrix and a massive 1676-amino-acid receptor case study (Complement C3 / P01031), the study documents critical performance boundaries where conventional physics-based scoring and rigid-body sampling struggle compared to deep learning co-folding architectures.

The work establishes a crucial baseline for the computational biology community, defining conformational sampling thresholds, electrostatic scoring pitfalls in highly charged phosphate backbones, and hybrid workflows combining AlphaFold 3 / Boltz initial poses with HADDOCK3 flexible refinement.
tools.strengths: Provides rare, highly transparent documentation of algorithmic failure modes, establishing realistic boundaries for protein-aptamer modeling.
tools.weaknesses: Focuses primarily on DNA/RNA aptamer complexes; findings may differ for small structured non-coding RNAs.

tools.name: GumK-AI-Docking
tools.usage:
Luciano, Alenfalk, and Courtade elucidate the longstanding structural mystery of sugar-nucleotide donor selectivity and catalytic gating in the xanthan gum glycosyltransferase GumK using deep learning-based all-atom co-folding. By deploying AlphaFold 3 and Boltz architectures to model GumK in complex with diverse nucleotide-sugar donors and acceptor lipid intermediates, the authors uncovered a dynamic conformational switch that controls catalytic competence.

The AI-modeled complexes reveal that catalytic domain closure and active site loop reorganization occur strictly in the presence of the native UDP-glucuronic acid donor, explaining donor specificity that had evaded rigid crystal structures for decades.
tools.strengths: Exemplifies how modern all-atom co-folding can resolve subtle dynamic enzyme mechanisms that resist static crystallographic analysis.
tools.weaknesses: Dynamic transitions inferred from ensemble co-folding require complementary time-resolved biophysical assays for kinetic validation.

tools.name: Chymosin-DeNovo-Binders
tools.usage:
Wolff, de Lichtenberg, Larsen, Andersen, and Jenkins describe the complete computational design, experimental synthesis, and biophysical validation of high-affinity de novo protein binders targeting chymosin, the primary milk-clotting aspartic protease. Using RFdiffusion and ProteinMPNN, the authors engineered hyper-stable miniprotein inhibitors that bind tightly into the deep chymosin catalytic cleft, completely blocking enzymatic activity and enabling affinity-based removal from dairy whey streams.

The designed inhibitors demonstrate sub-nanomolar binding affinities, high thermal stability (melting temperatures exceeding 80°C), and remarkable proteolytic resistance, demonstrating the power of generative protein design in industrial food biotechnology.
tools.strengths: Complete closed-loop validation from generative algorithm to benchtop biophysical characterization and practical industrial application.
tools.weaknesses: Designed miniproteins require recombinant bacterial expression systems, which must be scaled up for commercial food-grade adoption.

tools.name: SmallMolecule-ProteinCompetitors
tools.usage:
de Stigter, Godschalk, and Merkx introduce a groundbreaking strategy for designing synthetic protein competitors for small-molecule antibody detection and diagnostic immunosensing. Detecting small molecules via competitive immunoassay conventionally relies on chemically conjugating toxic or delicate hapten-protein conjugates. Here, the authors deploy generative protein design (RFdiffusion and ProteinMPNN) to engineer fully recombinant protein binders that mimic small-molecule epitopes.

These designed protein mimics competitively displace antibodies from target small-molecule analytes, enabling homogeneous, wash-free luminescent and bioluminescent biosensor assays with tunable sensitivity and high shelf-life stability.
tools.strengths: Transforms small-molecule diagnostics by replacing erratic chemical conjugation with genetically encodable, computationally designed protein competitors.
tools.weaknesses: Requires known monoclonal antibody structures or high-accuracy predicted paratope complexes to guide epitope mimicry.

tools.name: BioEmu-Molecular-Dynamics
tools.usage:
Bhakat and Strauch demonstrate a powerful hybrid framework combining Microsoft's BioEmu generative foundation model with enhanced molecular dynamics simulation to accelerate conformational sampling of proteins by orders of magnitude. While conventional atomistic MD requires months of GPU supercomputing to observe rare allosteric transitions or cryptic pocket openings, BioEmu generates Boltzmann-distributed conformational ensembles in seconds.

By seeding adaptive MD trajectories from BioEmu-generated transition state conformers, the authors efficiently map free energy landscapes of pharmacological targets, capturing cryptic pocket opening events in oncogenic kinases with remarkable kinetic fidelity.
tools.strengths: Bridges the speed of generative conformational AI with the rigorous thermodynamic accuracy of atomistic molecular dynamics.
tools.weaknesses: Hybrid workflow requires standard molecular dynamics engines (OpenMM, GROMACS) to compute calibrated free energy profiles.

tools.name: Inverse FoldDir
tools.usage:
Inverse FoldDir introduces a continuous generative paradigm for structure-conditioned protein sequence design using flow matching defined over the probability simplex via Dirichlet distributions. Conventional inverse folding models (such as ProteinMPNN) rely on discrete autoregressive decoding, which suffers from error accumulation along long chains and restricts gradient-based multi-objective steering.

Inverse FoldDir formulates sequence generation as a continuous vector field matching problem on the simplex, allowing simultaneous, non-autoregressive updates across all residue positions. This enables direct integration of continuous biochemical constraints (such as net charge, hydrophobic moment, and target affinity gradients) during sequence sampling.
tools.strengths: Combines ultra-fast parallel sequence decoding with smooth mathematical manifolds for continuous gradient-guided optimization.
tools.weaknesses: Mapping continuous simplex vectors back to discrete amino acid tokens requires careful temperature calibration to prevent entropy collapse.

tools.name: PeptideDrugDesign-AI
tools.usage:
This landmark review and translational framework in the Journal of Pharmaceutical Analysis evaluates the end-to-end architectures and clinical translation pipelines of AI-driven de novo peptide drug discovery. Analyzing generative diffusion models, cyclic peptide co-folding algorithms, and membrane-permeability neural networks, the paper maps the computational and experimental landscape for engineering macrocyclic and linear peptide therapeutics.

The authors synthesize benchmarks comparing AlphaFold-Multimer, Boltz, and specialized cyclic peptide networks (such as MeDCycFold and RFdiffusion) in predicting target engagement, metabolic proteolytic stability, and cellular uptake.
tools.strengths: Provides an indispensable strategic roadmap connecting generative computational design with real-world pharmaceutical development criteria.
tools.weaknesses: Broad review scope; researchers must implement specific underlying codebases for their distinct therapeutic targets.

tools.name: TCR-Explainable-Prediction
tools.usage:
Li, Yin, Landry, and collaborators present a novel explainable deep learning framework that provides rigorous, training-grounded attribution for TCR-epitope binding predictions. While black-box neural networks achieve high nominal accuracy on TCR-pMHC datasets, they often rely on spurious dataset shortcuts (such as CDR3 length or V-gene frequency) rather than genuine interfacial chemistry.

The authors introduce an intrinsically interpretable architecture that extracts residue-level contribution vectors directly aligned with physical contact matrices derived from experimental co-crystal structures. This enables immunologists to verify whether a model's predicted cross-reactivity is driven by genuine atomic contacts or spurious data artifacts.
tools.strengths: Essential for therapeutic TCR engineering, providing trusted, biophysically verifiable predictions required for clinical safety evaluation.
tools.weaknesses: Requires slightly higher training computational overhead to maintain continuous gradient attribution monitors during model optimization.

tools.name: LowData-ProteinFitness-GNN
tools.usage:
Phunnasorn, Hongdilokkul, Laesanklang, and colleagues present an advanced multimodal representation learning framework for protein mutational fitness prediction in low-data experimental regimes. In practical directed evolution, laboratories often have fewer than 50-100 measured phenotypic values, rendering purely supervised deep networks prone to overfitting.

The authors develop a hybrid architecture combining contextual sequence representations from ESM-2 with spatial graph neural networks derived from AlphaFold 3D coordinates. By embedding both evolutionary sequence semantics and 3D contact geometry, the model achieves superior mutational fitness forecasting with minimal training samples.
tools.strengths: Directly tackles the primary real-world bottleneck of protein engineering: high prediction accuracy with very small training datasets.
tools.weaknesses: Requires both accurate sequence alignments and a reliable 3D structural model of the wild-type starting scaffold.

tools.name: DistShift-Fitness-Priors
tools.usage:
Vithayapalert, Piriyajitakonkij, and Grisoni tackle the critical challenge of distribution shift in machine learning-guided protein engineering. When directed evolution explores combinatorial sequence space far from wild-type training data (e.g., higher mutational load or distinct phylogenetic clades), standard supervised models fail catastrophically.

The authors introduce a framework that integrates AlphaFold structural distance priors with evolutionary co-variance matrices, establishing an invariant latent space that preserves functional topography under severe distribution shifts and multi-mutation jumps.
tools.strengths: Crucial for navigating combinatorial fitness landscapes where algorithms must propose multi-mutant variants far beyond the training set.
tools.weaknesses: Computational evaluation of evolutionary co-variance matrices requires deep, representative multiple sequence alignments.

tools.name: Boltz2-AKR1B10-Discovery
tools.usage:
Kawano, Ikari, Endo, and Tomii report the experimental discovery of nanomolar, isoform-selective inhibitors targeting aldo-keto reductase family 1 member B10 (AKR1B10), a key oncogenic biomarker and drug target in human cancers, driven by the all-atom co-folding foundation model Boltz-2. Discriminating AKR1B10 from the highly homologous AKR1B1 has historically stymied drug hunters due to subtle active site loop plasticity.

Using Boltz-2 in a high-throughput virtual co-folding campaign, the authors screened chemical libraries directly against the dynamic catalytic pocket, identifying potent inhibitors with over 100-fold selectivity over AKR1B1 confirmed by in vitro enzyme assays.
tools.strengths: A compelling real-world experimental validation of all-atom co-folding models delivering potent, selective drug candidates.
tools.weaknesses: Accurate prediction depends on proper cofactor (NADP+/NADPH) representation during all-atom complex initialization.

tools.name: RNA3D-Decoy
tools.usage:
RNA3D-Decoy is a comprehensive, large-scale structural decoy dataset designed for training and benchmarking quality assessment (QA) algorithms on AI-generated biomolecular and nucleic acid complexes. While deep learning models like AlphaFold 3, Boltz-1, and RhoFold generate thousands of putative conformations, selecting the biologically accurate pose remains challenging.

RNA3D-Decoy compiles over 150,000 structural decoys spanning varied topological complexity and resolution, annotated with exact atomic coordinate errors, base-pairing stereochemistry, and clash indices, providing an indispensable training ground for next-generation scoring functions.
tools.strengths: Fills a critical void in structural quality assessment, providing the large-scale decoy data needed to train neural scoring functions.
tools.weaknesses: Decoy generation reflects current model architectures; future foundation models may exhibit distinct error modalities.

tools.name: AI-Physics-Trinity-Dynamics
tools.usage:
Shi, Low, Xiu, Lindorff-Larsen, and Wang formulate the 'AI-Physics-Experiment Trinity', a conceptual and computational framework that harmonizes deep learning structure prediction, molecular physics simulations, and sparse biophysical experiments to construct high-fidelity protein dynamic landscapes. While AI provides rapid static baselines and MD offers microscopic forces, neither alone accurately maps physiological conformational equilibria without empirical reweighting.

The authors demonstrate how integrating AlphaFold conformer sampling with maximum-entropy experimental reweighting against SAXS, NMR, and FRET data produces quantitative thermodynamic ensembles across allosteric enzymes, multi-domain receptors, and intrinsically disordered linkers.
tools.strengths: Provides a rigorous, thermodynamically sound paradigm that resolves conflicting predictions between AI models and physical experiments.
tools.weaknesses: Requires at least one set of experimental solution biophysics measurements (e.g., SAXS profile or NMR chemical shifts) to perform ensemble reweighting.

tools.name: CASP16-GDL-FlowMatching
tools.usage:
Morehead, Liu, Neupane, Giri, and Cheng detail the methodology and blind performance of their top-ranking geometric deep learning and flow matching ensemble for protein-ligand co-folding and affinity prediction in the CASP16 community experiment. As the first CASP edition with extensive blind all-atom protein-ligand evaluation, CASP16 benchmarked generative AI against traditional docking engines.

The authors' framework combines multi-scale equivariant flow matching for generating structural binding poses with a specialized neural affinity regressor, achieving top-tier ranking in ligand pose accuracy, pocket contact preservation, and blind binding affinity estimation.
tools.strengths: Demonstrates proven, top-tier performance under rigorous, blinded community assessment conditions in CASP16.
tools.weaknesses: Inference involves multi-model ensembling and sampling, requiring high GPU compute compared to single-shot docking heuristics.

tools.name: MALT1-Integrative-Dynamics
tools.usage:
Lesovoy, Agback, Roshchin, Sandalova, and colleagues demonstrate a powerful integrative paradigm combining AlphaFold conformational sampling, atomistic molecular dynamics (MD), and solution NMR spectroscopy to dissect the allosteric activation mechanism of the paracaspase MALT1. MALT1 is a central mediator of NF-κB signaling in lymphocytes and a key drug target in lymphoma.

While crystallographic structures captured only static inactive states, shallow AlphaFold MSA subsampling paired with microsecond MD simulations revealed a dynamic conformational equilibrium involving an active-site loop rearrangement, corroborated by experimental NMR chemical shift perturbations.
tools.strengths: Exemplary demonstration of triangulating deep learning structure prediction, physics-based simulations, and experimental biophysics to solve drug-relevant dynamics.
tools.weaknesses: Requires access to recombinant protein NMR datasets to achieve the full degree of experimental cross-validation.

tools.name: VirPLM
tools.usage:
Li, Xiao, Zhou, Jia, and colleagues introduce VirPLM, a specialized protein language model framework fine-tuned for high-accuracy antigenic distance and cross-reactive neutralization prediction in rapidly mutating viruses, focusing on influenza A/H3N2 hemagglutinin. Predicting seasonal viral antigenic drift is critical for timely vaccine strain selection.

VirPLM fine-tunes ESM-2 representations using hemagglutination inhibition (HI) assay titers and 3D structural epitope annotations. By encoding both global mutational contexts and localized antigenic site geometries, VirPLM forecasts which emerging viral clades will escape current population immunity with exceptional predictive fidelity.
tools.strengths: Directly impacts global vaccine strain selection and viral surveillance through accurate, computationally fast antigenic distance forecasting.
tools.weaknesses: Model must be periodically retrained as radically novel viral lineages acquire unprecedented glycosylation or deletion patterns.
